//! The routes on a running App (testkit.rs): what a client can make them hold, and give back.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use futures_util::FutureExt;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};

use super::testkit::{Kit, data, data_bits, eventually, reset};

// ManifestCell::refresh: one walk of the game folder for everyone who asks meanwhile, and its manifest kept whoever
// is still there to take it.  A request that went (a reset) took the walk's result with it:
// the next ?refresh walked again, and a client that asked and reset at once kept as many walks going as it liked.
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn a_manifest_walk_is_kept_when_its_asker_goes() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |root| {
        for i in 0..300 {
            std::fs::write(root.join(format!("game/TRACKS/f{i:03}.bin")), b"x").unwrap();
        }
    })
    .await;
    let before = kit.app.current_manifest().unwrap();
    // asked for, and given up at once (the walk of 300 files is under way by then)
    let _ = kit.app.refresh_manifest().now_or_never();
    eventually("the walk's manifest in place", || !Arc::ptr_eq(&kit.app.current_manifest().unwrap(), &before)).await;
    assert_eq!(kit.app.current_manifest().unwrap().count, before.count);
}

// Every share of a budget a request takes is given back however the client goes: the requests in progress (a file
// sent piece by piece), the compressors (a run compressed chunk by chunk), the connections, and /lan's (an upgrade
// answered, and one refused for opening too fast after it took its share).
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn every_share_comes_back_when_the_client_goes() {
    // (answers larger than what the kernel's buffers take while the client reads nothing: 8 MiB that compress by a
    // tenth, and as much noise)
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |root| {
        std::fs::write(root.join("game/TRACKS/big.bin"), data_bits(8 << 20, 7)).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(root.join("game/TRACKS/noise.bin"), data(8 << 20, false)).unwrap();
    })
    .await;
    let app = &kit.app;
    // a download read a little, then reset
    for (path, enc) in [
        ("/data/TRACKS/noise.bin", ""),
        ("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/big.bin?b=0&n=8", "zstd"),
        ("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/big.bin?b=0&n=8", "br"),
        ("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/big.bin?b=0&n=8", "gzip"),
    ] {
        let mut s = kit.send(path, &[("Accept-Encoding", enc)]).await;
        let mut b = [0u8; 4096];
        let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
        assert!(n > 0 && b.starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 200 "), "{path} {enc}");
        if !enc.is_empty() {
            assert_eq!(app.compressors.count(), 1, "{path} {enc}: a compressor held while it streams");
        }
        assert_eq!(app.requests.count(), 1);
        reset(s);
        eventually("the shares back", || app.requests.count() == 0 && app.compressors.count() == 0 && app.conns.count() == 0).await;
    }
    // /lan: more upgrades than the burst allows, each closed after its answer
    let mut refused = 0;
    for _ in 0..24 {
        let mut s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(kit.addr).await.unwrap();
        s.write_all(
            b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n\
              Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\n\r\n",
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        let mut b = [0u8; 64];
        let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
        if b[..n].starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 429 ") {
            refused += 1;
        } else {
            assert!(b[..n].starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 101 "), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..n]));
        }
        drop(s);
        eventually("the /lan share back", || app.lan_conns.count() == 0).await;
    }
    assert!(refused >= 3, "the burst is 20: {refused} refused");
    eventually("the connections back", || app.conns.count() == 0).await;
}

// An open /lan WebSocket keeps its place on the port's count (and its client's connection share, which a loopback
// peer like this one, always a trusted proxy, does not take) for as long as the switch's tasks keep it open, as Node
// counted an upgraded socket until its 'close'; it comes back as the connection goes.
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn an_open_lan_connection_keeps_its_place_on_the_port() {
    let kit = Kit::start_with(&[], nfsu2_http::Limits { max_connections: 1, ..Default::default() }, |_| {}).await;
    let app = &kit.app;
    let mut s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(kit.addr).await.unwrap();
    s.write_all(
        b"GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n\
          Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\n\r\n",
    )
    .await
    .unwrap();
    let mut b = [0u8; 256];
    let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
    assert!(b[..n].starts_with(b"HTTP/1.1 101 "), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..n]));
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
    // whether another connection gets an answer: none while the WebSocket is open, one once it is gone
    let answered = || async {
        let mut c = kit.send("/robots.txt", &[]).await;
        let mut b = [0u8; 64];
        matches!(tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), c.read(&mut b)).await, Ok(Ok(n)) if n > 0)
    };
    assert!(!answered().await, "the port's one place is the WebSocket's");
    assert_eq!(app.lan_conns.count(), 1);
    drop(s);
    eventually("the /lan share back", || app.lan_conns.count() == 0).await;
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    while !answered().await {
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5), "the port's place back");
    }
}

/// The answer of a /data-blocks/ run, de-chunked and decoded.
fn decoded(enc: &str, z: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    match enc {
        "zstd" => out = zstd::stream::decode_all(z).unwrap(),
        "br" => {
            std::io::Read::read_to_end(&mut brotli::Decompressor::new(z, 4096), &mut out).unwrap();
        }
        "gzip" => {
            std::io::Read::read_to_end(&mut flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(z), &mut out).unwrap();
        }
        _ => out = z.to_vec(),
    }
    out
}

// the runs as they are on disk, in every encoding, and as they are where they do not compress
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn runs_come_back_exact() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |root| {
        let mut b = data(3 << 20, false);
        b.extend(data((2 << 20) + 12345, true));
        std::fs::write(root.join("game/TRACKS/mixed.bin"), b).unwrap();
    })
    .await;
    let raw = std::fs::read(kit.path("game/TRACKS/mixed.bin")).unwrap();
    for enc in ["zstd", "br", "gzip", ""] {
        for (b, n) in [(0u64, 3u64), (3, 2), (2, 8), (4, 1)] {
            let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/mixed.bin?b={b}&n={n}"), &[("Accept-Encoding", enc)]).await;
            assert_eq!(a.status, 200);
            let want = &raw[(b << 20) as usize..raw.len().min(((b + n) << 20) as usize)];
            let got_enc = a.header("content-encoding").unwrap_or("");
            assert_eq!(decoded(got_enc, &a.body), want, "b={b} n={n} {enc}");
            // the noise of the first 3 MiB is sent as it is
            assert_eq!(got_enc, if b < 3 || enc.is_empty() { "" } else { enc }, "b={b} n={n} {enc}");
        }
    }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    assert_eq!(kit.app.compressors.count(), 0);
}

/// a game file's m and s, as the manifest names them
fn version(kit: &Kit, rel: &str) -> String {
    let md = std::fs::metadata(kit.path(&format!("game/{rel}"))).unwrap();
    format!("m={}&s={}", super::etag::num(super::etag::mtime_s(&md)), md.len())
}

// o and l in place of b and n: those bytes as they are, with their length, kept for good by a shared cache only when
// the address names this version; past the end as far as the file goes, from past it 416, numbers that are not 400
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn exact_ranges_come_back_as_they_are() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |root| {
        std::fs::write(root.join("game/TRACKS/pics.bin"), data((1 << 20) + 5000, true)).unwrap();
    })
    .await;
    let raw = std::fs::read(kit.path("game/TRACKS/pics.bin")).unwrap();
    let v = version(&kit, "TRACKS/pics.bin");
    let all = [("Accept-Encoding", "zstd, br, gzip")];
    let url = |o: usize, l: usize, v: &str| format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/pics.bin?o={o}&l={l}&{v}");
    for (o, l) in [(0, 16), (16, 30000), ((1 << 20) - 100, 4000), (raw.len() - 10, 10)] {
        let a = kit.get(&url(o, l, &v), &all).await;
        assert_eq!(a.status, 200, "o={o} l={l}");
        assert_eq!(a.header("content-encoding"), None);
        assert_eq!(a.header("content-length"), Some(l.to_string().as_str()));
        assert_eq!(a.body, &raw[o..o + l], "o={o} l={l}");
        assert_eq!(a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP));
        assert_eq!(a.header("cdn-cache-control"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP));
    }
    let a = kit.get(&url(raw.len() - 10, 100, &v), &all).await;
    assert_eq!((a.status, a.body.as_slice()), (200, &raw[raw.len() - 10..]));
    // no version, or another one: never kept by a shared cache
    for other in ["", "m=1&s=16"] {
        let a = kit.get(&url(0, 16, other), &all).await;
        assert_eq!((a.status, a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control")), (200, Some("no-store")), "{other}");
        assert_eq!(a.body, &raw[..16]);
    }
    let head = kit.request("HEAD", &url(16, 30000, &v), &all, b"").await;
    assert_eq!((head.status, head.header("content-length")), (200, Some("30000")));
    assert!(head.body.is_empty());
    assert_eq!(kit.get(&url(raw.len(), 1, &v), &all).await.status, 416);
    for bad in ["o=0&l=0", "o=0", "o=x&l=1", "o=-1&l=1", "o=0&l=8388609", "o=1234567890123&l=1"] {
        assert_eq!(kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/pics.bin?{bad}"), &all).await.status, 400, "{bad}");
    }
    assert_eq!(kit.get("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/none.bin?o=0&l=16", &all).await.status, 404);
}

// One block to a client that takes br: compressed as it is sent and kept by a shared cache for a while only, until
// its block is kept at brotli's best; then that, with its length, kept for good.  Noise is sent as it is, a run of
// more blocks and a client without br as before.
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn a_block_goes_out_as_kept_once_it_is() {
    let kit = Kit::start_keeping(1, |_| {}).await;
    // a file the manifest does not have yet: only the answers queue its blocks
    let mut raw = data(1 << 20, false);
    raw.extend(data((1 << 20) + 777, true));
    std::fs::write(kit.path("game/TRACKS/late.bin"), &raw).unwrap();
    let v = version(&kit, "TRACKS/late.bin");
    let block = |b: usize| raw[b << 20..raw.len().min((b + 1) << 20)].to_vec();
    let all = [("Accept-Encoding", "zstd, br, gzip")];
    let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1&{v}"), &all).await;
    assert_eq!(a.status, 200);
    assert_eq!(a.header("content-encoding"), Some("zstd"), "compressed as it is sent");
    assert_eq!(a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control"), Some(super::blocks::EDGE_WHILE));
    assert_eq!(decoded("zstd", &a.body), block(1));
    let mut kept = None;
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    while kept.is_none() {
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(20), "block 1 kept");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
        let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1&{v}"), &all).await;
        if a.header("content-encoding") == Some("br") {
            kept = Some(a);
        }
    }
    let a = kept.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(a.header("content-length"), Some(a.body.len().to_string().as_str()));
    assert_eq!(a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP));
    assert_eq!(a.header("cdn-cache-control"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP));
    assert_eq!(decoded("br", &a.body), block(1));
    // the address from before /v2: none; one that names no version: never kept by a shared cache
    let old = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1&{v}"), &all).await;
    assert_eq!(old.status, 404);
    let bare = kit.get("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1", &all).await;
    assert_eq!(bare.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control"), Some("no-store"));
    // a HEAD: the kept block's head
    let head = kit.request("HEAD", &format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1&{v}"), &all, b"").await;
    assert_eq!((head.header("content-encoding"), head.header("content-length")), (Some("br"), a.header("content-length")));
    // noise: as it is, a while, then for good once kept as one sent as it is
    let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=0&n=1&{v}"), &all).await;
    assert_eq!((a.header("content-encoding"), a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control")), (None, Some(super::blocks::EDGE_WHILE)));
    assert_eq!(a.body, block(0));
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    loop {
        let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=0&n=1&{v}"), &all).await;
        assert_eq!((a.header("content-encoding"), &a.body), (None, &block(0)));
        if a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control") == Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP) {
            break;
        }
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(20), "block 0 kept as it is");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    }
    // a client without br, and a run of two: compressed as they are sent, kept for good as before
    let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=1&n=1&{v}"), &[("Accept-Encoding", "gzip")]).await;
    assert_eq!((a.header("content-encoding"), a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control")), (Some("gzip"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP)));
    assert_eq!(decoded("gzip", &a.body), block(1));
    let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/late.bin?b=0&n=2&{v}"), &all).await;
    assert_eq!(a.header("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control"), Some(nfsu2_headers::EDGE_KEEP));
    assert_eq!(decoded(a.header("content-encoding").unwrap_or(""), &a.body), raw[..2 << 20]);
    // the 5-minute line's counts, then none
    let line = kit.app.sent.take();
    assert!(
        line.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit() && c != '0') && line.contains(" kept, ") && line.contains(" as they are"),
        "{line}"
    );
    assert_eq!(kit.app.sent.take(), "");
}

// The manifest's files: every block kept without being asked for (the sweep at the start)
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn the_manifests_blocks_are_kept_unasked() {
    let kit = Kit::start_keeping(2, |root| std::fs::write(root.join("game/TRACKS/swept.bin"), data((2 << 20) + 5000, true)).unwrap()).await;
    let raw = std::fs::read(kit.path("game/TRACKS/swept.bin")).unwrap();
    let v = version(&kit, "TRACKS/swept.bin");
    // swept.bin's three blocks kept: a HEAD of a kept one is br (of one not kept, the head of the block as it is), and
    // queues none.  (Counting the files in blocks/ took the half-written ones too, and the manifest's other blocks: it
    // went on before these were all kept.)
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    for b in 0..3usize {
        let path = format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/swept.bin?b={b}&n=1&{v}");
        while kit.request("HEAD", &path, &[("Accept-Encoding", "br")], b"").await.header("content-encoding") != Some("br") {
            assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(30), "the manifest's block {b} kept in 30 s");
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
        }
    }
    for b in 0..3usize {
        let a = kit.get(&format!("/data-blocks/v2/TRACKS/swept.bin?b={b}&n=1&{v}"), &[("Accept-Encoding", "br")]).await;
        assert_eq!(a.header("content-encoding"), Some("br"), "block {b}");
        assert!(a.header("content-length").is_some());
        assert_eq!(decoded("br", &a.body), raw[b << 20..raw.len().min((b + 1) << 20)], "block {b}");
    }
}

// A file put in place while it is asked for (a build or a deploy renames the new version over the old one): every
// answer is one version, with that version's length and ETag.  (The size and ETag came from a look at the path, the
// bytes from an open after it: an answer with one version's length and the other's bytes, cut short or cut off.)
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn a_file_put_in_place_meanwhile_is_answered_as_one_version() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |root| std::fs::write(root.join("game/GLOBAL/x.bin"), vec![b'a'; 10_000]).unwrap()).await;
    let (path, tmp) = (kit.path("game/GLOBAL/x.bin"), kit.path("game/x.tmp"));
    let stop = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
    let writer = {
        let stop = stop.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut long = true;
            while !stop.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                let (byte, n) = if long { (b'b', 20_000) } else { (b'a', 10_000) };
                std::fs::write(&tmp, vec![byte; n]).unwrap();
                std::fs::rename(&tmp, &path).unwrap();
                long = !long;
            }
        })
    };
    let mut seen: std::collections::HashMap<String, (u8, usize)> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    let (mut bad, mut n) = (Vec::new(), 0);
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    while t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(1500) {
        n += 1;
        let mut s = kit.send("/data/GLOBAL/x.bin", &[]).await;
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        if s.read_to_end(&mut b).await.is_err() || !b.windows(4).any(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") {
            bad.push("the connection broke".to_string());
            continue;
        }
        let a = super::testkit::Answer::parse(&b);
        let len: usize = a.header("content-length").and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
        let etag = a.header("etag").unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let one = a.body.first().copied().unwrap_or(0);
        if a.status != 200 || a.body.len() != len || a.body.iter().any(|&c| c != one) || len != if one == b'a' { 10_000 } else { 20_000 } {
            bad.push(format!("{} {} bytes of {:?} as {len}", a.status, a.body.len(), one as char));
        } else if *seen.entry(etag).or_insert((one, len)) != (one, len) {
            bad.push("one ETag for two versions".to_string());
        }
    }
    stop.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    writer.join().unwrap();
    assert!(bad.is_empty(), "{} of {n} answers: {:?}", bad.len(), &bad[..bad.len().min(5)]);
}

// /seen: the page's load and its Play counted for the day (days.rs), each browser once; anything else answered the
// same and not counted
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn seen_counts_each_browser_once() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
    let (a, b) = ("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", "BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB");
    for path in [
        format!("/seen?at=page&id={a}"),
        format!("/seen?at=page&id={a}"),
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={a}"),
        format!("/seen?at=page&id={b}"),
        format!("/seen?at=roam&id={b}"),
        "/seen?at=play&id=not%20an%20id".to_string(),
        "/seen?at=play".to_string(),
    ] {
        let r = kit.get(&path, &[]).await;
        assert_eq!(r.status, 204, "{path}");
        assert!(r.body.is_empty());
    }
    let r = kit.request("HEAD", &format!("/seen?at=play&id={b}"), &[], b"").await;
    assert_eq!(r.status, 204);
    assert_eq!(kit.app.days.today(nfsu2_util::now_ms()).1, [2, 1, 0, 0]);
}

// /country: the connection's own country as a trusted proxy (here this machine) names it, lower case, never stored;
// none without the header or with one that is no country; not kept by any cache
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn country_is_the_connections_own() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
    for (cc, want) in [
        (Some("NL"), r#"{"country":"nl"}"#),
        (Some(" br "), r#"{"country":"br"}"#),
        (Some("XX"), r#"{"country":null}"#),
        (Some("T1"), r#"{"country":null}"#),
        (Some("Netherlands"), r#"{"country":null}"#),
        (None, r#"{"country":null}"#),
    ] {
        let h: Vec<(&str, &str)> = cc.map(|c| ("CF-IPCountry", c)).into_iter().collect();
        let r = kit.get("/country", &h).await;
        assert_eq!(r.status, 200, "{cc:?}");
        assert_eq!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&r.body), want, "{cc:?}");
        assert_eq!(r.header("content-type"), Some("application/json"));
        assert!(r.header("cache-control").is_some_and(|c| c.contains("no-store")), "{cc:?}");
    }
}

// /seen at a day's first Play: the device and the changed settings go into the day's totals (settings_days.rs); a
// load, a Play without them (an older page), a bad device or no id tell nothing
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn seen_tallies_the_settings_told_at_play() {
    let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
    let (a, b) = ("AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA", "BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB");
    for path in [
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={a}&k=phone&s=fps%3D30%2Croam_name%3Dset"),
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={b}&k=pc&s="),
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={b}&k=pc&s=fps=120,hud=43"),
        format!("/seen?at=page&id={a}&k=pc&s=fps%3D60"),
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={a}&k=toaster&s=fps%3D60"),
        format!("/seen?at=play&id={a}"),
        "/seen?at=play&k=pc&s=fps%3D60".to_string(),
    ] {
        let r = kit.get(&path, &[]).await;
        assert_eq!(r.status, 204, "{path}");
    }
    let (_, _, t) = kit.app.days.settings(7, nfsu2_util::now_ms());
    assert_eq!(t.reports, [2, 1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(t.counts["fps"]["30"], [0, 1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(t.counts["fps"]["120"], [1, 0, 0]);
    assert_eq!(t.counts["roam_name"]["set"], [0, 1, 0]);
    assert!(!t.counts["fps"].contains_key("60"));
}

/// an answer's whole length once its head is in (its Content-Length; none: no body)
fn answer_len(b: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    let end = b.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n")?;
    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..end]).to_ascii_lowercase();
    let len = head.split("content-length: ").nth(1).and_then(|r| r.split("\r\n").next()).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
    Some(end + 4 + len)
}

/// A measurement, not a check: requests a second and the server's CPU per request for the small routes (the
/// router, the headers, the file checks), 32 keep-alive connections, one request at a time on each, the client on
/// a runtime of its own.  cargo test --release -- --ignored bench_routes --nocapture
#[test]
#[ignore]
fn bench_routes() {
    let server = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().unwrap();
    let kit = server.block_on(Kit::start(&[], |_| {}));
    let etag = server.block_on(kit.get("/index.html", &[])).header("etag").unwrap().to_string();
    let addr = kit.addr;
    let client = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().unwrap();
    for (name, path, extra) in [
        ("/players", "/players", String::new()),
        ("/index.html 200", "/index.html", String::new()),
        ("/index.html 304", "/index.html", format!("If-None-Match: {etag}\r\n")),
        ("/data/ range", "/data/GLOBAL/small.bin", "Range: bytes=0-99\r\n".to_string()),
        ("/data-blocks/ as is", "/data-blocks/v2/GLOBAL/small.bin?b=0&n=1", String::new()),
        ("404", "/nothing/here.js", String::new()),
    ] {
        // (NFSU2_BENCH_ROUTE: that one alone, for a profiler)
        if std::env::var("NFSU2_BENCH_ROUTE").is_ok_and(|r| r != name) {
            continue;
        }
        let (conns, per) = (32, 2000);
        let req = format!("GET {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nUser-Agent: bench\r\n{extra}\r\n");
        let cpu0 = nfsu2_util::cpu::process_cpu_seconds();
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        client.block_on(async {
            let tasks: Vec<_> = (0..conns)
                .map(|_| {
                    let req = req.clone();
                    tokio::spawn(async move {
                        let mut s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(addr).await.unwrap();
                        s.set_nodelay(true).unwrap();
                        let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64 << 10];
                        for _ in 0..per {
                            s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).await.unwrap();
                            let (mut got, mut want) = (0, usize::MAX);
                            while got < want {
                                let n = s.read(&mut buf[got..]).await.unwrap();
                                assert!(n > 0, "closed");
                                got += n;
                                if want == usize::MAX {
                                    want = answer_len(&buf[..got]).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            for t in tasks {
                t.await.unwrap();
            }
        });
        let s = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
        // (the process's CPU: the client's runtime too, which costs about the same for every route)
        let cpu = nfsu2_util::cpu::process_cpu_seconds() - cpu0;
        let n = (conns * per) as f64;
        println!("{name:<22} {:>8.0} requests/s  {:>6.1} us of CPU each (server and client)", n / s, cpu / n * 1e6);
    }
    drop(kit);
}

/// what the players on the switch do, every 5 minutes while any are on (counts only)
const BREAKDOWN_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5 * 60);
/// who is in free roam or Online, for the day's counts (days.rs): often enough to see a short visit
const DAYS_SWEEP_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
/// SO_SNDBUF of a /lan connection (NFSU2_LAN_SNDBUF; 0: the kernel's own), which Linux doubles: what a player's path
/// does not take waits in the switch's own queue then, where its rules see it (roam_queue), not in the kernel's,
/// which Linux grows to 4 MB (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-22: up to 4 MB waiting there for one player, seconds of free roam)
const LAN_SNDBUF: u64 = 32 << 10;
/// the threads that compress the game data's blocks at brotli's best, once, at the lowest priority
/// (NFSU2_COMPRESS_THREADS; kept.rs): a game folder with every language pack (5600 blocks, 3100 that compress) in
/// about half an hour; none on a --dev server unless given
const COMPRESS_THREADS: u64 = 2;
/// keyphrase saves: counted at the start, then swept (the unused removed) and counted again every day
const VAULT_SWEEP_EVERY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600);

/// "1.2 GB", "340.5 MB"
pub(super) fn size(bytes: u64) -> String {
    if bytes >= 1_000_000_000 { format!("{:.2} GB", bytes as f64 / 1e9) } else { format!("{:.1} MB", bytes as f64 / 1e6) }
}

/// the console's line for a sweep: counts only, never a keyphrase
fn vault_line(s: &Sweep, max: u64, seconds: f64) -> String {
    let mut l = format!("[vault] {} keyphrases, {} of {} (counted in {seconds:.1} s)", s.keyphrases, size(s.bytes), size(max));
    if s.removed > 0 {
        l.push_str(&format!("; {} removed after two years unused", s.removed));
    }
    if s.temps > 0 {
        l.push_str(&format!("; {} unfinished writes cleared", s.temps));
    }
    l
}

/// a measurement knob from the environment (a whole number), else the default
fn env_num(name: &str, def: u64) -> u64 {
    std::env::var(name).ok().and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok()).unwrap_or(def)
}

/// the state folder: made private to this server's user (the files inside are 0600 too)
fn state_folder(o: &Options) -> String {
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700).create(&o.state) {
        die(&format!("{}: {e}", o.state));
    }
    // (only a folder of this user's own is made 0700: not ours to change otherwise; /proc/self is owned by the
    // process's user)
    if let (Ok(st), Ok(me)) = (std::fs::metadata(&o.state), std::fs::metadata("/proc/self"))
        && st.uid() == me.uid()
    {
        let _ = std::fs::set_permissions(&o.state, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o700));
    }
    match std::fs::canonicalize(&o.state) {
        Ok(p) => p.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        Err(e) => die(&format!("{}: {e}", o.state)),
    }
}

/// --http-socket's listener: "@name" in the network namespace's abstract space (Linux), else a file, made anew (a
/// socket's file stays after its process ends) and open to every user: the proxy may run as a user of its own
/// (cloudflared's image: 65532), and anything on this machine reaches the HTTP port too.  For each message a page and
/// the switch exchange, a Unix socket spares both ends TCP's work on 127.0.0.1 (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-30, 5,800 players:
/// the kernel's network work was about 60 % of the CPU, much of it this hop's)
fn bind_unix(at: &str) -> std::io::Result<tokio::net::UnixListener> {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    if let Some(name) = at.strip_prefix('@') {
        use std::os::linux::net::SocketAddrExt;
        let l = std::os::unix::net::UnixListener::bind_addr(&std::os::unix::net::SocketAddr::from_abstract_name(name)?)?;
        l.set_nonblocking(true)?;
        return tokio::net::UnixListener::from_std(l);
    }
    if std::fs::symlink_metadata(at).is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_socket()) {
        std::fs::remove_file(at)?;
    }
    let l = tokio::net::UnixListener::bind(at)?;
    std::fs::set_permissions(at, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o666))?;
    Ok(l)
}

/// the certificate file's time, for the check once a minute (0 when it cannot be read, as fs.watchFile has it)
async fn cert_mtime(p: &str) -> f64 {
    tokio::fs::metadata(p).await.map(|m| etag::mtime_ms(&m)).unwrap_or(0.0)
}

/// a renewed certificate (certbot, a new Origin CA certificate) is picked up without a restart
async fn reload_cert(app: &Arc<App>, tls: &Arc<TlsState>) {
    let t = tls.clone();
    match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || t.reload()).await {
        Ok(Ok(names)) => {
            app.host_check.set_cert_names(&[names.dns, names.ips].concat());
            log::line("certificate reloaded");
        }
        Ok(Err(m)) => log::error(&format!("certificate not reloaded: {m}")),
        Err(e) => log::error(&format!("certificate not reloaded: {e}")),
    }
}

pub async fn run(o: Options, cores: usize) {
    let real_state = state_folder(&o);
    // the console kept in the state folder too, a file a day (nfsu2_util::logfile): it outlasts a deploy
    let logs = paths::join(&o.state, "logs");
    let logs_up = match nfsu2_util::logfile::to_files(Path::new(&logs)) {
        Ok(()) => true,
        Err(e) => {
            log::error(&format!("{logs}: {e} (no log files: the console only)"));
            false
        }
    };
    if !o.artifacts.is_empty()
        && let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&o.artifacts)
    {
        die(&format!("{}: {e}", o.artifacts));
    }
    // ETags without file-system detail: a keyed hash (the key never leaves this machine)
    let etag_key = etag::load_key(&o.state).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("{}/etag.key: {e}", o.state)));

    // ---- /lan: the switch, the game's Online mode at 10.77.0.1 and free roam's hub at 10.77.0.253 ----
    let trace = if o.online_trace.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(LobbyTrace::open(Path::new(&o.online_trace)).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("{}: {e}", o.online_trace))))
    };
    let tap = trace.as_ref().map(|t| t.tap());
    // the lines a client causes in Online mode (logins, games, races, friends) count against that client's share of
    // the console, as its joins and refusals do (the Online audit's ONL-8)
    // claimed names (nfsu2-claims): with keyphrase saves only (a name is claimed by a keyphrase)
    let claims = (o.vault_gb > 0.0).then(|| Arc::new(nfsu2_claims::Claims::open(Path::new(&o.state), nfsu2_util::now_ms())));
    // the operator's bans, and the control socket that makes them (control.rs); the hosts' [cheat] lines of races get
    // a handle that `ban` takes for a week (control.rs Marker)
    let bans = Arc::new(nfsu2_bans::Bans::open(Path::new(&o.state)).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("{}/bans.json: {e}", o.state))));
    // how many come each day (days.rs): the day so far, from before a restart
    let days = Arc::new(super::days::Days::open(&o.state, nfsu2_util::now_ms()));
    let marker = super::control::Marker::new(bans.clone());
    let online = o.online.then(|| {
        let m = marker.clone();
        OnlineHost::spawn(OnlineOptions {
            state_dir: Some(PathBuf::from(paths::join(&o.state, "online"))),
            log: Arc::new(move |line: &str, key: Option<&str>| {
                let tagged = m.tag(line);
                let line = tagged.as_deref().unwrap_or(line);
                match key {
                    None => log::line(line),
                    Some(k) => log::limited("online", "Online lines", k, line, 30),
                }
            }),
            tap: tap.clone(),
            claims: claims.clone(),
            // the names the operator took away (control.rs rename): no login under one
            deny: Some(bans.deny()),
        })
    });
    // (its lines: the cap on the players' links going down while the server is busy and back up, at most one every 5 s)
    let m = marker.clone();
    let roam_log = Arc::new(move |line: &str| log::line(m.tag(line).as_deref().unwrap_or(line)));
    // (a player under a name taken away plays alone, as under another's claimed name; one who races others in a car
    // past the operator's numbers is race-banned by the server: autoban.rs)
    let car_bans = super::autoban::from_env();
    let roam_options =
        RoamOptions { deny: Some(bans.deny()), car_bans: car_bans.as_ref().map(|(c, _)| c.clone()), ..RoamOptions::default() };
    let roam = o.roam_hub.then(|| RoamHub::spawn_with(roam_options, roam_log, claims.clone()));
    // keyphrase saves: a folder in the state folder (none with --vault-gb 0)
    let vault = (o.vault_gb > 0.0).then(|| {
        let dir = paths::join(&o.state, "vault");
        Arc::new(Vault::open(VaultOptions::sized(PathBuf::from(&dir), o.vault_gb)).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("{dir}: {e}"))))
    });
    let lan_sndbuf = env_num("NFSU2_LAN_SNDBUF", LAN_SNDBUF) as usize;
    // the bundle clock's tick, 50 ms (nfsu2-lan); NFSU2_BUNDLE_MS another (0: none), for measurements
    let d = LanOptions::default();
    let fixed = std::env::var_os("NFSU2_BUNDLE_MS").is_some().then(|| env_num("NFSU2_BUNDLE_MS", d.bundle_ms));
    let lan_options = LanOptions {
        max_peers: o.max_peers,
        max_payload: limits::WS_MAX_PAYLOAD,
        bundle_ms: fixed.unwrap_or(d.bundle_ms),
        bundle_max_ms: fixed.unwrap_or_else(|| env_num("NFSU2_BUNDLE_MAX_MS", d.bundle_max_ms)),
        bundle_budget: env_num("NFSU2_BUNDLE_BUDGET", d.bundle_budget),
        bundle_jitter: env_num("NFSU2_BUNDLE_JITTER", (d.bundle_jitter * 100.0) as u64) as f64 / 100.0,
        // LAN play's clock, 4 ms; NFSU2_LAN_MS another (0: none, each datagram at once), for measurements
        lan_ms: env_num("NFSU2_LAN_MS", d.lan_ms),
        fpred: env_num("NFSU2_FPRED", 1) != 0,
        probe_echo: env_num("NFSU2_PROBE_ECHO", 1) != 0,
        send_buffer_os: lan_sndbuf,
        ..d
    };
    // the switch's addresses outlive a restart (by the hashes of their tokens): the players come back to them
    let lan = LanSwitch::new(
        lan_options,
        if o.dev { &o.lan_impair } else { "" },
        online.clone().map(|h| h as Arc<dyn Host>),
        roam.clone().map(|h| h as Arc<dyn Host>),
        tap,
        Some(PathBuf::from(paths::join(&o.state, "lan-addresses.json"))),
    );
    if let Some(h) = &online {
        h.attach_switch(lan.switch_send());
    }
    if let Some(h) = &roam {
        h.attach_switch(lan.switch_send());
    }
    marker.set_switch(lan.clone());
    // the switch's lines: the players' license plates in free roam (a new one, one that reads as a slur)
    lan.on_line(Box::new(|line: &str| log::line(line)));

    // Cloudflare's check for a claim (turnstile.rs: off without its two keys)
    let turnstile = super::turnstile::Turnstile::from_env();
    if let Some(c) = &claims {
        log::line(&format!(
            "[names] {} names claimed; Cloudflare's check {}",
            c.count(nfsu2_util::now_ms()),
            if turnstile.is_some() { "on" } else { "off (no NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SITE and NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SECRET)" }
        ));
    }
    let names = claims.clone().map(|c| super::names::NamesRoute::new(c, turnstile));
    // the threads that keep the game data's blocks at brotli's best (kept.rs; 0: none): none on a --dev server unless
    // given, where a test's fresh state folder took 2 cores for most of an hour (2026-11-03: three test servers at
    // once, 6 of the PC's 20) for smaller downloads no test needs
    let compress_threads = env_num("NFSU2_COMPRESS_THREADS", if o.dev { 0 } else { COMPRESS_THREADS }) as usize;
    let app = Arc::new(App::new(
        o,
        real_state,
        etag_key,
        lan.clone(),
        online,
        roam.clone(),
        vault.clone(),
        names,
        bans,
        days.clone(),
        (cores / 2).max(2),
        lan_sndbuf,
        compress_threads,
    ));
    log::line(if app.lastfm.is_some() {
        "[lastfm] scrobbles on"
    } else {
        "[lastfm] scrobbles off (no NFSU2_LASTFM_KEY and NFSU2_LASTFM_SECRET)"
    });
    // the pages' friend messages (friends.rs)
    if let Some(f) = &app.friends {
        f.attach();
    }
    let o = &app.o;
    let control = super::control::listen(app.clone());
    // (with free roam's hub only: its lobby races are where the cars are seen)
    if let (Some((cars, races)), Some(_)) = (car_bans, &app.roam) {
        super::autoban::start(app.clone(), marker.clone(), &cars, races);
    }

    // the switch's players, every 5 minutes while any are on
    {
        let lan = lan.clone();
        let roam = app.roam.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut shown = false;
            let mut thinned = 0;
            let mut was = nfsu2_lan::Breakdown::default();
            let (mut cpu_was, mut workers, mut quota) =
                (process_cpu_seconds(), WorkersBusy::new(&tokio::runtime::Handle::current()), QuotaBusy::find());
            let mut every = interval_at(Instant::now() + BREAKDOWN_EVERY, BREAKDOWN_EVERY);
            loop {
                every.tick().await;
                // the CPU of the last 5 minutes: the server's, its workers' busy time, and the fullest quota's (the
                // game's containers' together: nfsu2.slice)
                let cpu = process_cpu_seconds();
                let server = (cpu - cpu_was) / BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64();
                let (busy, slice) = (workers.sample(), quota.as_mut().and_then(QuotaBusy::sample_use));
                cpu_was = cpu;
                let b = lan.breakdown().await;
                if b.players == 0 && !shown {
                    continue;
                }
                shown = b.players > 0;
                // how many are behind on their connection (its queues past the server: the kernel's, cloudflared's,
                // the tunnel's) and get fewer of the other cars' updates meanwhile (nfsu2-lan lag.rs)
                log::line(&format!(
                    "[players] {} on the switch: {} in Online mode, {} on the LAN or Online screens, {} in free roam ({} of them not driving: \
                     a race, a shop, the menus), {} leaving or starting; {} more than a second behind on their connection, {} getting \
                     fewer car updates ({} left out since the last count)",
                    b.players,
                    b.online,
                    b.lan,
                    b.roam,
                    b.away,
                    b.other,
                    b.behind,
                    b.thinning,
                    b.thinned - thinned
                ));
                // co-op free roam's second players (nfsu2-roam `coop_seats`): one more endpoint on their page's place each
                if let Some(n) = roam.as_ref().map(|r| r.coop_seats()).filter(|&n| n > 0) {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] of them in free roam, {n} with a second player beside them (co-op)"));
                }
                // LAN broadcasts (server.dll's adverts) not sent to pages with LAN play open but no socket on their port
                // (nfsu2-lan Peer::takes_udp)
                let skipped = b.bcast_skipped - was.bcast_skipped;
                if skipped > 0 {
                    log::line(&format!(
                        "[players] LAN broadcasts not sent since the last count (no socket on their port there): {skipped} ({:.1} Mbit/s)",
                        (b.bcast_skipped_bytes - was.bcast_skipped_bytes) as f64 * 8.0 / 1e6 / BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64()
                    ));
                }
                // the line (nfsu2-lan queue.rs): pages waiting for a place, and how long the longest of those let in
                // waited
                if b.waiting > 0 || b.waited > 0 {
                    log::line(&format!(
                        "[players] {} waiting in line for a place; the longest wait of those let in since the line began {} min",
                        b.waiting,
                        b.waited.div_ceil(60)
                    ));
                }
                // what free roam sent the pages in compact bundles since the last count: friends' car states (by their
                // fields, nfsu2-lan fpred.rs, or as a byte delta) and the rest
                let (sb, se, sf) = (b.snap_bytes - was.snap_bytes, b.snap_entries - was.snap_entries, b.fpred_entries - was.fpred_entries);
                let (ob, oe) = (b.other_bytes - was.other_bytes, b.other_entries - was.other_entries);
                if se + oe > 0 {
                    log::line(&format!(
                        "[players] to the pages in compact bundles since the last count: {:.1} MB in {se} car states ({:.1} bytes each, \
                         {sf} of them by their fields), {:.1} MB in {oe} other datagrams",
                        sb as f64 / 1e6,
                        sb as f64 / se.max(1) as f64,
                        ob as f64 / 1e6
                    ));
                }
                // the same and the hosts' messages by kind (nfsu2-lan mix.rs): where the bytes to the pages went
                if let Some(l) = nfsu2_lan::mix::line(&b.mix, &was.mix, BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64()) {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] to the pages by kind since the last count: {l}"));
                }
                // what the pages sent, by kind, and the WebSocket messages each way (each one is work for the kernel and
                // cloudflared, whatever its size)
                if let Some(l) = nfsu2_lan::mix::line(&b.mix_in, &was.mix_in, BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64()) {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] from the pages by kind since the last count: {l}"));
                }
                if let Some(l) = nfsu2_lan::mix::msg_line(&b.msgs, &was.msgs, BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64()) {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] WebSocket messages since the last count: {l}"));
                }
                // the same by kind of player: who costs the messages (the one place that takes these counts)
                let kinds = lan.messages_by_kind().await;
                if let Some(l) = nfsu2_lan::mix::kinds_line(&kinds, BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs_f64()) {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] WebSocket messages by kind of player since the last count (those on now): {l}"));
                }
                // where the players are (Cloudflare's country) and how long their paths are: to the server, and from one
                // player to another through it, of free roam's links and LAN play's pairs (nfsu2-lan paths.rs)
                for l in lan.paths().await {
                    log::line(&format!("[players] {l}"));
                }
                let slice = slice.map_or(String::new(), |q| {
                    format!("; {} {:.2} of its {} cores ({:.0} %)", q.group, q.used, q.cores, q.share() * 100.0)
                });
                log::line(&format!(
                    "[players] CPU in the last 5 minutes: the server {server:.2} cores, its switch's workers {:.0} % busy{slice}",
                    busy * 100.0
                ));
                thinned = b.thinned;
                was = b;
            }
        });
    }
    // the game data's answers, every 5 minutes while there were any (blocks.rs Sent)
    {
        let app = app.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut every = interval_at(Instant::now() + BREAKDOWN_EVERY, BREAKDOWN_EVERY);
            loop {
                every.tick().await;
                let sent = app.sent.take();
                if !sent.is_empty() {
                    log::line(&format!("[blocks] in the last 5 minutes: {sent}"));
                }
            }
        });
    }
    // the day's counts (days.rs): who is in free roam or Online now, every SWEEP_EVERY; the day so far written and on
    // the console when it changed
    {
        let (lan, days) = (lan.clone(), days.clone());
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut every = interval_at(Instant::now() + DAYS_SWEEP_EVERY, DAYS_SWEEP_EVERY);
            let mut shown = [0; 4];
            let mut ticks = 0u64;
            loop {
                every.tick().await;
                let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
                for w in lan.who().await.iter().filter(|w| w.left.is_none()) {
                    let what = match w.doing {
                        "Online" => super::days::Seen::Online,
                        "free roam" => super::days::Seen::Roam,
                        _ => continue,
                    };
                    if let Some(id) = &w.browser {
                        days.seen(id, what, now);
                    }
                }
                ticks += 1;
                if !ticks.is_multiple_of(BREAKDOWN_EVERY.as_secs() / DAYS_SWEEP_EVERY.as_secs()) {
                    continue;
                }
                let (_, c) = days.today(now);
                if c != shown {
                    shown = c;
                    log::line(&format!("[days] today so far (UTC): {}", super::days::counts_text(c)));
                }
                let d = days.clone();
                if let Ok(Err(e)) = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || d.save()).await {
                    log::error(&format!("days.json: {e}"));
                }
            }
        });
    }
    // the /lan openers' buckets that are full again hold nothing worth keeping
    {
        let app = app.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut every = interval_at(Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60), Duration::from_secs(60));
            loop {
                every.tick().await;
                app.lan_opens.prune();
                if let Some(v) = &app.vault {
                    v.prune();
                }
                if let Some(f) = &app.friends {
                    f.prune();
                }
                if let Some(l) = &app.lastfm {
                    l.prune();
                }
                // the claimed names: the ended ones go, names.json written when anything changed
                if let Some(n) = &app.names {
                    n.prune();
                    let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
                    n.claims.prune(now);
                    let c = n.claims.clone();
                    if let Ok(Err(e)) = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || c.save(now)).await {
                        log::error(&format!("names.json: {e}"));
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }

    // ---- listening ----
    let limits = Arc::new(Limits { max_connections: limits::max_connections(o.max_peers), ..Limits::default() });
    let mut servers = Vec::new();
    let mut bound_to = o.bind.clone();
    if o.tls == Tls::Cert {
        // A --tls-cert certificate: its names (SAN), for the Host check and the handshake, which goes through only for a
        // server name (SNI) the certificate covers, so a scanner that connects to the bare address, or asks for any
        // other name, never sees the certificate or the domain in it (the audit's F4).  With Cloudflare's ranges trusted,
        // a peer there must show Cloudflare's origin-pull certificate (App::client_certificate).
        let (cert, key) = (Path::new(&o.tls_cert), Path::new(&o.tls_key));
        let loaded = if o.trust.cloudflare {
            TlsState::load_with_client_ca(cert, key, nfsu2_headers::CLOUDFLARE_ORIGIN_PULL_CA)
        } else {
            TlsState::load(cert, key)
        };
        let (tls, names) = match loaded {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(m) => die(&format!("the certificate files cannot be used: {m}")),
        };
        app.host_check.set_cert_names(&[names.dns, names.ips].concat());
        let (listener, host) = bind(&o.bind, o.https_port, if o.bind_set { None } else { Some("0.0.0.0") })
            .await
            .unwrap_or_else(|m| die(&format!("cannot listen: {m}")));
        bound_to = host;
        servers.push(serve(listener, Some(tls.clone()), limits.clone(), app.clone()));
        // the certificate file, checked once a minute, and SIGHUP
        {
            let (app, tls, cert) = (app.clone(), tls.clone(), o.tls_cert.clone());
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                let mut last = cert_mtime(&cert).await;
                let mut every = interval_at(Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(60), Duration::from_secs(60));
                loop {
                    every.tick().await;
                    let cur = cert_mtime(&cert).await;
                    if cur != last {
                        last = cur;
                        reload_cert(&app, &tls).await;
                    }
                }
            });
        }
        {
            let (app, tls) = (app.clone(), tls.clone());
            let mut hup = signal(SignalKind::hangup()).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("SIGHUP: {e}")));
            tokio::spawn(async move {
                while hup.recv().await.is_some() {
                    reload_cert(&app, &tls).await;
                }
            });
        }
    }
    if o.http_port != 0 {
        let (listener, _) = bind("127.0.0.1", o.http_port, None).await.unwrap_or_else(|m| die(&format!("cannot listen: {m}")));
        servers.push(serve(listener, None, limits.clone(), app.clone()));
    }
    if !o.http_socket.is_empty() {
        let listener = bind_unix(&o.http_socket).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("cannot listen on {}: {e}", o.http_socket)));
        // as from 127.0.0.1: the proxy on this machine it is for is trusted there, and reports the player's address
        servers.push(serve_unix(listener, ([127, 0, 0, 1], 0).into(), limits.clone(), app.clone()));
    }
    if let Err(e) = app.refresh_manifest().await {
        die(&format!("the game folder {}: {e}", o.data));
    }
    // ready before the first player asks
    {
        let app = app.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            app.compressed_wasm().await;
        });
    }

    // SIGTERM, SIGINT: the switch saves its addresses, the hosts stop, the claimed names and the day so far are written, the control
    // socket's file goes, then the process ends
    let control_up = control.is_some();
    {
        let (lan, trace, claims, days) = (lan.clone(), trace.clone(), claims.clone(), days.clone());
        let mut term = signal(SignalKind::terminate()).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("SIGTERM: {e}")));
        let mut int = signal(SignalKind::interrupt()).unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("SIGINT: {e}")));
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                tokio::select! {
                    _ = term.recv() => {}
                    _ = int.recv() => {}
                }
                lan.stop();
                if let Some(t) = &trace {
                    t.close();
                }
                if let Some(c) = &claims
                    && let Err(e) = c.save(nfsu2_util::now_ms())
                {
                    log::error(&format!("names.json: {e}"));
                }
                if let Err(e) = days.save() {
                    log::error(&format!("days.json: {e}"));
                }
                if let Some(c) = &control {
                    c.remove();
                }
                for s in &servers {
                    s.abort();
                }
                tokio::spawn(async {
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
                    std::process::exit(0);
                });
            }
        });
    }

    let here = if cfg!(target_os = "macos") { "this Mac" } else { "this host" };
    let mut names = vec!["localhost".to_string()];
    for n in app.host_check.names() {
        if !names.contains(&n) {
            names.push(n);
        }
    }
    let mut lines = vec![
        "NFSU2 web server".to_string(),
        format!("  game data : {} ({} entries of the game's own)", o.data, app.manifest_count()),
        format!(
            "  game.wasm : {}",
            if Path::new(&o.wasm).exists() { o.wasm.clone() } else { format!("{}  (missing: run web/build.sh)", o.wasm) }
        ),
        format!(
            "  {here:<10}: {}{}",
            if o.http_port != 0 { format!("http://localhost:{}/", o.http_port) } else { "(no local HTTP port)".into() },
            if o.tls == Tls::Proxy { "  (the proxy forwards here)" } else { "" }
        ),
    ];
    if !o.http_socket.is_empty() {
        lines.push(format!(
            "  socket    : HTTP on {} too, as from 127.0.0.1 (cloudflared's origin unix:{}: no TCP on this machine)",
            o.http_socket, o.http_socket
        ));
    }
    match o.tls {
        Tls::None => lines.push("  other PCs : none: they need HTTPS, from --tls-cert/--tls-key or a proxy or tunnel in front".into()),
        Tls::Cert => lines.push(format!(
            "  HTTPS     : port {} on {}, certificate {}",
            o.https_port,
            if bound_to == "::" { ":: (IPv6 and IPv4)".to_string() } else { bound_to.clone() },
            o.tls_cert
        )),
        Tls::Proxy => {
            lines.push("  TLS       : done by the proxy or tunnel in front (it forwards to the address above, WebSockets included)".into())
        }
    }
    lines.push(format!(
        "  proxies   : this machine{} (client address from {})",
        if o.trust.entries.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(", {}", o.trust.entries.join(", ")) },
        o.real_ip
    ));
    if o.trust.cloudflare && o.tls == Tls::Cert {
        lines.push(
            "  cloudflare: its addresses must show its origin-pull certificate (turn on Authenticated Origin Pulls), or their handshakes fail"
                .into(),
        );
    }
    lines.push(format!("  names     : {} (other Host names get 421)", names.join(", ")));
    lines.push(format!("  switch    : at most {} players", o.max_peers));
    lines.push(format!(
        "  free roam : {}",
        if o.roam_hub {
            "the hub at 10.77.0.253 on the switch gives each player the cars of its nearest, as many as its game shows (64 at most), one way where they show fewer (core 15; --roam-hub off: groups of 65 by broadcast)"
        } else {
            "no hub (--roam-hub off): players find each other by broadcast, groups of 65"
        }
    ));
    if o.roam_hub {
        // the quota the hub's busy cap reads besides the workers (nfsu2_util::cpu::QuotaBusy)
        let quotas = QuotaBusy::find().map(|q| q.quotas()).unwrap_or_default();
        lines.push(match quotas.iter().min_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1)) {
            Some((group, cores)) => {
                format!("  CPU quota : {cores} cores for {group}; over 85 % of them in use, free roam gives fewer friends")
            }
            None => {
                "  CPU quota : none seen (a container sees its slice's with cgroup: host); free roam's busy cap reads the workers".into()
            }
        });
    }
    lines.push(format!(
        "  online    : {}",
        if o.online {
            format!(
                "the game's Online mode at 10.77.0.1 on the switch (any name logs in; race results per persona in {})",
                paths::join(&o.state, "online")
            )
        } else {
            "off (--online off)".into()
        }
    ));
    lines.push(format!(
        "  saves     : {}",
        match &app.vault {
            Some(v) => {
                let vo = v.store.options();
                format!(
                    "keyphrase saves (/vault) in {}, up to {} (new keyphrases until {}, growing {} a day at most); one \
                     unused for two years goes",
                    vo.dir.display(),
                    size(vo.max_bytes),
                    size(vo.new_until),
                    size(vo.per_day)
                )
            }
            None => "no keyphrase saves (--vault-gb 0)".into(),
        }
    ));
    lines.push(format!(
        "  blocks    : {}",
        app.kept.as_ref().map_or_else(
            || format!("compressed as they are sent (NFSU2_COMPRESS_THREADS=0{})", if o.dev { ", --dev's default" } else { "" }),
            |k| k.summary()
        )
    ));

        format!(
            "  bans      : {bans}; nfsu2-server ctl who, kick, ban, raceban, rename, unban, bans, history (through {})",
            paths::join(&o.state, super::control::SOCKET)

    } else {

    });

    }

            "  dev       : test pages (/test/), test scripts (/tests/), source maps{}",
            if o.artifacts.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!(", PUT /artifacts/<name>.png into {}", o.artifacts) }
        ));
    }

    log::line(&lines.join("\n"));

    // count that stopped is tried again in ten minutes, not a day (until one ends, the caps wait)
    if let Some(v) = vault {
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            loop {
                let (t0, st) = (std::time::Instant::now(), v.clone());
                let failed = match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || st.sweep(nfsu2_util::now_ms())).await {
                    Ok(Ok(s)) => {
                        log::line(&vault_line(&s, v.options().max_bytes, t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64()));

                    }

                        log::error(&format!("[vault] the count of the keyphrase saves stopped: {e}"));
                        true
                    }
                    Err(e) => {
                        log::error(&format!("[vault] the count of the keyphrase saves stopped: {e}"));
                        true
                    }
                };
                tokio::time::sleep(if failed { Duration::from_secs(600) } else { VAULT_SWEEP_EVERY }).await;
            }
        });
    }

    std::future::pending::<()>().await;
}

//! What the players who play change on the Settings page, a day at a time (UTC).  A browser's first Play of a day
//! tells the settings it took from its settings.ini that differ from its device's defaults (web/src/app/settings.ts
//! `changedSettings`, page-id.ts `seen`: `/seen?at=play&id=…&k=<pc|phone|tablet>&s=<key=value,…>`), a switch as on/off,
//! a choice or a number as it applies, the player's own words (a name, a room, crews) only as "set".  The day keeps
//! the totals alone, per kind of device: how many browsers told it ([`Tally::reports`]), and for each setting and
//! value how many have it.  The page tells it once a day (it keeps the day it did), so nothing per browser is kept
//! here and nothing ties a count to a browser.  The day so far sits in days.json beside the day's counts (days.rs);
//! each day that ended is a block of settings.csv, a line per setting and value.  `nfsu2-server ctl settings [n]`
//! sums the last days ([`Tally::table`]).  A script can tell anything: the caps keep a day's tally small whatever
//! it is told, and the counts are for the operator, not for anything that matters.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;

use serde_json::Value;

/// the kinds of device a report names (`k`), in the order the counts keep them
pub const DEVICES: [&str; 3] = ["pc", "phone", "tablet"];
/// settings.csv's head
pub const CSV_HEAD: &str = "day,setting,value,computers,phones,tablets";
/// settings.csv's line of a day's reports, in the setting's place
const REPORTS: &str = "(browsers)";
/// a setting's values past `MAX_VALUES` count here (no value the page tells has brackets)
pub const OTHER: &str = "(other)";
/// the longest `s` taken (the page's longest is about 1 KB: every setting changed)
const MAX_TOLD: usize = 4096;
/// settings a report tells at most (the page has about 60)
const MAX_A_REPORT: usize = 64;
/// settings a day counts at most: a setting first told after this many is not counted that day
const MAX_SETTINGS: usize = 128;
/// values a setting counts in a day, `OTHER` among them
const MAX_VALUES: usize = 32;

/// a setting's name as the page writes it (settings.ts KEYS)
pub fn key_ok(k: &str) -> bool {
    (1..=32).contains(&k.len()) && k.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_lowercase() || b.is_ascii_digit() || b == b'_')
}

/// a value as the page writes it (settings.ts TALLY_VALUE)
pub fn value_ok(v: &str) -> bool {
    (1..=24).contains(&v.len()) && v.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b":._+-".contains(&b))
}

/// what a browser told at its day's first Play
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct Report {
    /// `DEVICES`' index
    device: usize,
    pairs: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Report {
    /// `k` and `s` of a /seen?at=play; None without them (an older page, or a Play after the day's first) or with a
    /// device this does not know.  A pair that is not key=value as the page writes them is skipped, and a setting
    /// told twice counts once.
    pub fn parse(k: Option<&str>, s: Option<&str>) -> Option<Report> {
        let device = DEVICES.iter().position(|d| Some(*d) == k)?;
        let s = s?;
        if s.len() > MAX_TOLD {
            return None;
        }
        let mut pairs: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
        for p in s.split(',') {
            let Some((key, value)) = p.split_once('=') else { continue };
            if !key_ok(key) || !value_ok(value) || pairs.iter().any(|(k, _)| k == key) {
                continue;
            }
            if pairs.len() == MAX_A_REPORT {
                break;
            }
            pairs.push((key.into(), value.into()));
        }
        Some(Report { device, pairs })
    }
}

/// a day's totals (or several days' summed)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Tally {
    /// browsers that told their settings, per device
    pub reports: [u64; 3],
    /// setting -> value -> browsers with it, per device
    pub counts: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, [u64; 3]>>,
}

impl Tally {
    /// a report counted, within the day's caps
    pub fn add(&mut self, r: &Report) {
        self.reports[r.device] += 1;
        for (k, v) in &r.pairs {
            if !self.counts.contains_key(k) {
                if self.counts.len() >= MAX_SETTINGS {
                    continue;
                }
                self.counts.insert(k.clone(), BTreeMap::new());
            }
            let values = self.counts.get_mut(k).expect("there now");
            if let Some(n) = values.get_mut(v) {
                n[r.device] += 1;
                continue;
            }
            let v = if values.len() < MAX_VALUES - 1 { v.clone() } else { OTHER.to_string() };
            values.entry(v).or_default()[r.device] += 1;
        }
    }

    /// another day's (or days') totals added in, without the caps
    pub fn merge(&mut self, o: &Tally) {
        for i in 0..3 {
            self.reports[i] += o.reports[i];
        }
        for (k, vs) in &o.counts {
            let values = self.counts.entry(k.clone()).or_default();
            for (v, c) in vs {
                let n = values.entry(v.clone()).or_default();
                for i in 0..3 {
                    n[i] += c[i];
                }
            }
        }
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.reports == [0; 3]
    }

    /// days.json's "settings": {"reports":[pc,phone,tablet],"counts":{"fps":{"30":[pc,phone,tablet]}}}
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Value {
        let counts: serde_json::Map<String, Value> = self
            .counts
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, vs)| (k.clone(), Value::Object(vs.iter().map(|(v, c)| (v.clone(), Value::from(c.to_vec()))).collect())))
            .collect();
        serde_json::json!({ "reports": self.reports.to_vec(), "counts": counts })
    }

    /// the totals to_json wrote (none: an empty tally, as in a days.json from before them)
    pub fn from_json(v: Option<&Value>) -> Tally {
        let three = |v: &Value| -> [u64; 3] {
            let a = v.as_array();
            [0, 1, 2].map(|i| a.and_then(|a| a.get(i)).and_then(Value::as_u64).unwrap_or(0))
        };
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        let Some(v) = v else { return t };
        if let Some(r) = v.get("reports") {
            t.reports = three(r);
        }
        if let Some(Value::Object(m)) = v.get("counts") {
            for (k, vs) in m {
                if let Value::Object(vs) = vs {
                    t.counts.insert(k.clone(), vs.iter().map(|(v, c)| (v.clone(), three(c))).collect());
                }
            }
        }
        t
    }

    /// settings.csv's lines of a day: its reports, then a line per setting and value
    pub fn csv_lines(&self, day: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let r = self.reports;
        let mut out = vec![format!("{day},{REPORTS},,{},{},{}", r[0], r[1], r[2])];
        for (k, vs) in &self.counts {
            for (v, c) in vs {
                out.push(format!("{day},{k},{v},{},{},{}", c[0], c[1], c[2]));
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// The last `n` days of a settings.csv summed: (those days, oldest first; their totals)
    pub fn from_csv(text: &str, n: usize) -> (Vec<String>, Tally) {
        let rows: Vec<Vec<&str>> = text
            .lines()
            .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && *l != CSV_HEAD)
            .map(|l| l.split(',').collect())
            .filter(|f: &Vec<&str>| f.len() == 6)
            .collect();
        let mut days: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for f in &rows {
            if !days.iter().any(|d| d == f[0]) {
                days.push(f[0].to_string());
            }
        }
        let days = days[days.len().saturating_sub(n)..].to_vec();
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        for f in rows.iter().filter(|f| days.iter().any(|d| d == f[0])) {
            let c = [f[3], f[4], f[5]].map(|x| x.parse::<u64>().unwrap_or(0));
            if f[1] == REPORTS {
                for i in 0..3 {
                    t.reports[i] += c[i];
                }
            } else {
                let n = t.counts.entry(f[1].to_string()).or_default().entry(f[2].to_string()).or_default();
                for i in 0..3 {
                    n[i] += c[i];
                }
            }
        }
        (days, t)
    }

    /// The operator's table: each setting, most changed first, with the share of browsers that changed it (all of
    /// them, then computers, phones and tablets alone), and under it its values, most set first (the first `values`
    /// of them).
    pub fn table(&self, values: usize) -> String {
        let all = self.reports.iter().sum::<u64>();
        let share = |n: u64, of: u64| if of == 0 { "-".to_string() } else { format!("{:.1}%", n as f64 * 100.0 / of as f64) };
        let row = |name: &str, c: [u64; 3]| {
            let n = c.iter().sum::<u64>();
            format!(
                "{name:<30} {n:>9} {:>7} {:>10} {:>7} {:>8}",
                share(n, all),
                share(c[0], self.reports[0]),
                share(c[1], self.reports[1]),
                share(c[2], self.reports[2])
            )
        };
        let sum = |vs: &BTreeMap<String, [u64; 3]>| vs.values().fold([0u64; 3], |a, c| [a[0] + c[0], a[1] + c[1], a[2] + c[2]]);
        let mut settings: Vec<(&String, [u64; 3], &BTreeMap<String, [u64; 3]>)> =
            self.counts.iter().map(|(k, vs)| (k, sum(vs), vs)).collect();
        settings.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.iter().sum::<u64>().cmp(&a.1.iter().sum::<u64>()).then(a.0.cmp(b.0)));
        let mut out = vec![
            format!("{:<30} {:>9} {:>7} {:>10} {:>7} {:>8}", "setting / value", "browsers", "all", "computers", "phones", "tablets"),
            row("(told their settings)", self.reports),
        ];
        for (k, c, vs) in settings {
            out.push(row(k, c));
            let mut vs: Vec<(&String, &[u64; 3])> = vs.iter().collect();
            vs.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.iter().sum::<u64>().cmp(&a.1.iter().sum::<u64>()).then(a.0.cmp(b.0)));
            for (v, c) in vs.iter().take(values) {
                out.push(row(&format!("  = {v}"), **c));
            }
            if vs.len() > values {
                out.push(format!("  ({} more values)", vs.len() - values));
            }
        }
        out.join("\n")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn told(k: &str, s: &str) -> Report {
        Report::parse(Some(k), Some(s)).unwrap()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_report_takes_only_what_the_page_writes() {
        assert_eq!(Report::parse(None, Some("fps=30")), None, "no device: an older page");
        assert_eq!(Report::parse(Some("pc"), None), None, "no settings: not the day's first Play");
        assert_eq!(Report::parse(Some("fridge"), Some("fps=30")), None);
        assert_eq!(Report::parse(Some("pc"), Some(&"a=b,".repeat(2000))), None, "too long");
        assert_eq!(told("phone", ""), Report { device: 1, pairs: vec![] }, "nothing changed still counts");
        let r = told("pc", "fps=30,FPS=60,fps=60,render=scale:0.75,roam_name=set,x=a b,y=,=z,nopair,resolution=2560x1440");
        let pairs: Vec<(&str, &str)> = r.pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.as_str())).collect();
        assert_eq!(pairs, [("fps", "30"), ("render", "scale:0.75"), ("roam_name", "set"), ("resolution", "2560x1440")]);
        let many: Vec<String> = (0..100).map(|i| format!("k{i}=1")).collect();
        assert_eq!(told("pc", &many.join(",")).pairs.len(), MAX_A_REPORT);
    }

    #[test]
    fn counts_per_device_within_the_caps() {
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        t.add(&told("pc", "fps=30,hud=43"));
        t.add(&told("phone", "fps=30"));
        t.add(&told("phone", ""));
        t.add(&told("tablet", "fps=120"));
        assert_eq!(t.reports, [1, 2, 1]);
        assert_eq!(t.counts["fps"]["30"], [1, 1, 0]);
        assert_eq!(t.counts["fps"]["120"], [0, 0, 1]);
        assert_eq!(t.counts["hud"]["43"], [1, 0, 0]);

        // a setting's values past the cap count as one; settings past theirs are not counted
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        for i in 0..100 {
            t.add(&told("pc", &format!("gamepad_deadzone=0.{i}")));
        }
        assert_eq!(t.counts["gamepad_deadzone"].len(), MAX_VALUES);
        assert_eq!(t.counts["gamepad_deadzone"][OTHER], [100 - (MAX_VALUES as u64 - 1), 0, 0]);
        t.add(&told("pc", "gamepad_deadzone=0.5"));
        assert_eq!(t.counts["gamepad_deadzone"]["0.5"], [2, 0, 0], "a value counted before still counts");
        for i in 0..200 {
            t.add(&told("pc", &format!("k{i}=1")));
        }
        assert_eq!(t.counts.len(), MAX_SETTINGS);
        assert_eq!(t.reports, [301, 0, 0]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn json_and_csv_keep_the_totals() {
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        t.add(&told("pc", "fps=30,hud=43"));
        t.add(&told("phone", "fps=30"));
        assert_eq!(Tally::from_json(Some(&t.to_json())), t);
        assert_eq!(Tally::from_json(None), Tally::default(), "a days.json from before the tally");

        let mut u = Tally::default();
        u.add(&told("tablet", "fps=120"));
        let csv = [CSV_HEAD.to_string()]
            .into_iter()
            .chain(t.csv_lines("2026-11-02"))
            .chain(u.csv_lines("2026-11-03"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("\n");
        assert_eq!(t.csv_lines("2026-11-02"), ["2026-11-02,(browsers),,1,1,0", "2026-11-02,fps,30,1,1,0", "2026-11-02,hud,43,1,0,0"]);
        let (days, last) = Tally::from_csv(&csv, 1);
        assert_eq!(days, ["2026-11-03"]);
        assert_eq!(last, u);
        let (days, both) = Tally::from_csv(&csv, 30);
        assert_eq!(days, ["2026-11-02", "2026-11-03"]);
        let mut sum = t.clone();
        sum.merge(&u);
        assert_eq!(both, sum);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_table_puts_the_most_changed_first() {
        let mut t = Tally::default();
        for _ in 0..3 {
            t.add(&told("phone", "fps=30,hud=43"));
        }
        t.add(&told("pc", "fps=120"));
        t.add(&told("pc", ""));
        let s = t.table(1);
        let lines: Vec<&str> = s.lines().collect();
        assert!(lines[1].starts_with("(told their settings)") && lines[1].contains(" 5 ") && lines[1].contains("100.0%"), "{s}");
        assert!(lines[2].starts_with("fps ") && lines[2].contains("80.0%"), "{s}");
        assert!(lines[3].starts_with("  = 30 ") && lines[3].contains("60.0%") && lines[3].contains("100.0%"), "{s}");
        assert_eq!(lines[4], "  (1 more values)");
        assert!(lines[5].starts_with("hud ") && lines[5].ends_with('-'), "no tablets told: {s}");
    }
}
