//! What the route tests share: a made-up install folder, page folder and module in a temporary folder, the App on an
//! ephemeral port of 127.0.0.1 (no Online host, no free-roam hub), and a raw client that reads whole answers.

use std::net::SocketAddr;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::TcpStream;

use nfsu2_http::Limits;
use nfsu2_lan::{LanOptions, LanSwitch};

use super::{App, etag};
use crate::options::{RealFs, parse};

pub struct Kit {
    pub dir: tempfile::TempDir,
    pub app: Arc<App>,
    pub addr: SocketAddr,
    server: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
}

impl Drop for Kit {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.server.abort();
    }
}

/// bytes that compress (a few values) or not (xorshift noise)
pub fn data(n: usize, compressible: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
    data_bits(n, if compressible { 2 } else { 8 })
}

/// noise of `bits` bits a byte (7: it compresses by a little, so a run stays about as large as it is)
pub fn data_bits(n: usize, bits: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut x = 0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1du64;
    (0..n)
        .map(|_| {
            x ^= x << 13;
            x ^= x >> 7;
            x ^= x << 17;
            if bits == 2 { ((x & 3) as u8) * 0x41 } else { (x as u8) & ((1u16 << bits) - 1) as u8 }
        })
        .collect()
}

impl Kit {
    /// the server with these options besides the folders; `files(root)` adds what a test needs to the folder (game/,
    /// repo/web/dist/, repo/out/web/)
    pub async fn start(args: &[&str], files: impl FnOnce(&std::path::Path)) -> Kit {
        Kit::start_with(args, Limits::default(), files).await
    }

    /// `start`, with the engine's limits given (max_connections: the port's count)
    pub async fn start_with(args: &[&str], limits: Limits, files: impl FnOnce(&std::path::Path)) -> Kit {
        Kit::start_full(args, limits, 0, files).await
    }

    /// `start`, with threads that keep the game data's blocks at brotli's best (kept.rs; none in the others)
    pub async fn start_keeping(threads: usize, files: impl FnOnce(&std::path::Path)) -> Kit {
        Kit::start_full(&[], Limits::default(), threads, files).await
    }

    async fn start_full(args: &[&str], limits: Limits, compress_threads: usize, files: impl FnOnce(&std::path::Path)) -> Kit {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().expect("a temporary folder");
        let root = std::fs::canonicalize(dir.path()).expect("its real path");
        let p = |r: &str| root.join(r);
        for d in ["game/GLOBAL", "game/TRACKS", "repo/web/dist", "repo/out/web", "state"] {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(p(d)).expect("a folder");
        }
        std::fs::write(p("game/SPEED2.EXE"), b"MZ the game").expect("a file");
        std::fs::write(p("game/GLOBAL/small.bin"), data(1000, true)).expect("a file");
        std::fs::write(p("repo/web/dist/index.html"), b"<!doctype html>").expect("a file");
        files(&root);
        let s = |r: &str| p(r).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let mut argv: Vec<String> =
            ["--data", &s("game"), "--state", &s("state"), "--online", "off", "--roam-hub", "off"].iter().map(|a| a.to_string()).collect();
        argv.extend(args.iter().map(|a| a.to_string()));
        let o = parse(&argv, &|_| None, &s("repo"), &s(""), &RealFs).expect("the options");
        let real_state = std::fs::canonicalize(&o.state).expect("the state folder").to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let key = etag::load_key(&o.state).expect("the ETag key");
        let lan = LanSwitch::new(LanOptions { max_peers: o.max_peers, ..LanOptions::default() }, "", None, None, None, None);
        let vault = (o.vault_gb > 0.0).then(|| {
            let opts = nfsu2_vault::VaultOptions::sized(std::path::PathBuf::from(&o.state).join("vault"), o.vault_gb);
            Arc::new(nfsu2_vault::Vault::open(opts).expect("the vault"))
        });
        let bans = Arc::new(nfsu2_bans::Bans::open(std::path::Path::new(&o.state)).expect("the bans"));
        let names = vault.as_ref().map(|_| super::names::NamesRoute::new(Arc::new(nfsu2_claims::Claims::in_memory()), None));
        let days = Arc::new(super::days::Days::open(&o.state, nfsu2_util::now_ms()));
        let app = Arc::new(App::new(o, real_state, key, lan, None, None, vault, names, bans, days, 2, 0, compress_threads));
        app.refresh_manifest().await.expect("the manifest");
        let (listener, _) = nfsu2_http::bind("127.0.0.1", 0, None).await.expect("a port");
        let addr = listener.local_addr().expect("its address");
        let server = nfsu2_http::serve(listener, None, Arc::new(limits), app.clone());
        Kit { dir, app, addr, server }
    }

    pub fn path(&self, rel: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        std::fs::canonicalize(self.dir.path()).expect("its real path").join(rel)
    }

    /// a connection with this request written to it
    pub async fn send(&self, path: &str, headers: &[(&str, &str)]) -> TcpStream {
        let mut s = TcpStream::connect(self.addr).await.expect("connect");
        let mut req = format!("GET {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n");
        for (k, v) in headers {
            req.push_str(&format!("{k}: {v}\r\n"));
        }
        req.push_str("Connection: close\r\n\r\n");
        s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).await.expect("write");
        s
    }

    /// any request, with a body (a Content-Length for it when there is one): the whole answer
    pub async fn request(&self, method: &str, path: &str, headers: &[(&str, &str)], body: &[u8]) -> Answer {
        let mut s = TcpStream::connect(self.addr).await.expect("connect");
        let mut req = format!("{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n");
        for (k, v) in headers {
            req.push_str(&format!("{k}: {v}\r\n"));
        }
        if !body.is_empty() {
            req.push_str(&format!("Content-Length: {}\r\n", body.len()));
        }
        req.push_str("Connection: close\r\n\r\n");
        let mut all = req.into_bytes();
        all.extend_from_slice(body);
        s.write_all(&all).await.expect("write");
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), s.read_to_end(&mut b)).await.expect("an answer in time").expect("read");
        Answer::parse(&b)
    }

    /// GET path: the whole answer
    pub async fn get(&self, path: &str, headers: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Answer {
        let mut s = self.send(path, headers).await;
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), s.read_to_end(&mut b)).await.expect("an answer in time").expect("read");
        Answer::parse(&b)
    }
}

/// the connection goes with a reset (SO_LINGER 0), as a client that is killed or that drops a request does
pub fn reset(s: TcpStream) {
    let _ = s.set_zero_linger();
    drop(s);
}

/// an answer as the client read it: the status, the headers (names in lower case), the body (de-chunked)
pub struct Answer {
    pub status: u16,
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Answer {
    pub fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Answer {
        let end = b.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n").expect("a whole head");
        let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..end]).into_owned();
        let mut lines = head.split("\r\n");
        let status = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.split(' ').nth(1)).and_then(|c| c.parse().ok()).expect("a status line");
        let headers: Vec<(String, String)> =
            lines.filter_map(|l| l.split_once(": ")).map(|(k, v)| (k.to_ascii_lowercase(), v.to_string())).collect();
        let mut body = b[end + 4..].to_vec();
        if headers.iter().any(|(k, v)| k == "transfer-encoding" && v == "chunked") {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            let mut at = 0;
            loop {
                let nl = at + body[at..].windows(2).position(|w| w == b"\r\n").expect("a chunk size");
                let n = usize::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(&body[at..nl]).expect("hex"), 16).expect("hex");
                if n == 0 {
                    break;
                }
                out.extend_from_slice(&body[nl + 2..nl + 2 + n]);
                at = nl + 2 + n + 2;
            }
            body = out;
        }
        Answer { status, headers, body }
    }

    pub fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.headers.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == name).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }
}

/// waits (up to 5 s) for `ok()`
pub async fn eventually(what: &str, mut ok: impl FnMut() -> bool) {
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    while !ok() {
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5), "{what}: not in 5 s");
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
    }
}

//! Cloudflare Turnstile: the check that a person, not a script, claims a name (/names, names.rs).  The page shows
//! Cloudflare's widget for the site key and sends what it got; the server asks Cloudflare (siteverify) whether that
//! passed, once.  Off unless the server has both keys: NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SITE and NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SECRET (from the
//! Cloudflare dashboard; the secret never on the command line).  With them the page's Content-Security-Policy lets in
//! Cloudflare's script and frame (challenges.cloudflare.com: nfsu2-headers `CSP_TURNSTILE`).
//!
//! The question goes out over HTTPS (outbound.rs), 10 s at most.  NFSU2_TURNSTILE_VERIFY
//! points it elsewhere (the tests' own server, over http://).

use std::time::Duration;

use super::outbound::{Https, form};

pub const VERIFY: &str = "https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/siteverify";
const TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

pub struct Turnstile {
    /// the widget's key (the page's, public)
    pub site: String,
    secret: String,
    verify: String,
    https: Https,
}

impl Turnstile {
    /// the keys from the environment (both, or none)
    pub fn from_env() -> Option<Turnstile> {
        let get = |k: &str| std::env::var(k).ok().map(|v| v.trim().to_string()).filter(|v| !v.is_empty());
        let (site, secret) = (get("NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SITE")?, get("NFSU2_TURNSTILE_SECRET")?);
        Some(Turnstile::new(site, secret, get("NFSU2_TURNSTILE_VERIFY").unwrap_or_else(|| VERIFY.to_string())))
    }

    pub fn new(site: String, secret: String, verify: String) -> Turnstile {
        Turnstile { site, secret, verify, https: Https::new() }
    }

    /// the widget's answer passed Cloudflare's check (Err: Cloudflare could not be asked)
    pub async fn passed(&self, response: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
        if response.is_empty() || response.len() > 2048 {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let body = format!("secret={}&response={}", form(&self.secret), form(response));
        let post = self.https.post_form(&self.verify, &body);
        let (status, answer) = tokio::time::timeout(TIMEOUT, post).await.map_err(|_| "no answer in 10 s".to_string())??;
        if status != 200 {
            return Err(format!("answered {status}"));
        }
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&answer).map_err(|e| format!("its answer: {e}"))?;
        Ok(v.get("success").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};

    /// a server that answers one request with `answer`, and what it was asked
    async fn fake(answer: &'static str) -> (String, tokio::task::JoinHandle<String>) {
        let l = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let url = format!("http://{}/turnstile/v0/siteverify", l.local_addr().unwrap());
        let h = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let (mut s, _) = l.accept().await.unwrap();
            let mut got = Vec::new();
            let mut b = [0u8; 4096];
            while !String::from_utf8_lossy(&got).contains("response=") {
                let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
                got.extend_from_slice(&b[..n]);
            }
            s.write_all(answer.as_bytes()).await.unwrap();
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&got).into_owned()
        });
        (url, h)
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn cloudflare_says_yes_or_no() {
        let (url, h) = fake("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n{\"success\":true}").await;
        let t = Turnstile::new("site".into(), "s3cret&=".into(), url);
        assert_eq!(t.passed("tok en").await, Ok(true));
        let asked = h.await.unwrap();
        assert!(asked.starts_with("POST /turnstile/v0/siteverify HTTP/1.1\r\n"), "{asked}");
        assert!(asked.ends_with("secret=s3cret%26%3D&response=tok%20en"), "{asked}");
        let (url, _) = fake("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n11\r\n{\"success\":false}\r\n0\r\n\r\n").await;
        let t = Turnstile::new("site".into(), "s".into(), url);
        assert_eq!(t.passed("x").await, Ok(false));
        let (url, _) = fake("HTTP/1.1 500 Oops\r\n\r\n").await;
        let t = Turnstile::new("site".into(), "s".into(), url);
        assert!(t.passed("x").await.is_err());
        // nothing to ask about
        assert_eq!(t.passed("").await, Ok(false));
    }
}

//! A request target read as the Node server read it: `new URL('http://x' + url)` for a path ("/path?query", origin
//! form), `new URL(url)` for anything else (an absolute URL, and an Origin header), by the WHATWG URL parser's rules:
//! "\" is "/" in a special scheme's path, "." and ".." segments are resolved (also as "%2e"), what the path and query
//! percent-encode sets name is encoded, tabs and newlines are dropped, and a host is lowercased, percent-decoded and
//! read as an IPv4 or IPv6 address where it is one.  Then `decodeURIComponent` and `URLSearchParams`.
//!
//! Only what the routes need: the pathname, the query's parameters and the host.  Left out: Unicode host names (IDNA:
//! refused here, where Node would turn them into punycode), the validation of punycode labels beyond "xn--" alone,
//! and file URLs' Windows drive letters.

use std::fmt::Write;
use std::net::Ipv6Addr;

/// What a parsed URL gives the routes.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Url {
    /// `u.host`: the host and the port unless it is the scheme's own ("" for none)
    pub host: String,
    /// `u.pathname`, still percent-encoded
    pub pathname: String,
    /// `u.search` without its "?" (None: no "?")
    pub query: Option<String>,
}

impl Url {
    /// `u.searchParams.get(name)`
    pub fn param(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
        search_params(self.query.as_deref()?).into_iter().find(|(k, _)| k == name).map(|(_, v)| v)
    }
    /// `u.searchParams.has(name)`
    pub fn has_param(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.query.as_deref().is_some_and(|q| search_params(q).iter().any(|(k, _)| k == name))
    }
}

/// `new URL(target.startsWith('/') ? 'http://x' + target : target)`; None where it throws
pub fn parse_target(target: &str) -> Option<Url> {
    if target.starts_with('/') { Some(parse_path(target)) } else { parse_absolute(target) }
}

/// leading and trailing C0 controls and spaces go, and every tab and newline
fn preprocess(input: &str) -> String {
    input.trim_matches(|c: char| c <= '\u{20}').chars().filter(|&c| c != '\t' && c != '\n' && c != '\r').collect()
}

/// `new URL('http://x' + target)` for a target that starts with "/"
pub fn parse_path(target: &str) -> Url {
    let s = preprocess(&format!("http://x{target}"));
    let rest = &s["http://x".len()..];
    let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(rest, true);
    Url { host: "x".into(), pathname, query }
}

const SPECIAL: [(&str, Option<u16>); 6] =
    [("ftp", Some(21)), ("file", None), ("http", Some(80)), ("https", Some(443)), ("ws", Some(80)), ("wss", Some(443))];

/// `new URL(input)` without a base; None where it throws
pub fn parse_absolute(input: &str) -> Option<Url> {
    let s = preprocess(input);
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    if b.is_empty() || !b[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut i = 1;
    while i < b.len() && (b[i].is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b[i], b'+' | b'-' | b'.')) {
        i += 1;
    }
    if i >= b.len() || b[i] != b':' {
        return None;
    }
    let scheme = s[..i].to_ascii_lowercase();
    let rest = &s[i + 1..];
    let special = SPECIAL.iter().find(|(n, _)| *n == scheme);
    match special {
        Some(&("file", _)) => parse_file(rest),
        Some(&(_, default_port)) => {
            // the special authority slashes, however many and of either kind
            let rest = rest.trim_start_matches(['/', '\\']);
            let (host, after) = authority(rest, true, default_port)?;
            let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(after, true);
            Some(Url { host, pathname, query })
        }
        None => {
            if let Some(r) = rest.strip_prefix("//") {
                let (host, after) = authority(r, false, None)?;
                let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(after, false);
                Some(Url { host, pathname, query })
            } else if let Some(r) = rest.strip_prefix('/') {
                let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(&format!("/{r}"), false);
                Some(Url { host: String::new(), pathname, query })
            } else {
                // an opaque path ("mailto:x"): no host
                let end = rest.find(['?', '#']).unwrap_or(rest.len());
                let mut pathname = String::new();
                for c in rest[..end].chars() {
                    encode(&mut pathname, c, c0_control);
                }
                let query = query_of(&rest[end..], false);
                Some(Url { host: String::new(), pathname, query })
            }
        }
    }
}

/// a file URL: its host ("localhost" is none) and path; no port
fn parse_file(rest: &str) -> Option<Url> {
    let r = rest.strip_prefix(['/', '\\']);
    let Some(r) = r.and_then(|r| r.strip_prefix(['/', '\\'])) else {
        let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(rest, true);
        return Some(Url { host: String::new(), pathname, query });
    };
    let end = r.find(['/', '\\', '?', '#']).unwrap_or(r.len());
    let mut host = if end == 0 { String::new() } else { host_parse(&r[..end], false)? };
    if host == "localhost" {
        host.clear();
    }
    let (pathname, query) = path_and_query(&r[end..], true);
    Some(Url { host, pathname, query })
}

/// the authority up to the path: the host (after the last "@") and port, as `u.host`; and what follows
fn authority(rest: &str, special: bool, default_port: Option<u16>) -> Option<(String, &str)> {
    let end = if special { rest.find(['/', '\\', '?', '#']) } else { rest.find(['/', '?', '#']) }.unwrap_or(rest.len());
    let auth = &rest[..end];
    let hostport = match auth.rfind('@') {
        Some(at) => {
            let h = &auth[at + 1..];
            if h.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            h
        }
        None => auth,
    };
    // a ":" outside brackets starts the port
    let mut inside = false;
    let mut colon = None;
    for (i, c) in hostport.char_indices() {
        match c {
            '[' => inside = true,
            ']' => inside = false,
            ':' if !inside => {
                colon = Some(i);
                break;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let (name, port) = match colon {
        Some(i) => (&hostport[..i], Some(&hostport[i + 1..])),
        None => (hostport, None),
    };
    if name.is_empty() && (special || colon.is_some()) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut host = host_parse(name, !special)?;
    if let Some(p) = port {
        if !p.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
            return None;
        }
        if !p.is_empty() {
            let digits = p.trim_start_matches('0');
            if digits.len() > 5 {
                return None;
            }
            let n: u32 = if digits.is_empty() { 0 } else { digits.parse().ok()? };
            if n > 65535 {
                return None;
            }
            if default_port != Some(n as u16) {
                let _ = write!(host, ":{n}");
            }
        }
    }
    Some((host, &rest[end..]))
}

/// a C0 control or anything above "~"
fn c0_control(c: char) -> bool {
    c <= '\u{1F}' || c > '~'
}
fn query_set(c: char) -> bool {
    c0_control(c) || matches!(c, ' ' | '"' | '#' | '<' | '>')
}
fn special_query_set(c: char) -> bool {
    query_set(c) || c == '\''
}
fn path_set(c: char) -> bool {
    query_set(c) || matches!(c, '?' | '^' | '`' | '{' | '}')
}
/// Node's parser (Ada) encodes a path only when it holds a character of the path set as it was before "^" joined it
/// (its quick check of the path predates that): "/^" stays "/^", "/^{" is "/%5E%7B"
fn path_set_before_caret(c: char) -> bool {
    c != '^' && path_set(c)
}
fn no_set(_: char) -> bool {
    false
}

/// c, or its UTF-8 bytes as %XX when the set names it
fn encode(out: &mut String, c: char, set: fn(char) -> bool) {
    if set(c) {
        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
        for b in c.encode_utf8(&mut buf).bytes() {
            let _ = write!(out, "%{b:02X}");
        }
    } else {
        out.push(c);
    }
}

fn is_single_dot(s: &str) -> bool {
    s == "." || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("%2e")
}
fn is_double_dot(s: &str) -> bool {
    s == ".." || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case(".%2e") || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("%2e.") || s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("%2e%2e")
}

/// the path (from the path start state on) and the query of what follows the host
fn path_and_query(rest: &str, special: bool) -> (String, Option<String>) {
    let end = rest.find(['?', '#']).unwrap_or(rest.len());
    let path = &rest[..end];
    let query = query_of(&rest[end..], special);
    // the path start state: a special URL always has a path, its first "/" (or "\") is the start of it
    let body = if special {
        path.strip_prefix(['/', '\\']).unwrap_or(path)
    } else if path.is_empty() {
        return (String::new(), query);
    } else {
        path.strip_prefix('/').unwrap_or(path)
    };
    let sep = |c: char| c == '/' || (special && c == '\\');
    let set: fn(char) -> bool = if body.chars().any(path_set_before_caret) { path_set } else { no_set };
    let mut segs: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut buf = String::new();
    let mut chars = body.chars();
    loop {
        let c = chars.next();
        match c {
            Some(c) if !sep(c) => encode(&mut buf, c, set),
            _ => {
                let at_sep = c.is_some();
                if is_double_dot(&buf) {
                    segs.pop();
                    if !at_sep {
                        segs.push(String::new());
                    }
                } else if is_single_dot(&buf) {
                    if !at_sep {
                        segs.push(String::new());
                    }
                } else {
                    segs.push(std::mem::take(&mut buf));
                }
                buf.clear();
                if !at_sep {
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let mut pathname = String::with_capacity(path.len() + 1);
    for s in &segs {
        pathname.push('/');
        pathname.push_str(s);
    }
    (pathname, query)
}

/// the query of "?query#fragment" (None without a "?"), percent-encoded as the URL keeps it
fn query_of(rest: &str, special: bool) -> Option<String> {
    let q = rest.strip_prefix('?')?;
    let q = &q[..q.find('#').unwrap_or(q.len())];
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(q.len());
    for c in q.chars() {
        encode(&mut out, c, if special { special_query_set } else { query_set });
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// percent-decoding as the URL standard does it: "%XX" is that byte, any other "%" stays
fn percent_decode(s: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < s.len() {
        if s[i] == b'%'
            && i + 2 < s.len()
            && let (Some(h), Some(l)) = (hex(s[i + 1]), hex(s[i + 2]))
        {
            out.push(h << 4 | l);
            i += 3;
            continue;
        }
        out.push(s[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

fn hex(c: u8) -> Option<u8> {
    (c as char).to_digit(16).map(|d| d as u8)
}

/// `URLSearchParams` of a query: "&"-separated, "name=value" (no "=": an empty value), "+" a space, percent-decoded,
/// UTF-8 with U+FFFD for what is not
pub fn search_params(query: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for part in query.as_bytes().split(|&c| c == b'&') {
        if part.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = match part.iter().position(|&c| c == b'=') {
            Some(i) => (&part[..i], &part[i + 1..]),
            None => (part, &part[part.len()..]),
        };
        let decode = |x: &[u8]| {
            let plus: Vec<u8> = x.iter().map(|&c| if c == b'+' { b' ' } else { c }).collect();
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&percent_decode(&plus)).into_owned()
        };
        out.push((decode(k), decode(v)));
    }
    out
}

/// `decodeURIComponent(s)`; None where it throws (a "%" without two hex digits, bytes that are not UTF-8)
pub fn decode_uri_component(s: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if !s.contains('%') {
        return Some(s.to_string());
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    let byte_at = |i: usize| -> Option<u8> {
        if b.get(i) != Some(&b'%') {
            return None;
        }
        Some(hex(*b.get(i + 1)?)? << 4 | hex(*b.get(i + 2)?)?)
    };
    while i < b.len() {
        if b[i] != b'%' {
            // a whole character (s is UTF-8: copy up to the next "%")
            let next = s[i..].find('%').map_or(b.len(), |n| i + n);
            out.push_str(&s[i..next]);
            i = next;
            continue;
        }
        let b0 = byte_at(i)?;
        i += 3;
        if b0 < 0x80 {
            out.push(b0 as char);
            continue;
        }
        let n = if b0 & 0xE0 == 0xC0 {
            2
        } else if b0 & 0xF0 == 0xE0 {
            3
        } else if b0 & 0xF8 == 0xF0 {
            4
        } else {
            return None;
        };
        let mut octets = vec![b0];
        for _ in 1..n {
            let c = byte_at(i)?;
            if c & 0xC0 != 0x80 {
                return None;
            }
            octets.push(c);
            i += 3;
        }
        // from_utf8 refuses what decodeURIComponent refuses: overlong forms, surrogates, above U+10FFFF
        out.push_str(std::str::from_utf8(&octets).ok()?);
    }
    Some(out)
}

/// the host parser: an IPv6 address in brackets, an opaque host (a scheme that is not special), or a domain (ASCII
/// only here), which may be an IPv4 address
fn host_parse(input: &str, opaque: bool) -> Option<String> {
    if let Some(inner) = input.strip_prefix('[') {
        let inner = inner.strip_suffix(']')?;
        let a: Ipv6Addr = inner.parse().ok()?;
        return Some(format!("[{}]", ipv6_serialize(&a)));
    }
    if opaque {
        if input.chars().any(forbidden_host) {
            return None;
        }
        let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len());
        for c in input.chars() {
            encode(&mut out, c, c0_control);
        }
        return Some(out);
    }
    let decoded = percent_decode(input.as_bytes());
    // (Node turns a Unicode name into punycode: refused here)
    if !decoded.is_ascii() || decoded.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let domain = String::from_utf8(decoded).ok()?.to_ascii_lowercase();
    if domain.split('.').any(|l| l == "xn--") {
        return None;
    }
    if domain.chars().any(|c| forbidden_host(c) || c <= '\u{1F}' || c == '%' || c == '\u{7F}') {
        return None;
    }
    if ends_in_a_number(&domain) {
        return ipv4_parse(&domain).map(|v| format!("{}.{}.{}.{}", v >> 24, (v >> 16) & 255, (v >> 8) & 255, v & 255));
    }
    Some(domain)
}

fn forbidden_host(c: char) -> bool {
    matches!(c, '\0' | '\t' | '\n' | '\r' | ' ' | '#' | '/' | ':' | '<' | '>' | '?' | '@' | '[' | '\\' | ']' | '^' | '|')
}

fn ends_in_a_number(s: &str) -> bool {
    let mut parts: Vec<&str> = s.split('.').collect();
    if parts.last() == Some(&"") {
        if parts.len() == 1 {
            return false;
        }
        parts.pop();
    }
    let last = parts.last().copied().unwrap_or("");
    if !last.is_empty() && last.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return true;
    }
    ipv4_number(last).is_some()
}

/// one part of an IPv4 address: decimal, 0x hex or 0 octal (saturating: anything that large is refused anyway)
fn ipv4_number(s: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    if s.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let (digits, radix) = if let Some(h) = s.strip_prefix("0x").or_else(|| s.strip_prefix("0X")) {
        (h, 16)
    } else if s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('0') {
        (&s[1..], 8)
    } else {
        (s, 10)
    };
    let mut v: u64 = 0;
    for c in digits.chars() {
        let d = c.to_digit(radix)? as u64;
        v = v.saturating_mul(radix as u64).saturating_add(d);
    }
    Some(v)
}

fn ipv4_parse(s: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    let mut parts: Vec<&str> = s.split('.').collect();
    if parts.last() == Some(&"") && parts.len() > 1 {
        parts.pop();
    }
    if parts.len() > 4 {
        return None;
    }
    let nums: Vec<u64> = parts.iter().map(|p| ipv4_number(p)).collect::<Option<_>>()?;
    let (last, head) = nums.split_last()?;
    if head.iter().any(|&n| n > 255) {
        return None;
    }
    if *last >= 256u64.pow(5 - nums.len() as u32) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut v = *last;
    for (i, n) in head.iter().enumerate() {
        v += n * 256u64.pow(3 - i as u32);
    }
    Some(v as u32)
}

/// an IPv6 address as the URL standard writes it: lowercase hex, the first longest run of two or more zero pieces as
/// "::", never a dotted IPv4 tail
fn ipv6_serialize(a: &Ipv6Addr) -> String {
    let p = a.segments();
    let (mut best, mut best_len) = (None, 1);
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 8 {
        if p[i] == 0 {
            let start = i;
            while i < 8 && p[i] == 0 {
                i += 1;
            }
            if i - start > best_len {
                best = Some(start);
                best_len = i - start;
            }
        } else {
            i += 1;
        }
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 8 {
        if Some(i) == best {
            out.push_str(if i == 0 { "::" } else { ":" });
            i += best_len;
            continue;
        }
        let _ = write!(out, "{:x}", p[i]);
        if i != 7 {
            out.push(':');
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn path(t: &str) -> (String, Option<String>) {
        let u = parse_path(t);
        (u.pathname, u.query)
    }

    #[test]
    fn paths_as_node_reads_them() {
        // (each answer as node 24 gave it for new URL('http://x' + target))
        assert_eq!(path("/a^b{c}d`e\"f<g>h|i'j").0, "/a%5Eb%7Bc%7Dd%60e%22f%3Cg%3Eh|i'j");
        assert_eq!(path("/a b").0, "/a%20b");
        assert_eq!(path("/\u{7f}").0, "/%7F");
        assert_eq!(path("/é").0, "/%C3%A9");
        assert_eq!(path("/a\\b").0, "/a/b");
        assert_eq!(path("/.%2e/x").0, "/x");
        assert_eq!(path("/%2e%2E/x").0, "/x");
        assert_eq!(path("/a/./b/../c").0, "/a/c");
        assert_eq!(path("/a/..").0, "/");
        assert_eq!(path("/.").0, "/");
        assert_eq!(path("//x").0, "//x");
        assert_eq!(path("/x\t\ny").0, "/xy");
        assert_eq!(path("/x ").0, "/x");
        assert_eq!(path("/x\u{1}").0, "/x");
        assert_eq!(path("/x?q#f"), ("/x".into(), Some("q".into())));
        let u = parse_path("/x?a b&c=d+e&%zz=%C3%A9&=1&&x");
        assert_eq!(u.query.as_deref(), Some("a%20b&c=d+e&%zz=%C3%A9&=1&&x"));
        assert_eq!(
            search_params(u.query.as_deref().unwrap()),
            [("a b", ""), ("c", "d e"), ("%zz", "é"), ("", "1"), ("x", "")].map(|(a, b)| (a.to_string(), b.to_string()))
        );
        assert_eq!(u.param("c").as_deref(), Some("d e"));
        assert!(u.has_param("x") && !u.has_param("y"));
        assert!(parse_path("/data-manifest?refresh").has_param("refresh"));
    }

    fn host(a: &str) -> Option<(String, String, Option<String>)> {
        parse_absolute(a).map(|u| (u.host, u.pathname, u.query))
    }

    #[test]
    fn absolute_urls_as_node_reads_them() {
        let h = |a: &str| host(a).map(|x| x.0);
        assert_eq!(h("http://LOCALHOST:0080/a").as_deref(), Some("localhost"));
        assert_eq!(h("https://localhost:443").as_deref(), Some("localhost"));
        assert_eq!(h("ws://a:80").as_deref(), Some("a"));
        assert_eq!(h("ftp://a:21/").as_deref(), Some("a"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://localhost:8080/x").as_deref(), Some("localhost:8080"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://0x7f.1/").as_deref(), Some("127.0.0.1"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://127.1/").as_deref(), Some("127.0.0.1"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://[::FFFF:1.2.3.4]:8080/").as_deref(), Some("[::ffff:102:304]:8080"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://[1:0:0:2:0:0:0:3]/").as_deref(), Some("[1:0:0:2::3]"));
        assert_eq!(h("foo://LocalHost:9/x").as_deref(), Some("LocalHost:9"));
        assert_eq!(host("foo:/x"), Some(("".into(), "/x".into(), None)));
        assert_eq!(host("foo:x"), Some(("".into(), "x".into(), None)));
        assert_eq!(h("file://localhost/x").as_deref(), Some(""));
        assert_eq!(h("file://127.0.0.1/x").as_deref(), Some("127.0.0.1"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://u:p@host/x").as_deref(), Some("host"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://a@b@c/").as_deref(), Some("c"));
        assert_eq!(host("http:\\\\\\host\\x"), Some(("host".into(), "/x".into(), None)));
        assert_eq!(h("http:host/x").as_deref(), Some("host"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://%6c%6fcalhost/").as_deref(), Some("localhost"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://a..b/").as_deref(), Some("a..b"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://host:/x").as_deref(), Some("host"));
        assert_eq!(h("HTTP://H/").as_deref(), Some("h"));
        assert_eq!(h("http://*/x").as_deref(), Some("*"));
        assert_eq!(host("http://h?x"), Some(("h".into(), "/".into(), Some("x".into()))));
        assert_eq!(host("foo://"), Some(("".into(), "".into(), None)));
        for bad in [
            "http://1.2.3.4.5/",
            "http://1.2.3.256/",
            "http://xn--/",
            "http://host:65536/",
            "http://h:1a/",
            "http://[::1/",
            "http://a b/",
            "http://a%/",
            "null",
            "*",
            "foo://h:99999/",
            "",
            "1http://x/",
            "http://",
            "http://u@/",
        ] {
            assert_eq!(host(bad), None, "{bad}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_as_decode_uri_component() {
        for (s, d) in [
            ("%41", Some("A")),
            ("%e9", None),
            ("%C3%A9", Some("é")),
            ("%ff", None),
            ("%", None),
            ("%4", None),
            ("%C3", None),
            ("%ED%A0%80", None),
            ("%F4%90%80%80", None),
            ("%C0%AE", None),
            ("a%2fb", Some("a/b")),
            ("%E2%82%AC", Some("€")),
            ("é%20x", Some("é x")),
            ("%ZZ", None),
            ("/a%00b", Some("/a\0b")),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(decode_uri_component(s).as_deref(), d, "{s}");
        }
    }

    /// what the routes read of a target, as JSON, the way the node script below writes it
    fn reading(t: &str, absolute: bool) -> serde_json::Value {
        use serde_json::json;
        let u = if absolute { parse_absolute(t) } else { Some(parse_path(t)) };
        match u {
            None => json!("throws"),
            Some(u) => {
                let search = match u.query.as_deref() {
                    None | Some("") => String::new(),
                    Some(q) => format!("?{q}"),
                };
                let params: Vec<Vec<String>> =
                    u.query.as_deref().map(search_params).unwrap_or_default().into_iter().map(|(k, v)| vec![k, v]).collect();
                json!({ "host": if absolute { u.host.clone() } else { String::new() }, "pathname": u.pathname, "search": search, "params": params,
                    "decoded": decode_uri_component(&u.pathname) })
            }
        }
    }

    // the Node server's reading of a target (new URL, its pathname, searchParams, decodeURIComponent) against node's
    // own.  A node whose Ada predates "^" in the path set (v23.9.0 does: it leaves "/^{" as "/^%7B", where the Node
    // server's gave "/%5E%7B", see path_set_before_caret) reads every path with a "^" otherwise: with such a node the
    // targets that hold one are left out (and counted), the others still compared
    #[test]
    fn the_same_reading_as_node() {
        let (paths, abs) = corpus();
        let script = r#"
let input = ''; process.stdin.on('data', d => { input += d; }); process.stdin.on('end', () => {
  const { paths, abs } = JSON.parse(input);
  const read = (t, absolute) => {
    let u; try { u = new URL(absolute ? t : 'http://x' + t); } catch { return 'throws'; }
    let decoded; try { decoded = decodeURIComponent(u.pathname); } catch { decoded = null; }
    return { host: absolute ? u.host : '', pathname: u.pathname, search: u.search, params: [...u.searchParams], decoded };
  };
  const caret = new URL('http://x/^{').pathname;
  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ caret, reads: [...paths.map(t => read(t, false)), ...abs.map(t => read(t, true))] }));
});"#;
        let mut child = match std::process::Command::new("node")
            .args(["-e", script])
            .stdin(std::process::Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
            .spawn()
        {
            Ok(c) => c,
            Err(_) => {
                eprintln!("no node: the cross-check of the URL reading is skipped");
                return;
            }
        };
        let input = serde_json::json!({ "paths": paths, "abs": abs }).to_string();
        std::io::Write::write_all(child.stdin.as_mut().unwrap(), input.as_bytes()).unwrap();
        drop(child.stdin.take());
        let out = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
        assert!(out.status.success());
        let answer: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout).unwrap();
        let node = answer["reads"].as_array().unwrap();
        let old_caret = answer["caret"] == "/^%7B";
        let ours: Vec<serde_json::Value> = paths.iter().map(|t| reading(t, false)).chain(abs.iter().map(|t| reading(t, true))).collect();
        let targets: Vec<&String> = paths.iter().chain(abs.iter()).collect();
        let (mut differ, mut left_out) = (Vec::new(), 0);
        for ((t, n), o) in targets.iter().zip(node).zip(&ours) {
            if old_caret && t.contains('^') {
                left_out += 1;
                continue;
            }
            if n != o {
                differ.push(format!("{t:?}: node {n} ours {o}"));
            }
        }
        if left_out > 0 {
            eprintln!("node's Ada predates \"^\" in the path set: {left_out} of {} targets (with a \"^\") left out", targets.len());
        }
        assert!(left_out < targets.len() / 2, "most targets compared ({left_out} of {} left out)", targets.len());
        // (a Unicode host is refused here where node writes it as punycode: none in the corpus)
        let compared = targets.len() - left_out;
        assert!(differ.is_empty(), "{} of {compared} differ:\n{}", differ.len(), differ[..differ.len().min(30)].join("\n"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn ipv6_written_as_the_standard_says() {
        let s = |a: &str| ipv6_serialize(&a.parse().unwrap());
        assert_eq!(s("::"), "::");
        assert_eq!(s("::1"), "::1");
        assert_eq!(s("1::"), "1::");
        assert_eq!(s("1:0:0:2:0:0:0:3"), "1:0:0:2::3");
        assert_eq!(s("1:0:2:3:4:5:6:7"), "1:0:2:3:4:5:6:7");
        assert_eq!(s("2001:db8:0:0:1:0:0:1"), "2001:db8::1:0:0:1");
    }
}

//! /vault: keyphrase saves (nfsu2-vault), for this server's own pages only.
//!
//! The page sends its token as `Authorization: Bearer <43 characters of base64url>` (never in the URL: no log or
//! cache sees it); the keyphrase is kept under the token's SHA-256.  What it sends and gets back is the page's
//! encrypted save folder: the server neither reads nor checks it.
//!
//! - `GET /vault`: the current version, its rev as the ETag (`If-None-Match` it: 304), `x-vault-saved` when it was
//!   saved and `x-vault-earlier` when the copy of an earlier day was (none: no such header); 404 when there is no such
//!   keyphrase.  `GET /vault?earlier`: that copy, with its own ETag and `x-vault-saved` (404: none).  Without a token:
//!   401, which is how a page tells a server with keyphrase saves (one without answers 404).
//! - `PUT /vault` with `If-None-Match: *` (a new keyphrase) or `If-Match: "<rev>"` (the version the page has): 201 or
//!   200 with the new ETag and `x-vault-saved`; 412 when that does not hold, with the current ETag and
//!   `x-vault-saved` (none: no such keyphrase); 428 with neither; 413 past 256 KB; 507 when the server's room for them
//!   is full, or its disk nearly; 503 (Retry-After) when the bytes the saves may add a day, all clients together,
//!   are taken: a new keyphrase, or a save that grows one past 32 KB (crates/vault, Limits).
//! - `DELETE /vault`: the keyphrase and both its versions go (404: none).
//!
//! Per client (its budget key, and twice that per site as `Rate` does): 60 reads, then one a second; 60 writes, then
//! one every two seconds; 20 new keyphrases, then 20 a day; and 30 reads of keyphrases there are not, then 30 an hour
//! (checked before the read: a client that guesses keyphrases learns nothing past those).  More gets 429.  The
//! console counts keyphrases and bytes, never names one.

use std::sync::Arc;

use nfsu2_headers::Cache;
use nfsu2_http::{Request, Response};
use nfsu2_util::{Rate, js, log};
use nfsu2_vault::{Cond, Put, Vault, Want, id_of};

use super::{App, Fail, Hdrs, Res, finish, present, send, url};
use crate::options::js_to_number;

pub const READ_BURST: f64 = 60.0;
pub const READ_RATE: f64 = 1.0;
pub const WRITE_BURST: f64 = 60.0;
pub const WRITE_RATE: f64 = 0.5;
pub const NEW_BURST: f64 = 20.0;
pub const NEW_RATE: f64 = 20.0 / 86_400.0;
pub const MISS_BURST: f64 = 30.0;
pub const MISS_RATE: f64 = 30.0 / 3600.0;
/// file operations at once (each on a blocking thread)
pub const IO_AT_ONCE: usize = 32;

/// The keyphrase saves of an App: the store and its limits.
pub struct VaultRoute {
    pub store: Arc<Vault>,
    reads: Rate,
    writes: Rate,
    news: Rate,
    misses: Rate,
    io: tokio::sync::Semaphore,
}

impl VaultRoute {
    pub fn new(store: Arc<Vault>) -> VaultRoute {
        VaultRoute {
            store,
            reads: Rate::new(READ_BURST, READ_RATE),
            writes: Rate::new(WRITE_BURST, WRITE_RATE),
            news: Rate::new(NEW_BURST, NEW_RATE),
            misses: Rate::new(MISS_BURST, MISS_RATE),
            io: tokio::sync::Semaphore::new(IO_AT_ONCE),
        }
    }

    /// the buckets that are full again hold nothing worth keeping (every minute)
    pub fn prune(&self) {
        for r in [&self.reads, &self.writes, &self.news, &self.misses] {
            r.prune();
        }
    }
}

/// `Bearer <43 characters of base64url>`: the token (what its SHA-256 keeps the keyphrase under), or None
fn token(q: &Request) -> Option<&str> {
    let t = q.headers.get("authorization")?.strip_prefix("Bearer ")?;
    (t.len() == 43 && t.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'-' || c == b'_')).then_some(t)
}

/// `"<16 hex digits>"`, as the ETag carries a rev
fn etag(rev: u64) -> String {
    format!("\"{rev:016x}\"")
}

/// an If-Match's rev: one strong ETag of ours, else None
fn if_match(v: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    let h = js::trim(v).strip_prefix('"')?.strip_suffix('"')?;
    (h.len() == 16).then(|| u64::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok()).flatten()
}

impl App {
    /// /vault (keyphrase saves): see this module's doc
    pub(super) async fn vault(&self, q: &mut Request, s: &mut Response, u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        const CLOSE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("connection", "close")];
        let Some(v) = &self.vault else { return self.not_found(q, s).await };
        // only this server's own pages: a page of another site must not reach a player's saves through their browser
        let site_ok = q.headers.get("sec-fetch-site").is_none_or(|f| f == "same-origin");
        if !self.own_page(q) || !site_ok {
            return self.plain(q, s, 403, "Forbidden", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let method = q.method.clone();
        if !matches!(method.as_str(), "GET" | "HEAD" | "PUT" | "DELETE") {
            return self
                .plain(q, s, 405, "Method not allowed", &[("allow", "GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE"), ("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true)
                .await;
        }
        if method != "PUT" && (js_to_number(q.headers.get("content-length").unwrap_or("0")) > 0.0 || present(q, "transfer-encoding")) {
            return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let Some(id) = token(q).map(|t| id_of(t.as_bytes())) else {
            return self.plain(q, s, 401, "A keyphrase's token is needed", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        };
        let (_, key, site) = self.client(q);
        let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
        let store = v.store.clone();
        match method.as_str() {
            "GET" | "HEAD" => {
                if !v.reads.take(&key, &site) || !v.misses.check(&key, &site) {
                    return self.too_many(q, s).await;
                }
                let want = if u.has_param("earlier") { Want::Earlier } else { Want::Current };
                // a page that has the current version asks with its ETag: the head is enough for the 304
                let inm = q.headers.get("if-none-match").map(str::to_string);
                if want == Want::Current && inm.is_some() {
                    let st = store.clone();
                    let meta = self.vault_io(v, move || st.meta(&id, now)).await?;
                    if let Some(m) = meta
                        && nfsu2_headers::etag_matches(inm.as_deref(), &etag(m.cur.rev))
                    {
                        self.names_used(&id, now);
                        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
                        vault_headers(&mut h, m.cur.rev, m.cur.saved, m.prev.map(|p| p.saved));
                        s.head(304, h.0);
                        return finish(s).await;
                    }
                }
                let got = self.vault_io(v, move || store.get(&id, want, now)).await?;
                let found = got.and_then(|(m, body)| match want {
                    Want::Current => Some((m.cur, m.prev.map(|p| p.saved), body)),
                    Want::Earlier => m.prev.map(|p| (p, None, body)),
                });
                let Some((ver, earlier, body)) = found else {
                    v.misses.take(&key, &site);
                    return self.not_found(q, s).await;
                };
                // the keyphrase was used: its claimed name lasts as long as it (names.rs)
                self.names_used(&id, now);
                let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
                h.set("content-type", "application/octet-stream");
                h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
                vault_headers(&mut h, ver.rev, ver.saved, earlier);
                s.head(200, h.0);
                if method != "HEAD" {
                    send(s, &body).await?;
                }
                finish(s).await
            }
            "PUT" => {
                let cond = match (q.headers.get("if-match"), q.headers.get("if-none-match")) {
                    (Some(m), _) => match if_match(m) {
                        Some(r) => Cond::Rev(r),
                        None => return self.plain(q, s, 412, "Changed elsewhere", &[], Cache::Store, true).await,
                    },
                    (None, Some(n)) if js::trim(n) == "*" => Cond::New,
                    _ => return self.plain(q, s, 428, "If-Match or If-None-Match: * is needed", &[], Cache::Store, true).await,
                };
                if !v.writes.take(&key, &site) || (cond == Cond::New && !v.news.take(&key, &site)) {
                    return self.too_many(q, s).await;
                }
                let max = store.options().max_body;
                if js_to_number(q.headers.get("content-length").unwrap_or("0")) > max as f64 {
                    return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await;
                }
                let body = match q.read_body(max).await {
                    Ok(b) => b,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::TooLarge) => return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::Broken) => {
                        s.destroy();
                        return Err(Fail::Gone);
                    }
                };
                let put = self.vault_io(v, move || store.put(&id, cond, &body, now)).await?;
                let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
                let (code, text) = match put {
                    Put::Saved { meta, created } => {
                        self.names_used(&id, now);
                        vault_headers(&mut h, meta.cur.rev, meta.cur.saved, meta.prev.map(|p| p.saved));
                        if created { (201, "Saved") } else { (200, "Saved") }
                    }
                    Put::Conflict(m) => {
                        if let Some(m) = m {
                            vault_headers(&mut h, m.cur.rev, m.cur.saved, m.prev.map(|p| p.saved));
                        }
                        (412, "Changed elsewhere")
                    }
                    Put::TooLarge => (413, "Too large"),
                    Put::Full => {
                        let (n, bytes, _) = v.store.usage();
                        log::limited(
                            "vault",
                            "full",
                            "",
                            &format!("[vault] refused a save: the room for keyphrase saves is full ({n} keyphrases, {bytes} bytes)"),
                            1,
                        );
                        (507, "The server has no room for more saves")
                    }
                    Put::DiskLow => {
                        let o = v.store.options();
                        log::limited(
                            "vault",
                            "disk",
                            "",
                            &format!(
                                "[vault] refused a save: the disk has less than {} bytes or {} files free",
                                o.min_free, o.min_free_files
                            ),
                            1,
                        );
                        (507, "The server has no room for more saves")
                    }
                    Put::Busy => {
                        log::limited(
                            "vault",
                            "busy",
                            "",
                            &format!(
                                "[vault] refused a save: the {} a day the saves may add are taken for now (all clients \
                                 together)",
                                super::run::size(v.store.options().per_day)
                            ),
                            1,
                        );
                        h.set("retry-after", "3600");
                        (503, "The server takes no more new saves for now")
                    }
                };
                let body = format!("{text}\n");
                h.set("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8");
                h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
                s.head(code, h.0);
                send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
                finish(s).await
            }
            _ => {
                if !v.writes.take(&key, &site) {
                    return self.too_many(q, s).await;
                }
                if self.vault_io(v, move || store.delete(&id)).await? {
                    // its claimed name is free (names.rs)
                    self.release_names(&id);
                    self.plain(q, s, 200, "Deleted", &[], Cache::Store, true).await
                } else {
                    self.not_found(q, s).await
                }
            }
        }
    }

    async fn too_many(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        self.plain(q, s, 429, "Too many requests", &[("retry-after", "60")], Cache::Store, true).await
    }

    /// a file operation on a blocking thread, IO_AT_ONCE of them at most; an error is the 500's (no path in it)
    async fn vault_io<T: Send + 'static>(
        &self,
        v: &VaultRoute,
        f: impl FnOnce() -> std::io::Result<T> + Send + 'static,
    ) -> Result<T, Fail> {
        let _turn = v.io.acquire().await.map_err(|_| Fail::Error("keyphrase saves: closed".into()))?;
        match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(f).await {
            Ok(Ok(t)) => Ok(t),
            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(Fail::Error(format!("keyphrase saves: {e}"))),
            Err(e) => Err(Fail::Error(format!("keyphrase saves: {e}"))),
        }
    }
}

/// a version's ETag and time, and when the copy of an earlier day was saved
fn vault_headers(h: &mut Hdrs, rev: u64, saved: i64, earlier: Option<i64>) {
    h.set("etag", etag(rev));
    h.set("x-vault-saved", saved.to_string());
    if let Some(e) = earlier {
        h.set("x-vault-earlier", e.to_string());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::testkit::Kit;
    use super::*;

    const TOKEN: &str = "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA";
    const BEARER: (&str, &str) = ("Authorization", "Bearer AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA");

    fn bearer(t: &str) -> String {
        format!("Bearer {t}")
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_keyphrase_saved_read_changed_and_deleted() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        // a server with keyphrase saves answers a request without a token with 401 (how the page tells)
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[], b"").await.status, 401);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await.status, 404);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"box").await.status, 428);
        let a = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"box one").await;
        assert_eq!(a.status, 201);
        let tag1 = a.header("etag").unwrap().to_string();
        assert_eq!(a.header("cache-control"), Some("private, no-store, no-transform"));
        let saved: i64 = a.header("x-vault-saved").unwrap().parse().unwrap();
        assert!((saved - nfsu2_util::now_ms()).abs() < 10_000);
        let g = kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await;
        assert_eq!((g.status, g.body.as_slice(), g.header("etag")), (200, &b"box one"[..], Some(tag1.as_str())));
        assert_eq!(g.header("content-type"), Some("application/octet-stream"));
        assert_eq!(g.header("x-vault-earlier"), None);
        let h = kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", &tag1)], b"").await;
        assert_eq!((h.status, h.body.len()), (304, 0));
        // a second new one, or the wrong version: 412, with what is there
        let c = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"other").await;
        assert_eq!((c.status, c.header("etag")), (412, Some(tag1.as_str())));
        let c = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-Match", "\"0000000000000001\"")], b"other").await;
        assert_eq!((c.status, c.header("etag")), (412, Some(tag1.as_str())));
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-Match", "nonsense")], b"other").await.status, 412);
        let u = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-Match", &tag1)], b"box two").await;
        assert_eq!(u.status, 200);
        let tag2 = u.header("etag").unwrap().to_string();
        assert_ne!(tag1, tag2);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", &tag1)], b"").await.body, b"box two");
        // the same day: no earlier copy
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault?earlier", &[BEARER], b"").await.status, 404);
        // another keyphrase is another file; none of them names a token
        let other = bearer(&"B".repeat(43));
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[("Authorization", &other)], b"").await.status, 404);
        let hex: String = id_of(TOKEN.as_bytes()).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
        let file = kit.path("state/vault").join(&hex[..3]);
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_dir(&file).unwrap().count(), 1);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("DELETE", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("DELETE", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await.status, 404);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await.status, 404);
        assert_eq!(kit.app.vault.as_ref().unwrap().store.usage().0, 0);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn the_copy_of_an_earlier_day() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        let store = kit.app.vault.as_ref().unwrap().store.clone();
        let day_before = nfsu2_util::now_ms() - 2 * nfsu2_vault::DAY_MS;
        let Put::Saved { meta, .. } = store.put(&id_of(TOKEN.as_bytes()), Cond::New, b"old", day_before).unwrap() else { panic!() };
        let u = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-Match", &etag(meta.cur.rev))], b"new").await;
        assert_eq!((u.status, u.header("x-vault-earlier")), (200, Some(day_before.to_string().as_str())));
        let g = kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await;
        assert_eq!((g.body.as_slice(), g.header("x-vault-earlier")), (&b"new"[..], Some(day_before.to_string().as_str())));
        let e = kit.request("GET", "/vault?earlier", &[BEARER], b"").await;
        assert_eq!((e.status, e.body.as_slice()), (200, &b"old"[..]));
        assert_eq!(
            (e.header("etag"), e.header("x-vault-saved")),
            (Some(etag(meta.cur.rev).as_str()), Some(day_before.to_string().as_str()))
        );
        assert_eq!(e.header("x-vault-earlier"), None);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn only_this_servers_own_pages_and_whole_requests() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        for h in [
            ("Origin", "http://evil.example"),
            ("Origin", "null"),
            ("Sec-Fetch-Site", "cross-site"),
            ("Sec-Fetch-Site", "same-site"),
            ("Sec-Fetch-Site", "none"),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER, h], b"").await.status, 403, "{h:?}");
            assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, h, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"x").await.status, 403, "{h:?}");
        }
        let own = [BEARER, ("Origin", "http://localhost"), ("Sec-Fetch-Site", "same-origin")];
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &own, b"").await.status, 404);
        for t in ["Bearer short", &bearer(&"A".repeat(44)), &bearer(&format!("{}+", "A".repeat(42))), &format!("Basic {TOKEN}"), TOKEN] {
            assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[("Authorization", t)], b"").await.status, 401, "{t}");
        }
        let p = kit.request("POST", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"x").await;
        assert_eq!((p.status, p.header("allow")), (405, Some("GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE")));
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"body").await.status, 413);
        // refused by its Content-Length, before the body is read (so none is sent here)
        let over = ((256 << 10) + 1).to_string();
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", "*"), ("Content-Length", &over)], b"").await.status, 413);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", "*")], &vec![1u8; 256 << 10]).await.status, 201);
        // HEAD: the headers alone
        let h = kit.request("HEAD", "/vault", &[BEARER], b"").await;
        assert_eq!((h.status, h.header("content-length"), h.body.len()), (200, Some("262144"), 0));
        assert!(super::super::ROBOTS_TXT.contains("Disallow: /vault\n"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn guesses_and_new_keyphrases_are_limited() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        let t = |i: usize| bearer(&format!("{i:0>43}"));
        // 20 new keyphrases from one client, then 429
        for i in 0..20 {
            assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[("Authorization", &t(i)), ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"x").await.status, 201, "{i}");
        }
        let r = kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[("Authorization", &t(20)), ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"x").await;
        assert_eq!((r.status, r.header("retry-after")), (429, Some("60")));
        // 30 reads of keyphrases there are not, then even one that is there is refused
        for i in 100..130 {
            assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[("Authorization", &t(i))], b"").await.status, 404, "{i}");
        }
        assert_eq!(kit.request("GET", "/vault", &[("Authorization", &t(0))], b"").await.status, 429);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn none_with_vault_gb_0() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&["--vault-gb", "0"], |_| {}).await;
        assert!(kit.app.vault.is_none());

        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[BEARER, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"x").await.status, 404);
        assert!(!kit.path("state/vault").exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn etags_and_if_match() {
        assert_eq!(etag(0x00ab), "\"00000000000000ab\"");
        assert_eq!(if_match(" \"00000000000000ab\" "), Some(0xab));
        for bad in ["*", "W/\"00000000000000ab\"", "\"ab\"", "00000000000000ab", "\"0000000000000xab\"", "\"00000000000000ab\", \"1\""] {
            assert_eq!(if_match(bad), None, "{bad}");
        }
    }

{"id": "AT001707", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/src/app/wasm.rs", "originalBytes": 9850, "originalSha256": "4af6c2791790a45232f8163097c0e877e4047aee67e7cc4ec6ebad5fcfe89d6c", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 9850, "utf8TotalBytes": 9850}

//! The game module: /game.wasm brotli-compressed once per build (kept in memory, ~7 MB; quality 5 takes about half a
//! second for the 65 MB module and is within a few percent of the best ratio for it), and /game.json, which names it.
//!
//! Its hash is the module's content (the raw bytes the body is made from), which /game.json names and the page asks
//! /game.wasm?v= for, so a copy kept anywhere under that address is this module.

use std::io::Write;
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
use std::sync::Arc;

use bytes::Bytes;
use futures_util::FutureExt;
use futures_util::future::{BoxFuture, Shared};
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use serde_json::Value;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use nfsu2_headers::{Cache, etag_matches};
use nfsu2_http::{Request, Response};
use nfsu2_util::{js, log};

use super::url::Url;
use super::{App, Res, etag, files, finish, has_word, send, type_of};
use crate::paths;

/// the compressed module of one build
pub struct WasmReady {
    pub etag: String,
    pub hash: String,
    pub body: Bytes,
}

struct WasmEntry {
    etag: String,
    ready: Shared<BoxFuture<'static, Option<Arc<WasmReady>>>>,
}

/// the build compressed last, or being compressed
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct WasmCell(Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<WasmEntry>>>>);

/// read, hashed and compressed (blocking)
fn compress(path: &str) -> std::io::Result<(String, Vec<u8>)> {
    let raw = std::fs::read(path)?;
    let hash = js::base64url(&Sha256::digest(&raw))[..22].to_string();
    let t0 = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
    let params = brotli::enc::BrotliEncoderParams { quality: 5, size_hint: raw.len(), ..Default::default() };
    let mut w = brotli::CompressorWriter::with_params(Vec::with_capacity(raw.len() / 8), 1 << 16, &params);
    w.write_all(&raw)?;
    let body = w.into_inner();
    let mb = |n: usize| js::to_fixed(n as f64 / 1048576.0, 1);
    log::line(&format!(
        "game.wasm compressed for the network: {} MB -> {} MB in {} ms",
        mb(raw.len()),
        mb(body.len()),
        nfsu2_util::now_ms() - t0
    ));
    Ok((hash, body))
}

impl App {
    /// the module of the build on disk now, compressed (once per build; a request while it is
    /// being compressed waits for it); None when there is none
    pub async fn compressed_wasm(&self) -> Option<Arc<WasmReady>> {
        let md = tokio::fs::metadata(&self.o.wasm).await.ok()?;
        let etag = etag::etag_of(&self.etag_key, &["br", &self.o.wasm, &etag::num(md.size() as f64), &etag::num(etag::mtime_ms(&md))]);
        let ready = {
            let mut cur = self.wasm.0.lock();
            match cur.as_ref() {
                Some(e) if e.etag == etag => e.ready.clone(),
                _ => {
                    let e = Arc::new(WasmEntry { etag: etag.clone(), ready: self.start_compression(etag) });
                    *cur = Some(e.clone());
                    e.ready.clone()
                }
            }
        };
        ready.await
    }

    /// the compression of a build, under way from now on (on a blocking thread), whoever waits for it
    fn start_compression(&self, etag: String) -> Shared<BoxFuture<'static, Option<Arc<WasmReady>>>> {
        let cell = self.wasm.0.clone();
        let path = self.o.wasm.clone();
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let why = match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || compress(&path)).await {
                Ok(Ok((hash, body))) => return Some(Arc::new(WasmReady { etag, hash, body: Bytes::from(body) })),
                Ok(Err(e)) => e.to_string(),
                Err(e) => e.to_string(),
            };
            // the next request tries again
            log::error(&format!("game.wasm compression failed: {why}"));
            let mut cur = cell.lock();
            if cur.as_ref().is_some_and(|e| e.etag == etag) {
                *cur = None;
            }
            None
        });
        async move { task.await.ok().flatten() }.boxed().shared()
    }

    /// /game.wasm.  ?v=<hash>: the module /game.json named.  This one: every cache may keep it for good (the
    /// compressed body is made from the bytes hashed).  Another (a new build since): 409, and the page asks
    /// /game.json again; a copy of this module is never kept under another's address.
    pub async fn send_wasm(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, u: &Url) -> Res {
        let v = u.param("v");
        let c = self.compressed_wasm().await;
        if let (Some(v), Some(c)) = (&v, &c)
            && *v != c.hash
        {
            return self.plain(q, s, 409, "The game module changed: ask /game.json again", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        // 65 MB of code compresses to ~7 MB: other PCs start much sooner
        let range = q.headers.get("range").is_some_and(|r| !r.is_empty());
        if let Some(c) = c.filter(|_| !range && has_word(q.headers.get("accept-encoding").unwrap_or(""), "br")) {
            let cache = if v.as_deref() == Some(c.hash.as_str()) { Cache::Immutable } else { Cache::Revalidate };
            let mut h = self.headers(q, cache, true);
            h.set("content-type", type_of(".wasm").unwrap_or("application/wasm"));
            h.set("etag", c.etag.clone());
            h.set("vary", "accept-encoding");
            if etag_matches(q.headers.get("if-none-match"), &c.etag) {
                s.head(304, h.0);
                return finish(s).await;
            }
            h.set("content-encoding", "br");
            h.set("content-length", c.body.len().to_string());
            s.head(200, h.0);
            if q.method == "HEAD" {
                return finish(s).await;
            }
            return send_shared(s, &c.body).await;
        }
        // as it is (a client without br, a byte range): read from the disk again, so revalidated, never kept for good
        let opts = files::FileOpts { cache: Cache::Revalidate, extra: vec![("vary", "accept-encoding")], ..Default::default() };
        self.send_file(q, s, &paths::dirname(&self.o.wasm), Some(self.o.wasm.clone()), opts).await
    }

    /// /game.json: what was built, and which module this server sends now (module: its hash, for /game.wasm?v=)
    pub async fn send_game_json(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        let dir = paths::dirname(&self.o.game_json);
        let f = self.locate(&dir, Some(self.o.game_json.clone())).await;
        let c = match &f {
            Some(_) => self.compressed_wasm().await,
            None => None,
        };
        let mut info = None;
        if let (Some(c), Some(f)) = (&c, &f)
            && let Ok(b) = tokio::fs::read(&f.real).await
            && let Ok(Value::Object(m)) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&b))
        {
            info = Some((m, c.hash.clone()));
        }
        let Some((mut m, hash)) = info else {
            return self.send_file(q, s, &dir, None, files::FileOpts { found: f, ..Default::default() }).await;
        };
        m.insert("module".into(), Value::String(hash));
        let body = nfsu2_util::json::stringify(&js_numbers(Value::Object(m)));
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", type_of(".json").unwrap_or("application/json"));
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }
}

/// every number as JSON.parse reads it: a double (an integer past 2^53 is rounded as JS rounds it)
fn js_numbers(v: Value) -> Value {
    match v {
        Value::Number(n) => nfsu2_util::json::num(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)),
        Value::Array(a) => Value::Array(a.into_iter().map(js_numbers).collect()),
        Value::Object(m) => Value::Object(m.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, js_numbers(v))).collect()),
        v => v,
    }
}

/// A large shared buffer (the brotli module, ~7 MB) to one client in 64 KB slices with backpressure: handing the
/// whole buffer to the connection at once would have it encrypted into that connection's own memory on TLS, ~6 MB for
/// each client that asks and never reads (the phase-3 secfix review measured +400 MB for 64 such connections).
pub async fn send_shared(s: &mut Response, body: &Bytes) -> Res {
    for slice in body.chunks(64 << 10) {
        send(s, slice).await?;
    }
    finish(s).await
}

    }

//! `nfsu2-server ctl [--state <dir>] <command> [words...]`: an operator's command to the server that runs with that
//! state folder, through its control socket (app/control.rs: the commands).  The folder: --state, else NFSU2_STATE,
//! else the server's own default (out/web/server in the repository).  The words after the command are taken as
//! they come, so a message needs no quotes: `ctl kick Bob Stop ramming people`.  Exit code 0, or 1 when the server
//! said no (or is not there), 2 for no command.

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::os::unix::net::UnixStream;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::app::control::{SOCKET, USAGE, read_answer};
use crate::paths;

pub fn run(argv: &[String], env: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>, repo: &str, cwd: &str) -> i32 {
    let (state, words) = match argv {
        [flag, dir, rest @ ..] if flag == "--state" => (dir.clone(), rest),
        _ => (env("NFSU2_STATE").filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or_else(|| paths::join(repo, "out/web/server")), argv),
    };
    if words.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("usage: nfsu2-server ctl [--state <dir>] <command> [words...]\n{USAGE}");
        return 2;
    }
    let path = paths::join(&paths::resolve(cwd, &state), SOCKET);
    let ask = || -> std::io::Result<String> {
        let mut s = UnixStream::connect(&path)?;
        s.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(15)))?;
        let mut line = serde_json::to_string(words).map_err(std::io::Error::other)?;
        line.push('\n');
        s.write_all(line.as_bytes())?;
        let mut answer = String::new();
        s.read_to_string(&mut answer)?;
        Ok(answer)
    };
    match ask().map(|a| read_answer(&a)) {
        Ok(Some((true, text))) => {
            println!("{text}");
            0
        }
        Ok(Some((false, text))) => {
            eprintln!("{text}");
            1
        }
        Ok(None) => {
            eprintln!("{path}: no answer from the server");
            1
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{path}: {e} (is the server running, with this state folder?)");
            1
        }
    }
}

//! NFSU2 web: the server, in Rust.  It replaced the Node server, with the same options, environment, console lines,
//! files and answers.  What it serves, to Chrome on this machine, on the LAN, or (on a VPS) over the internet:
//!
//!   /                  the web app (web/dist)
//!   /game.wasm         the game module (out/web/nfsu2.wasm), brotli on the wire
//!   /game.json         what was built (size, memory layout, revision)
//!   /data/<path>       the NFSU2 install folder, read-only, with byte ranges: only what the game reads
//!                      (GAME_ENTRIES), never the rest of the folder (an installer's log, saves, mod settings)
//!   /data-manifest     those files: path, size, mtime
//!   /data-blocks/<path>?b=<first>&n=<count>
//!                      a run of 1 MiB blocks of one of them, compressed (zstd, br or gzip, whichever the client takes)
//!   /lan               WebSocket: the virtual LAN switch for multiplayer (nfsu2-lan), with the game's Online mode on
//!                      its 10.77.0.1 (nfsu2-online; --online off: none, the game then cannot connect) and free
//!                      roam's hub on 10.77.0.253 (nfsu2-roam: each player's peers are the players nearest to it;
//!                      --roam-hub off: none, players find each other by broadcast)
//!   /players           how many play on this server now: { players, online, roam, full, queue, roamBusy }, three
//!                      counts, whether a newcomer waits in line, how many do and whether free roam is busy, nothing
//!                      else (never cached);
//!                      ?room=<hash> adds room, how many of roam are in that free-roam room;
//!                      ?crews=<hash>,<hash>,... (at most 4) adds crews, how many of roam are in each of those crews
//!   (and for the operator, nothing on the network: control.sock in the state folder, which `nfsu2-server ctl` talks
//!   to: who is on, kick, ban, unban; src/ctl.rs, app/control.rs)
//!   test aids, only with --dev: the test pages (/test/) and source maps from web/dist-dev (web/build.mjs writes them
//!   there, never into web/dist), the repo's test scripts (/tests/), PUT /artifacts/<name>.png (with --artifacts)
//!
//! Its own names (the Host a request may carry, and the Origin of a /lan page): localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1],
//! always; with --tls-cert, the names in that certificate; the names given with --host (required with
//! --behind-proxy: the proxy forwards the player's Host, and this server cannot know the public name).  Anything
//! else gets 421.  HTTPS (Chrome allows WebGPU and SharedArrayBuffer only on secure origins; http://localhost is one)
//! comes from --tls-cert/--tls-key (a certificate from Let's Encrypt, or a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate; read
//! again when the file changes or on SIGHUP), or a reverse proxy or tunnel on this machine (Caddy, nginx,
//! cloudflared; --behind-proxy: plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:<http-port> only), or not at all (only this machine can
//! play, over http://localhost:<http-port>); plus plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:<http-port> for this machine (0 = none).
//!
//! The work runs on many cores: a tokio runtime with half the cores as workers, 2 to 8 (NFSU2_THREADS), the
//! compression of the game data on a pool of its own (half the cores), the Online host and the free-roam hub on a
//! thread each.  The repository the defaults are in (web/dist, out/web/nfsu2.wasm, out/web/server): NFSU2_REPO, else
//! the checkout whose out/web/server-rs the binary is in, else the one it was built from.

use mimalloc::MiMalloc;

#[global_allocator]
static GLOBAL: MiMalloc = MiMalloc;

mod app;
mod ctl;
mod options;
mod paths;

/// the message on stderr, then exit code 1
pub fn die(msg: &str) -> ! {
    nfsu2_util::log::error(msg);
    std::process::exit(1)
}

/// the repository the defaults are in: NFSU2_REPO, else the checkout this binary sits in, else the one it was built
/// from
fn repo(cwd: &str) -> String {
    match std::env::var_os("NFSU2_REPO") {
        Some(r) if !r.is_empty() => paths::resolve(cwd, &r.to_string_lossy()),
        _ => std::env::current_exe()
            .ok()
            .and_then(|e| checkout_of(&e))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| paths::normalize_abs(&format!("{}/../..", env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")))),
    }
}

/// <repo> for <repo>/out/web/server-rs/<binary>, where web/server-rs/build.sh puts it, also as a copy of a build of
/// the same sources made in another checkout (its cache)
fn checkout_of(exe: &std::path::Path) -> Option<String> {
    let dir = exe.parent()?;
    if !dir.ends_with("out/web/server-rs") {
        return None;
    }
    Some(dir.parent()?.parent()?.parent()?.to_str()?.to_owned())
}

fn main() {
    let argv: Vec<String> = std::env::args_os().skip(1).map(|a| a.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
    let cwd = std::env::current_dir().map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_else(|_| "/".into());
    let env = |k: &str| std::env::var_os(k).map(|v| v.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    // an operator's command to the running server (src/ctl.rs), not a server
    if argv.first().is_some_and(|a| a == "ctl") {
        std::process::exit(ctl::run(&argv[1..], &env, &repo(&cwd), &cwd));
    }
    let o = options::parse(&argv, &env, &repo(&cwd), &cwd, &options::RealFs).unwrap_or_else(|m| die(&m));
    let cores = std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get());
    // half the cores, 2 to 8: more workers do the same work for more CPU (parking and waking, stealing from each
    // other: 2000 players in free roam took 2.9 cores on 4 workers, 3.8 on 8, 4.3 on 12, at the same latency up to
    // 8), and the cores left over are the tunnel's in front (cloudflared pays for each message too)
    let env_threads = std::env::var("NFSU2_THREADS").ok().and_then(|v| v.trim().parse::<usize>().ok()).filter(|&n| n >= 1);
    let threads = env_threads.unwrap_or((cores / 2).clamp(2, 8));
    let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
        .worker_threads(threads)
        .thread_name("nfsu2-worker")
        .enable_all()
        .build()
        .unwrap_or_else(|e| die(&format!("the runtime: {e}")));
    rt.block_on(app::run(o, cores));
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::checkout_of;
    use std::path::Path;

    #[test]
    fn checkout_of_the_binary() {
        assert_eq!(checkout_of(Path::new("/home/a/wt/x/out/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server")).as_deref(), Some("/home/a/wt/x"));
        assert_eq!(checkout_of(Path::new("/home/a/wt/x/out/web/server-rs/target/release/nfsu2-server")), None);
        assert_eq!(checkout_of(Path::new("/nfsu2-server")), None);
        assert_eq!(checkout_of(Path::new("/x/myout/web/server-rs/nfsu2-server")), None);
    }
}
