pub const SYN: u8 = 1;
pub const SYNACK: u8 = 2;
pub const RST: u8 = 3;
pub const DATA: u8 = 4;
pub const FIN: u8 = 5;

pub async fn sleep(ms: u64) {
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(ms)).await;
}

/// "10.77.0.5" as a number
pub fn ip(s: &str) -> u32 {
    s.split('.').fold(0u32, |a, b| (a << 8) | b.parse::<u32>().unwrap())
}

pub fn be16(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> u16 {
    u16::from_be_bytes([b[at], b[at + 1]])
}

pub fn be32(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_be_bytes([b[at], b[at + 1], b[at + 2], b[at + 3]])
}

pub fn le32(b: &[u8], at: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes([b[at], b[at + 1], b[at + 2], b[at + 3]])
}

/// a port for a server process to listen on (it binds it itself): one nobody listens on now, outside the kernel's
/// range for outgoing connections (/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range), so that no client socket of the tests
/// running beside takes it before the server does, as one of `bind(0)`'s ports can be.
///  - "Nobody listens" is asked by connecting, not by listening on it a moment: on macOS a socket is made without
///    close-on-exec and gets it a moment later, and a server another test thread starts in that moment keeps a
///    listening socket on the port for as long as it runs (seen with lsof: 2 to 5 servers of other tests holding one;
///    the server meant for the port then dies with "port N is in use").
///  - And one no other test process on this machine has picked: another cargo test at the same time (another
///    worktree) walks the same ports, and both could find one free.  A picked port's lock is a file of its own in the
///    temp folder, locked for as long as this process lives (the kernel lets go of it when the process ends).
pub fn free_port() -> u16 {
    static NEXT: AtomicU16 = AtomicU16::new(0);
    static PICKED: Mutex<Vec<std::fs::File>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
    let locks = std::env::temp_dir().join("nfsu2-test-ports");
    let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&locks);
    let range = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range").unwrap_or_default();
    let mut r = range.split_whitespace().filter_map(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok());
    let (lo, hi) = (r.next().unwrap_or(32768), r.next().unwrap_or(60999));
    // 4000 ports below the range, or above it when there is no room below
    let (from, n) = if lo >= 5024 { (lo - 4000, 4000) } else { (hi + 1, (65535 - hi).min(4000)) };
    let start = std::process::id() % n;
    for _ in 0..n {
        let p = (from + (start + NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) as u32) % n) as u16;
        // (no temp folder to lock in: the port alone, as before)
        let lock = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).write(true).open(locks.join(p.to_string())).ok();
        if lock.as_ref().is_some_and(|f| f.try_lock().is_err()) {
            continue;
        }
        let to = std::net::SocketAddr::from(([127, 0, 0, 1], p));
        let refused = std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(&to, Duration::from_secs(1));
        if refused.is_err_and(|e| e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionRefused) {
            PICKED.lock().unwrap().extend(lock);
            return p;
        }
    }
    panic!("no free port");
}

/// polls f every 10 ms until it says yes (false after `ms`)
pub async fn wait_for(ms: u64, mut f: impl FnMut() -> bool) -> bool {
    let end = tokio::time::Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(ms);
    loop {
        if f() {
            return true;
        }
        if tokio::time::Instant::now() >= end {
            return false;
        }
        sleep(10).await;
    }
}

// ---- the switch -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The Online host as run.rs makes it, in memory only; the lines it logs, kept
pub fn online_host() -> (Arc<OnlineHost>, Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>) {
    let lines = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
    let l2 = lines.clone();
    let h = OnlineHost::spawn(OnlineOptions {
        state_dir: None,
        log: Arc::new(move |line: &str, _key: Option<&str>| l2.lock().unwrap().push(line.to_string())),
        tap: None,
        claims: None,
        deny: None,
    });
    (h, lines)
}

/// The free-roam hub as run.rs makes it (its options the test's)
pub fn roam_hub(o: RoamOptions) -> Arc<RoamHub> {
    RoamHub::spawn(o, Arc::new(|_line: &str| {}))
}

pub struct Switch {
    pub lan: Arc<LanSwitch>,
    pub port: u16,
    accept: JoinHandle<()>,
}

/// a switch with the real hosts, given the switch's way to the browsers as run.rs gives it to them
pub async fn start(o: LanOptions, online: Option<Arc<OnlineHost>>, roam: Option<Arc<RoamHub>>) -> Switch {
    let sw = start_with(o, online.clone().map(|h| h as Arc<dyn Host>), roam.clone().map(|h| h as Arc<dyn Host>)).await;
    if let Some(h) = &online {
        h.attach_switch(sw.lan.switch_send());
    }
    if let Some(h) = &roam {
        h.attach_switch(sw.lan.switch_send());
    }
    sw
}

/// a switch with any hosts (the caller gives them `lan.switch_send()`), on an ephemeral port: /lan?g=<id>&s=<id>
/// stand for the group and site ids the server derives from a client's address; SO_SNDBUF on the switch's sockets
/// as the server sets it (`send_buffer_os`)
pub async fn start_with(o: LanOptions, online: Option<Arc<dyn Host>>, roam: Option<Arc<dyn Host>>) -> Switch {
    let sndbuf = o.send_buffer_os;
    let lan = LanSwitch::new(o, "", online, roam, None, None);
    let sock = TcpSocket::new_v4().unwrap();
    if sndbuf > 0 {
        sock.set_send_buffer_size(sndbuf as u32).unwrap();
    }
    sock.bind("127.0.0.1:0".parse().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let listener = sock.listen(1024).unwrap();
    let port = listener.local_addr().unwrap().port();
    let l2 = lan.clone();
    let accept = tokio::spawn(async move {
        while let Ok((s, _)) = listener.accept().await {
            let _ = s.set_nodelay(true);
            tokio::spawn(serve(l2.clone(), s));
        }
    });
    Switch { lan, port, accept }
}

/// the upgrade to /lan, answered as the server answers it (src/app/lan.rs), and the connection attached to the switch
async fn serve(lan: Arc<LanSwitch>, mut s: TcpStream) {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    let mut tmp = [0u8; 4096];
    let end = loop {
        if let Some(i) = buf.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") {
            break i + 4;
        }
        if buf.len() > 16 << 10 {
            return;
        }
        match s.read(&mut tmp).await {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => return,
            Ok(n) => buf.extend_from_slice(&tmp[..n]),
        }
    };
    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..end]).to_string();
    let mut lines = head.split("\r\n");
    let target = lines.next().and_then(|l| l.split(' ').nth(1)).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let key = lines
        .filter_map(|l| l.split_once(':'))
        .find(|(k, _)| k.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("sec-websocket-key"))
        .map(|(_, v)| v.trim().to_string());
    let (path, query) = target.split_once('?').unwrap_or((&target, ""));
    let Some(key) = key.filter(|_| path == "/lan") else { return };
    if s.write_all(&nfsu2_ws::handshake_response(&key, None)).await.is_err() {
        return;
    }
    let (mut resume, mut group, mut site) = (false, None, None);
    for kv in query.split('&').filter(|kv| !kv.is_empty()) {
        let (k, v) = kv.split_once('=').unwrap_or((kv, ""));
        match k {
            "resume" => resume = true,
            "g" if group.is_none() => group = Some(v.to_string()),
            "s" if site.is_none() => site = Some(v.to_string()),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let pre = Bytes::copy_from_slice(&buf[end..]);
    let (r, w) = s.into_split();
    // the hello's "claim" names the keyphrase's owner, as the server's lan.rs has it
    let on_claim: nfsu2_lan::OnClaim = Box::new(nfsu2_claims::owner_of_token);
    lan.attach(r, w, pre, AttachOpts { resume, group, site, on_claim: Some(on_claim), ..AttachOpts::default() });
}

impl Switch {
    /// the switch stops (its hosts too), its connections end
    pub async fn close(self) {
        self.lan.stop();
        self.lan.terminate_all();
        self.accept.abort();
        sleep(20).await;
    }

    pub async fn info(&self) -> Value {
        self.lan.info().await
    }

    /// the peer on the switch at `vip`, as the tests see it
    pub fn peer(&self, vip: u32) -> Option<nfsu2_lan::PeerView> {
        self.lan.peers_view().into_iter().find(|p| p.vip == vip)
    }

    /// bytes queued to `vip` that the kernel has not taken (Node's `ws.bufferedAmount`)
    pub fn buffered(&self, vip: u32) -> usize {
        self.peer(vip).map_or(0, |p| p.buffered)
    }
}

// ---- frames ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// a frame of the virtual host's TCP (kind 4), UDP (3) or ICMP (5), as nfsu2-online's `vhost::lan_frame` makes one
pub fn lan_frame(kind: u8, src: u32, dst: u32, sport: u16, dport: u16, op: u8, cid: u32, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut f = vec![0u8; 24 + data.len()];
    f[0] = kind;
    f[4..8].copy_from_slice(&src.to_be_bytes());
    f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&dst.to_be_bytes());
    f[12..14].copy_from_slice(&sport.to_be_bytes());
    f[14..16].copy_from_slice(&dport.to_be_bytes());
    f[16] = op;
    f[17] = 64;
    f[20..24].copy_from_slice(&cid.to_le_bytes());
    f[24..].copy_from_slice(data);
    f
}

/// a datagram with ports to `dst` (kind 1 free roam, 3-5 LAN play), the source left for the switch to write
pub fn udp(dst: u32, sport: u16, dport: u16, kind: u8, data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut f = vec![0u8; 16 + data.len()];
    f[0] = kind;
    f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&dst.to_be_bytes());
    f[12..14].copy_from_slice(&sport.to_be_bytes());
    f[14..16].copy_from_slice(&dport.to_be_bytes());
    f[16..].copy_from_slice(data);
    f
}

/// a bundle (the switch's frame kind 32) of frames, each to its own destination (entries of n = 0)
pub fn bundle_of(frames: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = vec![32, 0, 0, 0];
    for f in frames {
        b.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0]);
        b.extend_from_slice(&(f.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
        b.extend_from_slice(f);
    }
    b
}

/// this process's resident memory, in bytes (/proc/self/statm)
pub fn rss() -> u64 {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/statm").unwrap_or_default();
    s.split_whitespace().nth(1).and_then(|v| v.parse::<u64>().ok()).unwrap_or(0) * 4096
}

/// CRC-32 (IEEE, zlib's crc32), for roam_core's datagrams
pub fn crc32(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {
    let mut c = !0u32;
    for &x in b {
        c ^= x as u32;
        for _ in 0..8 {
            c = if c & 1 != 0 { (c >> 1) ^ 0xEDB8_8320 } else { c >> 1 };
        }
    }
    !c
}

/// a player's datagram of this kind as roam_core.c lays it out: its header, the payload, its CRC
pub fn dgram(kind: u8, sender: u32, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let len = 16 + payload.len() + 4;
    let mut b = vec![0u8; len];
    b[..4].copy_from_slice(b"N2FR");
    b[4] = 1;
    b[5] = kind;
    b[6..8].copy_from_slice(&(len as u16).to_le_bytes());
    b[8..12].copy_from_slice(&sender.to_le_bytes());
    b[12..14].copy_from_slice(&7u16.to_le_bytes());
    b[16..16 + payload.len()].copy_from_slice(payload);
    let crc = crc32(&b[..len - 4]);
    b[len - 4..].copy_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
    b
}

/// a HELLO: room 0, in free roam (status 2), named "p", core version 1
pub fn roam_hello(sender: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    roam_hello_named(sender, b"p")
}

/// a free-roam HELLO under `name` (core version 1, in free roam, room 0)
pub fn roam_hello_named(sender: u32, name: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    roam_hello_named_in(sender, name, 0)
}

/// a free-roam HELLO under `name` in `room` (core version 1, in free roam)
pub fn roam_hello_named_in(sender: u32, name: &[u8], room: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut p = vec![0u8; 13 + name.len() + 1];
    p[0..2].copy_from_slice(&1u16.to_le_bytes());
    p[2] = 1;
    p[3] = 2;
    p[4..6].copy_from_slice(&47210u16.to_le_bytes());
    p[6..8].copy_from_slice(&3u16.to_le_bytes());
    p[8..12].copy_from_slice(&room.to_le_bytes());
    p[12] = name.len() as u8;
    p[13..13 + name.len()].copy_from_slice(name);
    dgram(1, sender, &p)
}

/// a SNAP: the sender's car at `pos`
pub fn roam_snap(sender: u32, pos: [f32; 3]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut p = vec![0u8; 6 + 52];
    p[0] = 2;
    p[4] = 1;
    p[10..14].copy_from_slice(&pos[0].to_le_bytes());
    p[14..18].copy_from_slice(&pos[1].to_le_bytes());
    p[18..22].copy_from_slice(&pos[2].to_le_bytes());
    // q.w (a valid quaternion)
    p[6 + 34..6 + 36].copy_from_slice(&32767i16.to_le_bytes());
    dgram(3, sender, &p)
}

/// a datagram to the hub, from port 47210 to 47210
pub fn to_hub(d: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    udp(ROAM_HUB_VIP, 47210, 47210, 1, d)
}

// ---- the lobby's messages (as nfsu2-online's aries writes them) -----------------------------------------------

/// a field's value as the lobby writes it (nfsu2-online `aries::encode_value`): every byte below 0x20, 0x7F and
/// = " : % ^ as %xx, in quotes when it has a space
pub fn encode_value(v: &str) -> String {
    let mut s = String::new();
    for c in v.bytes() {
        if c < 0x20 || matches!(c, 0x3d | 0x22 | 0x3a | 0x25 | 0x5e | 0x7f) {
            s.push_str(&format!("%{c:02x}"));
        } else {
            s.push(c as char);
        }
    }
    if v.as_bytes().contains(&0x20) { format!("\"{s}\"") } else { s }
}

/// a lobby message with no code (nfsu2-online `aries::encode_frame`): kind, code, length, the fields, a NUL
pub fn encode_frame(kind: &str, fields: &[(&str, String)]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut body = String::new();
    for (k, v) in fields {
        body.push_str(&format!("{k}={}\n", encode_value(v)));
    }
    let mut f = vec![0u8; 12];
    f[..kind.len()].copy_from_slice(kind.as_bytes());
    f.extend_from_slice(body.as_bytes());
    f.push(0);
    let n = f.len() as u32;
    f[8..12].copy_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
    f
}

/// one lobby message: its kind, its code (an error tag, "" for success) and its fields (nfsu2-online `aries::FieldMap`)
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Msg {
    pub kind: String,
    pub code: String,
    pub fields: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

impl Msg {
    pub fn get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&str> {
        self.fields.iter().find(|(x, _)| x == k).map(|(_, v)| v.as_str())
    }
}

fn tag_text(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    b.iter().filter(|&&c| c != 0).map(|&c| c as char).collect()
}

fn unescape(s: &[u8]) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < s.len() {
        // `/%([0-9a-fA-F]{2})/g`
        if s[i] == b'%' && i + 2 < s.len() && s[i + 1].is_ascii_hexdigit() && s[i + 2].is_ascii_hexdigit() {
            let hex = |c: u8| (c as char).to_digit(16).unwrap_or(0) as u8;
            out.push((hex(s[i + 1]) << 4 | hex(s[i + 2])) as char);
            i += 3;
            continue;
        }
        out.push(s[i] as char);
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

/// a message body's fields, none of them kept back as secret (nfsu2-online `aries::parse_fields`)
pub fn parse_fields(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let end = body.iter().position(|&c| c == 0).unwrap_or(body.len());
    let b = &body[..end];
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < b.len() {
        while i < b.len() && b[i] <= 0x20 {
            i += 1;
        }
        if i >= b.len() {
            break;
        }
        let mut k = i;
        while k < b.len() && b[k] > 0x20 && b[k] != b'=' {
            k += 1;
        }
        let key = tag_text(&b[i..k]).to_uppercase();
        if k >= b.len() || b[k] != b'=' {
            i = k;
            continue;
        }
        let j = k + 1;
        let raw;
        if j < b.len() && b[j] == b'"' {
            let mut q = j + 1;
            while q < b.len() && b[q] != b'"' {
                q += 1;
            }
            raw = &b[j + 1..q];
            i = q + 1;
        } else {
            let mut q = j;
            while q < b.len() && b[q] > 0x20 {
                q += 1;
            }
            raw = &b[j..q];
            i = q;
        }
        if !out.iter().any(|(x, _): &(String, String)| *x == key) {
            out.push((key, unescape(raw)));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// the messages in a byte stream, each at most 64 KiB (nfsu2-online `aries::FrameReader`)
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct AriesReader {
    buf: Vec<u8>,
    bad: bool,
}

impl AriesReader {
    pub fn push(&mut self, chunk: &[u8]) -> Vec<Msg> {
        if self.bad {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        self.buf.extend_from_slice(chunk);
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        while self.buf.len() >= 12 {
            let n = be32(&self.buf, 8) as usize;
            if !(12..=1 << 16).contains(&n) {
                self.bad = true;
                self.buf.clear();
                break;
            }
            if self.buf.len() < n {
                break;
            }
            let m: Vec<u8> = self.buf.drain(..n).collect();
            out.push(Msg { kind: tag_text(&m[..4]), code: tag_text(&m[4..8]), fields: parse_fields(&m[12..]) });
        }
        out
    }
}

// ---- a fake browser -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A TCP connection of the browser's game to the virtual host (runtime/web/net_lan.c as the tests speak it)
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Tcp {
    pub open: bool,
    pub reset: bool,
    pub fin: bool,
    reader: AriesReader,
    pub msgs: Vec<Msg>,
}

impl Tcp {
    pub fn last(&self, kind: &str) -> Option<&Msg> {
        self.msgs.iter().rev().find(|m| m.kind == kind)
    }
    pub fn count(&self, kind: &str) -> usize {
        self.msgs.iter().filter(|m| m.kind == kind).count()
    }
}

/// What a fake browser got.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Got {
    /// binary messages, as they came
    pub frames: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    /// control messages
    pub ctl: Vec<Value>,
    /// its game's TCP connections to the virtual host, by its own port
    pub tcp: HashMap<u16, Tcp>,
    /// its close: the code and reason of the switch's close frame (1005 without a code, 1006 without a frame)
    pub closed: Option<(u16, String)>,
    /// binary messages counted, not kept (a measurement's clients: their memory is the test process's too)
    pub drop_frames: bool,
    pub frame_count: usize,
    /// of `frames`, the indexes of those that came inside a bundle (kind 32)
    pub bundled: Vec<usize>,
    /// the last echo reply's sequence number
    pub echoed: u32,
    echo_seq: u32,
}

impl Got {
    /// the peer list as the page keeps it: the last whole list, with the changes after it (gone first, then the ones
    /// that joined or got their name)
    pub fn peers(&self) -> Option<Vec<Value>> {
        let at = self.ctl.iter().rposition(|m| m["t"] == "peers")?;
        let mut list: Vec<Value> = self.ctl[at]["peers"].as_array().cloned()?;
        for d in self.ctl[at + 1..].iter().filter(|m| m["t"] == "delta") {
            let gone: Vec<&Value> = d["gone"].as_array().map(|g| g.iter().collect()).unwrap_or_default();
            list.retain(|p| !gone.contains(&&p["vip"]));
            for p in d["peers"].as_array().into_iter().flatten() {
                match list.iter_mut().find(|q| q["vip"] == p["vip"]) {
                    Some(q) => *q = p.clone(),
                    None => list.push(p.clone()),
                }
            }
        }
        Some(list)
    }
    fn frame(&mut self, f: Vec<u8>) {
        // a bundle from the switch (kind 32, entries of n = 0: the frame with its own destination): its frames, as the
        // page takes them (the hub's lists come in them since they stopped being messages of their own)
        if f.first() == Some(&32) {
            let mut i = 4;
            while i + 4 <= f.len() {
                let n = u16::from_be_bytes([f[i + 2], f[i + 3]]) as usize;
                let at = i + 4 + 4 * f[i] as usize;
                if at + n > f.len() {
                    break;
                }
                self.bundled.push(self.frames.len());
                self.frame(f[at..at + n].to_vec());
                i = at + n;
            }
            return;
        }
        self.frame_count += 1;
        // the virtual host's echo replies (ICMP type 0): their sequence numbers, the barrier of `echo()`
        if f.len() >= 32 && f[0] == 5 && f[24] == 0 && be32(&f, 4) == VHOST_VIP {
            self.echoed = u16::from_be_bytes([f[30], f[31]]) as u32;
        }
        if self.drop_frames {
            return;
        }
        if f.len() >= 24
            && f[0] == 4
            && let Some(c) = self.tcp.get_mut(&be16(&f, 14))
        {
            match f[16] {
                SYNACK => c.open = true,
                RST => c.reset = true,
                FIN => c.fin = true,
                DATA => {
                    let m = c.reader.push(&f[24..]);
                    c.msgs.extend(m);
                }
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        self.frames.push(f);
    }
}

enum Cmd {
    Send(Message),
    Flush(oneshot::Sender<()>),
}

static NEXT_PORT: AtomicU16 = AtomicU16::new(50000);
static NEXT_CID: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(1);

/// A connection of the browser's game to the virtual host
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Conn {
    pub port: u16,
    pub cid: u32,
    pub dport: u16,
}

/// A fake browser: collects control messages and frames, follows its game's TCP connections to the virtual host;
/// its reading can be paused (the kernel's buffers fill, then the switch's queue for it grows: a receiver far
/// behind).
pub struct Browser {
    pub vip: u32,
    /// its welcome's token (what gives its address back to it)
    pub token: String,
    st: Arc<Mutex<Got>>,
    ver: watch::Receiver<u64>,
    tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Cmd>,
    paused: watch::Sender<bool>,
    tasks: Vec<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

impl Browser {
    /// ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/lan<query>, with a receive buffer of its own size (SO_RCVBUF) when given; waits for
    /// the welcome
    pub async fn open(port: u16, query: &str, rcvbuf: Option<u32>) -> Browser {
        Browser::open_at(&format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"), port, query, rcvbuf).await
    }

    /// the same with another Host (the binary answers only for its own names)
    pub async fn open_at(host: &str, port: u16, query: &str, rcvbuf: Option<u32>) -> Browser {
        Browser::open_full(host, port, query, rcvbuf, None).await
    }

    /// a page that reconnects (/lan?resume): its hello with its old address and token first, then the welcome
    pub async fn resume(host: &str, port: u16, name: &str, vip: u32, token: &str) -> Browser {
        let hello = serde_json::json!({ "t": "hello", "name": name, "vip": nfsu2_util::vip_str(vip), "token": token });
        Browser::open_full(host, port, "?resume", None, Some(hello.to_string())).await
    }

    /// `first`: a text message sent before the welcome is waited for
    pub async fn open_full(host: &str, port: u16, query: &str, rcvbuf: Option<u32>, first: Option<String>) -> Browser {
        Browser::open_from(host, port, query, rcvbuf, first, None).await
    }

    /// `xff`: the client's address as a proxy on this machine names it (X-Forwarded-For): a client of its own for the
    /// binary's limits per address
    pub async fn open_from(host: &str, port: u16, query: &str, rcvbuf: Option<u32>, first: Option<String>, xff: Option<&str>) -> Browser {
        use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::client::IntoClientRequest;
        let sock = TcpSocket::new_v4().unwrap();
        if let Some(n) = rcvbuf {
            sock.set_recv_buffer_size(n).unwrap();
        }
        let s = sock.connect(([127, 0, 0, 1], port).into()).await.expect("connect");
        let _ = s.set_nodelay(true);
        let mut q = format!("ws://{host}/lan{query}").into_client_request().unwrap();
        if let Some(a) = xff {
            q.headers_mut().insert("x-forwarded-for", a.parse().unwrap());
        }
        let (ws, _) = tokio_tungstenite::client_async(q, s).await.expect("the handshake");
        let (mut sink, mut stream) = ws.split();
        let st = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Got::default()));
        let (vtx, ver) = watch::channel(0u64);
        let (tx, mut rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Cmd>();
        let (paused, mut paused_rx) = watch::channel(false);
        let writer = tokio::spawn(async move {
            while let Some(c) = rx.recv().await {
                match c {
                    Cmd::Send(m) => {
                        if sink.send(m).await.is_err() {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    Cmd::Flush(done) => {
                        let _ = done.send(());
                    }
                }
            }
        });
        let writer_end = writer.abort_handle();
        let s2 = st.clone();
        let reader = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut code = None;
            loop {
                // paused: the socket is not read
                while *paused_rx.borrow_and_update() {
                    if paused_rx.changed().await.is_err() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                let Some(Ok(m)) = stream.next().await else { break };
                {
                    let mut g = s2.lock().unwrap();
                    match m {
                        Message::Binary(b) => g.frame(b.to_vec()),
                        Message::Text(t) => g.ctl.push(serde_json::from_str(t.as_str()).expect("JSON from the switch")),
                        Message::Close(f) => {
                            code = Some(f.map(|f| (u16::from(f.code), f.reason.to_string())).unwrap_or((1005, String::new())))
                        }
                        _ => {}
                    }
                }
                vtx.send_modify(|v| *v += 1);
            }
            writer_end.abort();
            s2.lock().unwrap().closed = Some(code.unwrap_or((1006, String::new())));
            vtx.send_modify(|v| *v += 1);
        });
        let mut b = Browser { vip: 0, token: String::new(), st, ver, tx, paused, tasks: vec![reader, writer] };
        if let Some(t) = first {
            b.text(&t);
        }
        let w = b.until_ms(8000, |g| g.ctl.iter().find(|m| m["t"] == "welcome").cloned()).await;
        b.vip = w["vip"].as_u64().expect("the welcome's vip") as u32;
        b.token = w["token"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string();
        b
    }

    /// a connection that may not be admitted: what it got by the time the switch closed it (or 2 s), and how
    pub async fn refused(host: &str, port: u16) -> (Vec<Value>, Option<(u16, String)>) {
        let s = TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.expect("connect");
        let (ws, _) = tokio_tungstenite::client_async(format!("ws://{host}/lan"), s).await.expect("the handshake");
        let (_sink, mut stream) = ws.split();
        let mut ctl = Vec::new();
        let mut closed = None;
        let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), async {
            while let Some(Ok(m)) = stream.next().await {
                match m {
                    Message::Text(t) => ctl.push(serde_json::from_str(t.as_str()).expect("JSON from the switch")),
                    Message::Close(f) => {
                        closed = Some(f.map(|f| (u16::from(f.code), f.reason.to_string())).unwrap_or((1005, String::new())))
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        })
        .await;
        (ctl, closed)
    }

    pub fn got(&self) -> MutexGuard<'_, Got> {
        self.st.lock().unwrap()
    }

    /// waits until f says yes (2 s at most)
    pub async fn until<T>(&self, f: impl FnMut(&Got) -> Option<T>) -> T {
        self.until_ms(2000, f).await
    }

    pub async fn until_ms<T>(&self, ms: u64, mut f: impl FnMut(&Got) -> Option<T>) -> T {
        self.try_until(ms, &mut f).await.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{}: timed out", nfsu2_util::vip_str(self.vip)))
    }

    /// waits until f says yes; None after `ms` (or once the connection closed without it)
    pub async fn try_until<T>(&self, ms: u64, mut f: impl FnMut(&Got) -> Option<T>) -> Option<T> {
        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(ms);
        let mut ver = self.ver.clone();
        loop {
            if let Some(v) = f(&self.got()) {
                return Some(v);
            }
            match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, ver.changed()).await {
                Ok(Ok(())) => {}
                _ => return f(&self.got()),
            }
        }
    }

    /// a hello as the page sends it on the LAN screens (its name, LAN play open)
    pub fn hello(&self, name: &str) {
        self.text(&serde_json::json!({ "t": "hello", "name": name, "lan": 1 }).to_string());
    }

    pub fn text(&self, s: &str) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Send(Message::text(s)));
    }

    pub fn binary(&self, b: Vec<u8>) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Send(Message::binary(b)));
    }

    /// `binary`, for another task
    pub fn sender(&self) -> impl Fn(Vec<u8>) + Send + Sync + 'static {
        let tx = self.tx.clone();
        move |b| {
            let _ = tx.send(Cmd::Send(Message::binary(b)));
        }
    }

    /// what it sent is on the socket (ws's send callback)
    pub async fn flush(&self) {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Flush(tx));
        let _ = rx.await;
    }

    /// stops reading its socket (true) or reads again (false)
    pub fn pause(&self, on: bool) {
        self.paused.send_replace(on);
    }

    pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
        self.got().closed.is_none() && !self.tasks[0].is_finished()
    }

    /// ws `close()`: a close frame without a code, then its 'close'
    pub async fn close(&self) -> (u16, String) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Send(Message::Close(None)));
        self.until_ms(5000, |g| g.closed.clone()).await
    }

    // ---- its game's TCP to the virtual host (10.77.0.1) ----

    /// a connection its game opened over another WebSocket of this browser (a page that reconnected): followed here
    /// from now on
    pub fn adopt(&self, c: Conn) {
        self.got().tcp.insert(c.port, Tcp { open: true, ..Tcp::default() });
    }

    /// a SYN to the virtual host's `dport`, from a port of its own
    pub fn connect_tcp(&self, dport: u16) -> Conn {
        let c = Conn { port: NEXT_PORT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed), cid: NEXT_CID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed), dport };
        self.got().tcp.insert(c.port, Tcp::default());
        self.tcp_out(c, SYN, &[]);
        c
    }

    pub fn tcp_out(&self, c: Conn, op: u8, data: &[u8]) {
        self.binary(lan_frame(4, self.vip, VHOST_VIP, c.port, c.dport, op, c.cid, data));
    }

    /// one lobby message on connection c
    pub fn send_msg(&self, c: Conn, kind: &str, fields: &[(&str, String)]) {
        self.tcp_out(c, DATA, &encode_frame(kind, fields));
    }

    /// what became of connection c so far
    pub fn tcp<T>(&self, c: Conn, f: impl FnOnce(&Tcp) -> T) -> T {
        f(&self.got().tcp[&c.port])
    }

    /// a connection to the virtual host's port `dport`, accepted
    pub async fn open_tcp(&self, dport: u16) -> Conn {
        self.try_open_tcp(dport).await.expect("the virtual host accepted the connection")
    }

    /// the same, None when it was refused (RST) or not answered in 2 s
    pub async fn try_open_tcp(&self, dport: u16) -> Option<Conn> {
        let c = self.connect_tcp(dport);
        let open = self.try_until(2000, |g| (g.tcp[&c.port].open || g.tcp[&c.port].reset).then_some(g.tcp[&c.port].open)).await;
        open.unwrap_or(false).then_some(c)
    }

    /// a lobby session up to a persona
    pub async fn login(&self, name: &str) -> Conn {
        let c = self.try_login(name).await;
        assert!(c.is_some(), "{name} logged in");
        c.unwrap()
    }

    /// the same, None when the lobby did not take it
    pub async fn try_login(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Conn> {
        let c = self.try_open_tcp(nfsu2_online::PORT_LOBBY).await?;
        self.send_msg(c, "auth", &[("NAME", name.into()), ("PASS", "x".into())]);
        self.send_msg(c, "pers", &[("PERS", name.into())]);
        self.try_until(3000, |g| g.tcp[&c.port].last("pers").map(|_| ())).await.map(|_| c)
    }

    /// a barrier: an ICMP echo to the virtual host, and its reply (the host has taken everything this browser sent
    /// before it, and what it answered is here); false when none came in 2 s
    pub async fn echo(&self) -> bool {
        let seq = {
            let mut g = self.got();
            g.echo_seq = g.echo_seq % 65535 + 1;
            g.echo_seq
        };
        let mut icmp = vec![8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1];
        icmp.extend_from_slice(&(seq as u16).to_be_bytes());
        self.binary(lan_frame(5, self.vip, VHOST_VIP, 0, 0, 0, 0, &icmp));
        self.try_until(2000, |g| (g.echoed == seq).then_some(())).await.is_some()
    }

    /// the browser's connection ends at once, no close frame (ws `terminate()`)
    pub fn terminate(&self) {
        for t in &self.tasks {
            t.abort();
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for Browser {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.terminate();
    }
}

//! What a client can send the server's hosts, at random (a fixed seed), through the whole binary: lobby and EA
//! Messenger messages with random fields on real sessions, raw TCP, UDP and ICMP frames to 10.77.0.1, free-roam
//! datagrams to 10.77.0.253 (well formed with random contents, and garbage), and bundles of them, within the
//! switch's budgets.  Nothing of it may panic (the console would show it: the panic hook's lines, "[online] a service
//! failed"), and the server goes on: /players answers, a newcomer logs in, SIGTERM ends it with exit code 0 and
//! readable files.
//!   cargo test --test fuzz        (NFSU2_FUZZ_SEED, NFSU2_FUZZ_FRAMES: another seed, more frames)

mod common;

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use common::*;
use nfsu2_online::{PORT_BUDDY, PORT_HTTP, PORT_LOBBY, PORT_REDIRECTOR, VHOST_VIP};
use nfsu2_roam::ROAM_HUB_VIP;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};

/// xorshift64*: the same frames for the same seed
struct Rng(std::cell::Cell<u64>);

impl Rng {
    fn next(&self) -> u64 {
        let mut x = self.0.get();
        x ^= x >> 12;
        x ^= x << 25;
        x ^= x >> 27;
        self.0.set(x);
        x.wrapping_mul(0x2545_F491_4F6C_DD1D)
    }
    fn below(&self, n: u64) -> u64 {
        self.next() % n.max(1)
    }
    fn chance(&self, pct: u64) -> bool {
        self.below(100) < pct
    }
    fn pick<'a, T>(&self, l: &'a [T]) -> &'a T {
        &l[self.below(l.len() as u64) as usize]
    }
    fn bytes(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        (0..n).map(|_| self.next() as u8).collect()
    }
}

const LOBBY_KINDS: &[&str] = &[
    "addr", "skey", "news", "sele", "~png", "auth", "acct", "lost", "cper", "dper", "pers", "move", "mesg", "auxi", "user", "onln", "gsea",
    "gcre", "gjoi", "gset", "gsta", "gdel", "glea", "rank", "snap", "rept", "zzzz", "@dir", "",
];
const BUDDY_KINDS: &[&str] = &[
    "AUTH", "EPGT", "RGET", "RADD", "RDEL", "RADM", "RRSP", "PADD", "PDEL", "USCH", "PSET", "SEND", "GINV", "GRSP", "GRVK", "DISC", "QQQQ",
];
const KEYS: &[&str] = &[
    "NAME",
    "PERS",
    "PASS",
    "ATTR",
    "AUTH",

    "COUNT",
    "CUSTFLAGS",
    "CUSTMASK",

];

/// a field's value: numbers of every kind, names, escapes, long text, any byte
fn value(r: &Rng, names: &[&str]) -> String {
    match r.below(14) {
        0 => String::new(),
        1 => r.below(10).to_string(),
        2 => (r.next() as i64).to_string(),
        3 => r.pick(&["-1", "0", "1e308", "-0", "NaN", "Infinity", "0x10", "99999999999999999999999", "2147483648", "1.5"]).to_string(),
        4 => r.pick(names).to_string(),
        5 => format!("TRACK={}", r.below(5000)),
        6 => "A".repeat(r.below(3000) as usize),
        7 => r.bytes(r.below(40) as usize).iter().map(|&c| c as char).collect(),
        8 => "%zz%4%%41\"=:^ ".to_string(),
        9 => base64(&r.bytes(r.below(400) as usize)),
        10 => resu(r),
        11 => format!("{}={}", r.pick(KEYS), r.below(100)),
        12 => "\u{e9}\u{ff}\u{7f}".to_string(),
        _ => r.pick(&["Lounge", "Circuit", "Sprint", "Drift", "Drag", "StreetX", "URL", "B", "P", "C", "G"]).to_string(),
    }
}

fn base64(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    const A: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
    let mut s = String::new();
    for c in b.chunks(3) {
        let n = (c[0] as u32) << 16 | (*c.get(1).unwrap_or(&0) as u32) << 8 | *c.get(2).unwrap_or(&0) as u32;
        for i in 0..4 {
            s.push(if i <= c.len() { A[(n >> (18 - 6 * i) & 63) as usize] as char } else { '=' });
        }
    }
    s
}

/// a race report (rank RESU) that is nearly the game's: version 3, random counts, places, types and times
fn resu(r: &Rng) -> String {
    let n = r.below(10) as usize;
    let mut b = vec![0u8; 8 + 55 * n + r.below(3) as usize];
    b[0] = if r.chance(80) { 3 } else { r.next() as u8 };
    b[1] = if r.chance(80) { n as u8 } else { r.next() as u8 };
    b[2] = r.below(9) as u8;
    b[4..6].copy_from_slice(&(r.below(5000) as u16).to_be_bytes());
    b[7] = r.next() as u8;
    for i in 0..n {
        let o = 8 + 55 * i;
        b[o] = r.below(10) as u8;
        b[o + 1] = r.below(10) as u8;
        b[o + 2] = r.next() as u8;
        let t = match r.below(4) {
            0 => f32::NAN,
            1 => -1.0,
            2 => 1e30,
            _ => r.below(600) as f32,
        };
        b[o + 8..o + 12].copy_from_slice(&t.to_be_bytes());
    }
    base64(&b)
}

fn fields(r: &Rng, names: &[&str]) -> Vec<(&'static str, String)> {
    (0..r.below(6)).map(|_| (*r.pick(KEYS), value(r, names))).collect()
}

/// one free-roam datagram: a well-formed header and CRC around a random payload, a HELLO or SNAP with odd values, or
/// garbage
fn roam(r: &Rng) -> Vec<u8> {
    match r.below(5) {
        0 => {
            let mut p = r.bytes(r.below(120) as usize);
            if p.len() >= 2 && r.chance(50) {
                p[0..2].copy_from_slice(&(r.below(4) as u16).to_le_bytes());
            }
            dgram(r.below(12) as u8, r.next() as u32, &p)
        }
        1 => roam_hello(r.below(4) as u32),
        2 => {
            let v = [f32::NAN, f32::INFINITY, -1e9, 1e6, 0.0, 30000.0];
            roam_snap(r.below(4) as u32, [*r.pick(&v), *r.pick(&v), *r.pick(&v)])
        }
        3 => {
            // a HELLO whose name and list of seen players run past its end
            let mut h = roam_hello(r.next() as u32);
            let at = 16 + 12;
            h[at] = r.next() as u8;
            if r.chance(50) {
                h[at + 2] = 255;
            }
            let len = h.len();
            let crc = crc32(&h[..len - 4]);
            h[len - 4..].copy_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
            h
        }
        _ => r.bytes(r.below(80) as usize),
    }
}

/// a frame of any kind to anyone (the hosts most of all)
fn raw_frame(r: &Rng, others: &[u32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let dst = match r.below(6) {
        0 | 1 => VHOST_VIP,
        2 | 3 => ROAM_HUB_VIP,
        4 => 0xFFFF_FFFF,
        _ => *r.pick(others),
    };
    let kind = *r.pick(&[1u8, 1, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 0, 2, 6, 31, 33, 255]);
    let dport = *r.pick(&[PORT_LOBBY, PORT_BUDDY, PORT_REDIRECTOR, PORT_HTTP, 47210, 1, 0, 65535]);
    let len = r.below(64) as usize;
    let mut f = lan_frame(kind, r.next() as u32, dst, r.next() as u16, dport, r.below(8) as u8, r.below(4) as u32, &r.bytes(len));
    if r.chance(10) {
        f.truncate(12 + r.below(13) as usize);
    }
    f
}

/// a bundle of up to 8 entries (destination lists of up to 3), now and then a broken one
fn bundle(r: &Rng, others: &[u32]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = vec![32, 0, 0, 0];
    for _ in 0..r.below(8) + 1 {
        let f = if r.chance(50) { udp(ROAM_HUB_VIP, 47210, 47210, 1, &roam(r)) } else { raw_frame(r, others) };
        let k = r.below(4) as usize;
        b.push(k as u8);
        b.push(0);
        let len = if r.chance(5) { r.next() as u16 } else { f.len() as u16 };
        b.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
        for _ in 0..k {
            let d = *r.pick(&[VHOST_VIP, ROAM_HUB_VIP, 0xFFFF_FFFF, *r.pick(others)]);
            b.extend_from_slice(&d.to_be_bytes());
        }
        b.extend_from_slice(&f);
    }
    b
}

async fn players(port: u16) -> String {
    let mut s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap();
    let q = format!("GET /players HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost:{port}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n");
    s.write_all(q.as_bytes()).await.unwrap();
    let mut r = Vec::new();
    let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), s.read_to_end(&mut r)).await;
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&r).to_string()
}

/// a session of the fuzz: its browser, its lobby connection (logged in again once the lobby closed it) and its
/// Messenger connection
struct Player {
    b: Browser,
    name: String,
    lobby: Conn,
    buddy: Conn,
}

impl Player {
    async fn new(port: u16, name: &str) -> Player {
        let b = Browser::open_at(&format!("localhost:{port}"), port, "", None).await;
        b.hello(name);
        let (lobby, buddy) = Player::login(&b, name).await.expect("logged in");
        Player { b, name: name.into(), lobby, buddy }
    }

    /// a lobby session and a Messenger login with its key (None: the lobby or the virtual host refused one)
    async fn login(b: &Browser, name: &str) -> Option<(Conn, Conn)> {
        let lobby = b.try_login(name).await?;
        let lkey = b.tcp(lobby, |t| t.last("pers").and_then(|m| m.get("LKEY")).unwrap_or("").to_string());
        let buddy = b.try_open_tcp(PORT_BUDDY).await?;
        b.send_msg(
            buddy,
            "AUTH",
            &[
                ("PROD", "NFS-CONSOLE-2005".into()),
                ("VERS", "0.1".into()),
                ("PRES", "20920".into()),
                ("USER", "/PC/NFS-CONSOLE-2005".into()),
                ("LKEY", lkey),
            ],
        );
        Some((lobby, buddy))
    }

    /// the lobby or Messenger closed a connection (a flood, a bad message): both go (RST), and a new login (the
    /// next round tries again when the lobby refused it)
    async fn again_if_closed(&mut self) -> bool {
        let closed = |c: Conn| self.b.tcp(c, |t| t.reset || t.fin);
        if !closed(self.lobby) && !closed(self.buddy) {
            return false;
        }
        for c in [self.lobby, self.buddy] {
            self.b.tcp_out(c, RST, &[]);
        }
        if let Some((l, m)) = Player::login(&self.b, &self.name).await {
            self.lobby = l;
            self.buddy = m;
        }
        true
    }
}

/// a race between the two players (the first creates the game, the other joins, it starts), then race reports with
/// its AUTH, random results and names, and now and then the game's other messages
async fn race(ps: &[Player], r: &Rng, i: usize) {
    let (h, o) = if r.chance(50) { (&ps[0], &ps[1]) } else { (&ps[1], &ps[0]) };
    let name = format!("g{}", i % 7);
    let track = if r.chance(80) { "TRACK=4014".to_string() } else { value(r, &["Fuzz1"]) };
    h.b.send_msg(h.lobby, "gcre", &[("NAME", name.clone()), ("PARAMS", track), ("MAXSIZE", value(r, &["Fuzz1"]))]);
    o.b.send_msg(o.lobby, "gjoi", &[("NAME", name.clone())]);
    h.b.send_msg(h.lobby, "gsta", &[("NAME", name.clone())]);
    // (the AUTH of this race when it started in time, else of one before, else any)
    let auth =
        h.b.try_until(50, |g| g.tcp.get(&h.lobby.port).and_then(|t| t.last("+ses")).and_then(|m| m.get("AUTH")).map(str::to_string)).await;
    let auth = auth.unwrap_or_else(|| value(r, &["Fuzz1"]));
    for p in [h, o] {
        let mut f = vec![("AUTH", auth.clone()), ("RESU", resu(r))];
        let names = ["NAME0", "NAME1", "NAME2"];
        for n in names.iter().take(r.below(4) as usize) {
            f.push((n, r.pick(&[&p.name[..], "Fuzz1", "Fuzz2", "Nobody", ""]).to_string()));
        }
        p.b.send_msg(p.lobby, "rank", &f);
    }
    if r.chance(30) {
        let kind = *r.pick(&["gdel", "glea", "gset", "snap", "gsea"]);
        h.b.send_msg(h.lobby, kind, &fields(r, &["Fuzz1", "Fuzz2"]));
    }
}

/// What the server did under the fuzz
struct FuzzRun {
    /// its console, from the start-up lines on
    lines: Vec<String>,
    /// /players after the fuzz and once a newcomer logged in
    players: Vec<String>,
    exit: Option<i32>,
    logins: usize,
    /// the state folder's files after the stop
    files: Vec<(String, String)>,
}

/// the fuzz against the server
async fn fuzz(seed: u64, frames: usize) -> FuzzRun {
    let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let data = tmp.path().join("game");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&data).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(data.join("SPEED2.EXE"), "MZ").unwrap();
    let state = tmp.path().join("state");
    let port = free_port();
    let mut child = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_nfsu2-server"))
        .env("NFSU2_THREADS", "2")
        .arg("--data")
        .arg(&data)
        .args(["--http-port", &port.to_string(), "--state"])
        .arg(&state)
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .spawn()
        .unwrap();
    let out = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
    for s in [Box::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap()) as Box<dyn std::io::Read + Send>, Box::new(child.stderr.take().unwrap())] {
        let out = out.clone();
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for l in BufReader::new(s).lines().map_while(Result::ok) {
                out.lock().unwrap().push(l);
            }
        });
    }
    assert!(
        wait_for(30_000, || out.lock().unwrap().iter().any(|l| l.starts_with("  access    :"))).await,
        "the server did not start: {:?}",
        out.lock().unwrap()
    );

    let mut ps = vec![Player::new(port, "Fuzz1").await, Player::new(port, "Fuzz2").await];
    // the raw frames come from a browser of their own: their SYNs hold the virtual host's connections for that
    // browser (8 at most) until the services' time-outs, and the players must be able to log in again
    let raw = Browser::open_at(&format!("localhost:{port}"), port, "", None).await;
    raw.hello("Raw");
    raw.got().drop_frames = true;
    let names = ["Fuzz1", "Fuzz2", "fuzz1", "Nobody", "", "Fuzz1 ", "F%41"];
    let others: Vec<u32> = ps.iter().map(|p| p.b.vip).chain([raw.vip]).collect();
    let r = Rng(std::cell::Cell::new(seed | 1));
    let mut logins = 0;
    for i in 0..frames {
        let p = &ps[r.below(2) as usize];
        let action = r.below(40);
        match action {
            0..=17 => {
                let kind = *r.pick(LOBBY_KINDS);
                let f = fields(&r, &names);
                p.b.send_msg(p.lobby, kind, &f);
            }
            18..=23 => {
                let kind = *r.pick(BUDDY_KINDS);
                let f = fields(&r, &names);
                p.b.send_msg(p.buddy, kind, &f);
            }
            24 | 25 => {
                // a lobby message whose header lies about its length, or DATA on a connection the host never opened
                let c =
                    if r.chance(50) { p.lobby } else { Conn { port: 1 + r.below(1000) as u16, cid: r.next() as u32, dport: PORT_LOBBY } };
                let mut m = encode_frame(r.pick(LOBBY_KINDS), &fields(&r, &names));
                let n = r.next() as u32;
                m[8..12].copy_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
                p.b.tcp_out(c, DATA, &m);
            }
            26..=29 => p.b.binary(udp(ROAM_HUB_VIP, 47210, *r.pick(&[47210u16, 47211, 47212, 1]), 1, &roam(&r))),
            30 => race(&ps, &r, i).await,
            31..=34 => raw.binary(raw_frame(&r, &others)),
            _ => raw.binary(bundle(&r, &others)),
        }
        // about 1000 frames a second in all: within the budgets of one client address (5000 frames, 512 KiB)
        if i % 20 == 19 {
            p.b.flush().await;
            sleep(20).await;
            for p in ps.iter_mut() {
                logins += p.again_if_closed().await as usize;
            }
        }
    }
    sleep(500).await;
    // (a session the last frames closed: logged in again, as in the loop)
    for p in ps.iter_mut() {
        logins += p.again_if_closed().await as usize;
    }
    assert!(ps.iter().all(|p| p.b.is_open()) && raw.is_open(), "the fuzzing browsers are still on the switch");
    // the server goes on
    let mut players = vec![http_body(&self::players(port).await)];
    let c = Browser::open_at(&format!("localhost:{port}"), port, "", None).await;
    c.hello("Late");
    c.login("Late").await;
    players.push(http_body(&self::players(port).await));
    drop(ps);
    drop((raw, c));
    let _ = Command::new("kill").args(["-TERM", &child.id().to_string()]).status();
    let t = Instant::now();
    let exit = loop {
        if let Some(st) = child.try_wait().unwrap() {
            break st.code();
        }
        if t.elapsed() > Duration::from_secs(10) {
            let _ = child.kill();
            break None;
        }
        sleep(20).await;
    };
    sleep(100).await;
    let files = ["online/stats.json", "online/buddies.json", "lan-addresses.json"]
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|f| std::fs::read_to_string(state.join(f)).ok().map(|s| (f.to_string(), s)))
        .collect();
    let lines = out.lock().unwrap().clone();
    FuzzRun { lines, players, exit, logins, files }
}

fn http_body(r: &str) -> String {
    r.split_once("\r\n\r\n").map_or(r, |x| x.1).to_string()
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
async fn random_frames_to_the_hosts_panic_nothing_and_the_server_goes_on() {
    let seed: u64 = std::env::var("NFSU2_FUZZ_SEED").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0x5EED_2026);
    let frames: usize = std::env::var("NFSU2_FUZZ_FRAMES").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(6000);
    let t0 = Instant::now();
    let run = fuzz(seed, frames).await;
    println!("{frames} frames in {:.1} s, {} logins again", t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64(), run.logins);
    println!("what the console said ({} lines):\n{}", run.lines.len(), run.lines.join("\n"));
    let bad: Vec<&String> = run.lines.iter().filter(|l| l.contains("panicked") || l.contains("a service failed")).collect();
    assert!(bad.is_empty(), "a panic: {bad:#?}");
    // /players: the three browsers, and one more with the newcomer, in Online mode too
    let p: Vec<serde_json::Value> = run.players.iter().map(|p| serde_json::from_str(p).unwrap()).collect();
    assert_eq!(p[0]["players"], 3, "{:?}", run.players);
    assert_eq!(p[1]["players"], 4, "{:?}", run.players);
    assert_eq!(p[1]["online"].as_u64(), p[0]["online"].as_u64().map(|n| n + 1), "{:?}", run.players);
    assert_eq!(run.exit, Some(0), "SIGTERM: exit code 0");
    for (f, s) in &run.files {
        assert!(serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(s).is_ok(), "{f}: {s}");

//! The switch (nfsu2-lan) with the Online host at 10.77.0.1 (nfsu2-online), and browsers on its WebSocket: the two
//! together.
//!   cargo test --test online_switch
//! - the host is on every peer list as server: true, frames to it never reach a browser, its answers do, broadcasts
//!   never reach it, a browser that leaves is reported
//! - ONL-2: what the host sends because of a client's frame is charged to that client (over its budget: that stream

mod common;

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

use bytes::Bytes;
use common::*;
use nfsu2_lan::LanOptions;
use nfsu2_online::{VHOST_NAME, VHOST_VIP};

use serde_json::{Value, json};

/// a stand-in for the online host: it keeps what the switch hands it
#[derive(Default)]
struct FakeOnline {
    seen: Mutex<Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>>,
    gone: Mutex<Vec<u32>>,
}

impl Host for FakeOnline {
    fn vip(&self) -> u32 {
        VHOST_VIP
    }
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        VHOST_NAME
    }
    fn listed(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
    fn frame(&self, from: u32, data: Bytes, _ctx: FrameCtx) {
        self.seen.lock().unwrap().push((from, data.to_vec()));
    }
    fn peer_gone(&self, vip: u32) {
        self.gone.lock().unwrap().push(vip);
    }
    fn info(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<Value> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = tx.send(json!({}));
        rx
    }
    fn vips(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<HashSet<u32>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = tx.send(HashSet::new());
        rx
    }
    fn stop(&self) {}
}

// the online host on the peer list, frames to it and back, no broadcasts
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn switch_the_online_host_on_the_peer_list_frames_to_it_and_back_no_broadcasts() {
    let online = Arc::new(FakeOnline::default());
    let s = start_with(LanOptions::default(), Some(online.clone() as Arc<dyn Host>), None).await;
    let send = s.lan.switch_send();
    let a = Browser::open(s.port, "", None).await;
    a.hello("Ann");
    let b = Browser::open(s.port, "", None).await;
    b.hello("Bob");
    let peers = a.until(|g| g.peers().filter(|l| l.len() == 3)).await;
    let servers: Vec<(u64, &str)> =
        peers.iter().filter(|p| p["server"] == true).map(|p| (p["vip"].as_u64().unwrap(), p["name"].as_str().unwrap())).collect();
    assert_eq!(servers, [(VHOST_VIP as u64, "NFSU2 Online")]);
    assert!(peers.iter().filter(|p| p["server"] != true).all(|p| p["vip"] != VHOST_VIP));
    // a frame to 10.77.0.1, with a forged source: the online host gets it with the sender's own address
    a.binary(lan_frame(4, 0x0a4d_00fe, VHOST_VIP, 50000, 20920, SYN, 5, &[]));
    assert!(wait_for(2000, || !online.seen.lock().unwrap().is_empty()).await);
    sleep(100).await;
    {
        let seen = online.seen.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(seen.len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(seen[0].0, a.vip);
        assert_eq!(be32(&seen[0].1, 4), a.vip);
    }
    assert_eq!(b.got().frames.len(), 0, "no browser sees it");
    // a broadcast never reaches the online host
    a.binary(lan_frame(3, 0, 0xffff_ffff, 9999, 9999, 0, 0, b"advert"));
    b.until(|g| (g.frames.len() == 1).then_some(())).await;
    assert_eq!(online.seen.lock().unwrap().len(), 1);
    // its answer reaches the browser
    assert_eq!(send(a.vip, Bytes::from(lan_frame(4, VHOST_VIP, a.vip, 20920, 50000, SYNACK, 5, &[])), None), SendResult::Sent);
    let f = a.until(|g| g.frames.iter().find(|x| x[16] == SYNACK).cloned()).await;
    assert_eq!(be32(&f, 4), VHOST_VIP);
    assert_eq!(
        send(ip("10.77.0.200"), Bytes::from(lan_frame(4, VHOST_VIP, 0, 1, 1, RST, 0, &[])), None),
        SendResult::Gone,
        "nobody there (null: not on the switch)"
    );
    // a browser that leaves is reported
    b.close().await;
    assert!(wait_for(2000, || !online.gone.lock().unwrap().is_empty()).await);
    sleep(100).await;
    assert_eq!(*online.gone.lock().unwrap(), [b.vip]);
    a.close().await;
    s.close().await;
}

/// a browser of client `group`, logged in to the lobby as `name`, then moved to the Lounge
async fn in_the_lounge(port: u16, group: &str, name: &str, rcvbuf: Option<u32>) -> (Browser, Conn) {
    let b = Browser::open(port, &format!("?g={group}"), rcvbuf).await;
    let c = b.login(name).await;
    b.send_msg(c, "move", &[("NAME", "Lounge".into())]);
    assert!(b.try_until(3000, |g| g.tcp[&c.port].last("move").map(|_| ())).await.is_some(), "{name} in the Lounge");
    (b, c)
}

// ONL-2, its first half: what the host sends for a client is charged to it (over its budget: that stream goes)
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn onl2_the_switch_what_the_host_sends_for_a_client_is_charged_to_it() {
    let (online, _lines) = online_host();
    // budgets small enough that one big car description to a room of five is more than a client's share
    let o = LanOptions {
        byte_rate: (4 << 10) as f64,
        group_byte_rate: (4 << 10) as f64,
        site_byte_rate: (1 << 20) as f64,
        max_payload: 1 << 20,
        ..LanOptions::default()
    };
    let sw = start(o, Some(online.clone()), None).await;
    let mut victims = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..5 {
        victims.push(in_the_lounge(sw.port, &format!("v{i}"), &format!("Victim{i}"), None).await);
    }
    // the victims' budgets fill up again
    sleep(2500).await;
    let (mal, mc) = in_the_lounge(sw.port, "mal", "Mallory", None).await;
    sleep(2500).await;
    let limited = sw.info().await["limited"].as_u64().unwrap();
    mal.send_msg(mc, "auxi", &[("TEXT", format!("C={}", "A".repeat(2000)))]);
    assert!(
        mal.try_until(2000, |g| g.tcp[&mc.port].reset.then_some(())).await.is_some(),
        "the client whose message made the server send more than its share loses that stream"
    );
    assert!(mal.is_open(), "... not its whole connection");
    for (v, c) in &victims {
        assert!(!v.tcp(*c, |t| t.reset) && v.is_open(), "the others keep theirs");
    }
    let info = sw.info().await;
    assert_eq!(info["limited"].as_u64().unwrap(), limited + 1, "the overrun counted once in the switch's limited");
    assert_eq!(info["online"]["overrun"], 1, "{}", info["online"]);
    sw.close().await;
}

// ONL-2, its second half: a receiver far behind loses its online stream, not its connection.  The receiver truly
// stops reading (small kernel buffers: its SO_RCVBUF and the switch's SO_SNDBUF, as the lan tests keep them) and
// another browser's LAN datagrams fill its queue on the switch until it is just past `send_buffer` (2 MiB here;
// datagrams queue up to `shed_queue`, 4 MiB here), past `online_queue` (1 MiB) too, so that only the order of the
// two checks keeps the connection.  That flood needs budgets that let it through, so this half runs on a switch of
// its own.
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn onl2_the_switch_a_receiver_far_behind_loses_its_online_stream_not_its_connection() {
    let (online, _lines) = online_host();
    let send_buffer = 2 << 20;
    let o = LanOptions {
        frame_rate: 100_000.0,
        byte_rate: (64 << 20) as f64,
        group_frame_rate: 100_000.0,
        group_byte_rate: (64 << 20) as f64,
        send_buffer,
        shed_queue: 4 << 20,
        send_buffer_os: 32 << 10,
        max_payload: 1 << 20,
        ..LanOptions::default()
    };
    let online_queue = LanOptions::default().online_queue;
    let sw = start(o, Some(online.clone()), None).await;
    let mut victims = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..5 {
        victims.push(in_the_lounge(sw.port, &format!("v{i}"), &format!("Victim{i}"), if i == 0 { Some(8 << 10) } else { None }).await);
    }
    let slow = &victims[0].0;
    let personas = |info: &Value| info["online"]["personas"].as_u64().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(personas(&sw.info().await), 5);
    // the slow receiver stops reading; a flood of LAN play's datagrams to it, in batches while its queue is short,
    // then one at a time until the queue is past `send_buffer` (and stays so: before the kernel's buffers are full an
    // ACK still frees some of it a moment later), so that no datagram of the flood finds it over the limit
    slow.pause(true);
    let flood = Browser::open(sw.port, "?g=flood", None).await;
    let mut n = 0;
    while n < 4000 {
        let q = sw.buffered(slow.vip);
        if q > send_buffer {
            sleep(100).await;
            if sw.buffered(slow.vip) > send_buffer {
                break;
            }
            continue;
        }
        let batch = if q + (128 << 10) < send_buffer { 8 } else { 1 };
        for _ in 0..batch {
            flood.binary(udp(slow.vip, 9999, 9999, 3, &[0x55; 8000]));
        }
        n += batch;
        flood.flush().await;
        sleep(if batch > 1 { 2 } else { 20 }).await;
    }
    let q = sw.buffered(slow.vip);
    println!("the receiver's queue: {q} bytes after {n} datagrams");
    assert!(q > send_buffer && q > online_queue, "the receiver is far behind ({q} bytes queued after {n} datagrams)");
    assert_eq!(sw.info().await["cuts"]["slow"], 0, "the flood itself cut nobody");
    victims[1].0.send_msg(victims[1].1, "mesg", &[("TEXT", "hello room".into())]);
    // the others heard the message (the host has handled it)
    for (v, c) in &victims[1..] {
        assert!(v.try_until(3000, |g| g.tcp[&c.port].last("+msg").map(|_| ())).await.is_some(), "the room heard it");
        assert!(!v.tcp(*c, |t| t.reset));
    }
    let info = sw.info().await;
    assert!(sw.peer(slow.vip).is_some_and(|p| p.open), "the slow receiver is still on the switch");
    assert_eq!(info["cuts"]["slow"], 0, "no connection was cut for it: {}", info["cuts"]);
    let vips = online.vips().await.unwrap();
    assert!(!vips.contains(&slow.vip), "its lobby session went");
    assert_eq!(personas(&info), 4, "{}", info["online"]);
    assert!(info["online"]["slow"].as_u64().unwrap() >= 1, "{}", info["online"]);
    // once it reads again it has all of what was queued, on the same connection
    slow.pause(false);
    assert!(wait_for(5000, || sw.buffered(slow.vip) == 0).await, "its queue drains");
    assert!(slow.is_open() && sw.peer(slow.vip).is_some(), "its connection stayed");
    sw.close().await;
}

// (a measurement: cargo test --test online_switch -- --ignored --nocapture; NFSU2_FLOOD_CONNS connections, 32 by
// default)  Clients within their budgets (2500 frames a second each, one client address each) send the Online host
// SYNs to a closed port (its cheapest frame: one RST back), in bundles of 250 every 100 ms.
// Every 500 ms: how long the host takes to answer info() (what is queued in front of it), what it got through, and
// this process's memory.
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
#[ignore]
async fn measure_the_online_hosts_queue_under_a_flood_of_frames() {
    let k: usize = std::env::var("NFSU2_FLOOD_CONNS").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(32);
    let secs: u64 = std::env::var("NFSU2_FLOOD_SECS").ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(4);
    let (online, _lines) = online_host();
    let sw = start(LanOptions { max_peers: 2000, max_payload: 1 << 20, ..LanOptions::default() }, Some(online.clone()), None).await;
    let mut floods = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..k {
        let b = Browser::open(sw.port, &format!("?g=flood{i}"), None).await;
        b.got().drop_frames = true;
        floods.push(b);
    }
    let rss0 = rss();
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    let stop = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
    for b in floods.iter() {
        let syns: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..250).map(|i| lan_frame(4, 0, VHOST_VIP, 40000 + i, 1, SYN, i as u32, &[])).collect();
        let bundle = bundle_of(&syns);
        let tx = b.sender();
        let stop = stop.clone();
        tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut iv = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
            while !stop.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                iv.tick().await;
                tx(bundle.clone());
            }
        }));
    }
    let mut worst = 0.0f64;
    for _ in 0..secs * 2 {
        sleep(500).await;
        let t = std::time::Instant::now();
        let info = online.info().await.unwrap();
        let ms = t.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1000.0;
        worst = worst.max(ms);
        let routed = sw.info().await["frames"].as_u64().unwrap();
        println!(
            "{:5.1} s: info() answered in {ms:7.1} ms; frames routed {routed}, SYNs the host took {}; memory +{} MB",
            t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            info["synIn"],
            (rss() as i64 - rss0 as i64) / (1 << 20)
        );
    }
    stop.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
    for t in tasks {
        let _ = t.await;
    }
    let t = std::time::Instant::now();
    let info = online.info().await.unwrap();
    println!(
        "{k} clients, {} frames a second offered: the host's queue drained {:.0} ms after the flood (worst wait {worst:.0} ms), {} SYNs",
        k * 2500,
        t.elapsed().as_secs_f64() * 1000.0,
        info["synIn"]
    );
    sw.close().await;
}

// (a measurement: cargo test --test online_switch -- --ignored --nocapture) The Online host's queue has no bound.
// Its thread made slow here by hand (the dev trace's tap takes 100 us a frame: a thread that handles 10,000 frames a
// second, as a stalled disk or a busy core would make it), 16 clients within their budgets send it SYNs to a closed
// port for 3 s.  What waits for the thread grows as long as they send (the free-roam hub drops frames past
// MAX_PENDING for this; Node could not fall behind: the host ran in the switch's own calls, and every socket waited
// for it): info() answers later and later, the memory grows, and once they stop it takes the thread seconds to
// catch up, while every Online player's lobby is that far behind.  (A first version of this measurement waited for
// each info() while the clients went on sending: it reached 3.8 GB in 10 minutes.)
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
#[ignore]
async fn measure_the_online_hosts_queue_behind_a_slow_thread() {
    use std::sync::Arc;
    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering::Relaxed};
    // (each SYN to a closed port: one RST back, one call of the tap: what the thread took)
    let taken = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
    let t2 = taken.clone();
    let online = nfsu2_online::OnlineHost::spawn(nfsu2_online::OnlineOptions {
        state_dir: None,
        log: Arc::new(|_: &str, _: Option<&str>| {}),
        tap: Some(Arc::new(move |_: &[u8]| {
            t2.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_micros(100));
        })),
        claims: None,
        deny: None,
    });
    let sw = start(LanOptions { max_peers: 2000, max_payload: 1 << 20, ..LanOptions::default() }, Some(online.clone()), None).await;
    let mut floods = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..16 {
        let b = Browser::open(sw.port, &format!("?g=flood{i}"), None).await;
        b.got().drop_frames = true;
        floods.push(b);
    }
    sleep(200).await;
    let (rss0, taken0) = (rss(), taken.load(Relaxed));
    let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let sent = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
    let mut tasks = Vec::new();
    for b in floods.iter() {
        let syns: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..250).map(|i| lan_frame(4, 0, VHOST_VIP, 40000 + i, 1, SYN, i as u32, &[])).collect();
        let bundle = bundle_of(&syns);
        let tx = b.sender();
        let (stop, sent) = (stop.clone(), sent.clone());
        tasks.push(tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut iv = tokio::time::interval(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
            while !stop.load(Relaxed) {
                iv.tick().await;
                tx(bundle.clone());
                sent.fetch_add(250, Relaxed);
            }
        }));
    }
    // every 500 ms, for 3 s: an info() asked now, answered (or not) within 200 ms; nothing here waits for the host
    let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
    for _ in 0..6 {
        sleep(500).await;
        let answered = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_millis(200), online.info()).await.is_ok();
        let (s, t) = (sent.load(Relaxed), taken.load(Relaxed) - taken0);
        let grown = rss() as i64 - rss0 as i64;
        println!(
            "{:4.1} s: info() {}; {s} frames sent to the host, {t} taken, {} waiting; memory +{} MB ({} bytes a frame waiting)",
            t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
            if answered { "answered in time" } else { "not answered in 200 ms" },
            s.saturating_sub(t),
            grown / (1 << 20),
            grown / s.saturating_sub(t).max(1) as i64
        );
    }
    stop.store(true, Relaxed);
    for t in tasks {
        let _ = t.await;
    }
    // the server stops now (SIGTERM: lan.stop(), which stops the host and waits for its files): the stop waits
    // behind every frame queued before it
    let s = sent.load(Relaxed);
    let t = std::time::Instant::now();
    let lan = sw.lan.clone();
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || lan.stop()).await.unwrap();
    println!("the flood ended ({s} frames sent): the stop took {:.1} s", t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    sw.close().await;
}

//! The switch (nfsu2-lan) with the free-roam hub at 10.77.0.253 (nfsu2-roam) and the Online host beside it, as
//! src/app/run.rs wires them, and browsers on its WebSocket: the hub on the switch.
//!   cargo test --test roam_switch
//! The hub ticks on its own thread every second, as it does in the server (the hub's own tests in crates/roam tick it
//! by hand), so the test waits for the list it looks for.

mod common;

use common::*;
use nfsu2_lan::LanOptions;
use nfsu2_online::VHOST_VIP;
use nfsu2_roam::{ROAM_HUB_VIP, RoamHub, RoamOptions};
use nfsu2_util::Host;
use serde_json::Value;

/// the hub's info() once `f` says yes of it (or after 2 s): the hub takes what the switch posts it on its own thread
async fn hub_until(hub: &RoamHub, f: impl Fn(&Value) -> bool) -> Value {
    let end = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_secs(2);
    loop {
        let v = hub.info().await.unwrap();
        if f(&v) || std::time::Instant::now() > end {
            return v;
        }
        sleep(20).await;
    }
}

/// the hub's PEERS list to `to` that names someone, out of what that browser got: (frame, first entry's vip, id)
fn list_from_hub(g: &Got, to: u32) -> Option<(Vec<u8>, u32, u32)> {
    g.frames
        .iter()
        .filter(|f| f.len() >= 16 + 17 && f[0] == 1 && be32(f, 4) == ROAM_HUB_VIP && be32(f, 8) == to)
        .find(|f| f[16 + 16] == 1 && f.len() >= 16 + 27)
        .map(|f| (f.clone(), be32(f, 16 + 17), le32(f, 16 + 23)))
}

// on the switch: frames to 10.77.0.253 reach the hub, its lists come back, a departure is forgotten
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn on_the_switch_frames_to_the_hub_reach_it_its_lists_come_back_a_departure_is_forgotten() {
    let hub = roam_hub(RoamOptions::default());
    let (online, _lines) = online_host();
    let sw = start(LanOptions { max_payload: 1 << 20, ..LanOptions::default() }, Some(online), Some(hub.clone())).await;
    let a = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    a.hello("Ann");
    let b = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    b.hello("Bob");
    a.binary(to_hub(&roam_hello(501)));
    a.binary(to_hub(&roam_snap(501, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])));
    b.binary(to_hub(&roam_hello(502)));
    b.binary(to_hub(&roam_snap(502, [20.0, 0.0, 0.0])));
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 2).await["players"], 2, "both reached the hub");
    // its next tick (one a second)
    let (got, vip, id) = a.until_ms(2500, |g| list_from_hub(g, a.vip)).await;
    assert_eq!(be32(&got, 8), a.vip, "Ann got a list from 10.77.0.253");
    assert!(a.until(|g| Some(g.bundled.is_empty())).await, "a page that takes no bundles: the list alone");
    assert_eq!(be16(&got, 12), 47210);
    assert_eq!(be16(&got, 14), 47210);
    assert_eq!(vip, b.vip);
    assert_eq!(id, 502);
    let info = sw.info().await;
    let peers = info["peers"].as_array().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(peers.len(), 2);
    assert!(!peers.iter().any(|p| p["vip"] == "10.77.0.253"), "the hub is on nobody's peer list");
    // the browsers' own lists: the two of them and the Online host, never the hub
    let list = a.until(|g| g.peers().filter(|l| l.len() == 3)).await;
    assert!(list.iter().all(|p| p["vip"] != ROAM_HUB_VIP), "{list:?}");
    assert!(list.iter().any(|p| p["vip"] == VHOST_VIP && p["server"] == true));
    // back from the LAN screens: free roam alone
    for x in [&a, &b] {
        x.text(r#"{"t":"lan","on":0}"#);
        x.text(r#"{"t":"ping","id":77}"#);
        x.until(|g| g.ctl.iter().any(|m| m["t"] == "pong" && m["id"] == 77).then_some(())).await;
    }
    let n = sw.lan.breakdown().await;
    assert_eq!((n.players, n.roam), (2, 2), "both counted in free roam (the console's [players] line): {n:?}");
    assert!(wait_for(2500, || hub.in_roam() == 2).await, "both driving in free roam (/players): {}", hub.in_roam());
    b.close().await;
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 1).await["players"], 1, "Bob left the switch: the hub forgot him");
    assert!(wait_for(2500, || hub.in_roam() == 1).await, "and at its next tick /players: {}", hub.in_roam());
    let roam: Value = sw.info().await["roam"].clone();
    assert_eq!(roam["players"], 1, "{roam}");
    a.close().await;
    sw.close().await;
}

// a browser whose connection just ends, without a close frame, is forgotten by the hub as well
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_connection_that_ends_without_a_close_frame_is_forgotten_by_the_hub() {
    let hub = roam_hub(RoamOptions::default());
    let sw = start(LanOptions::default(), None, Some(hub.clone())).await;
    let a = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    a.hello("Ann");
    a.binary(to_hub(&roam_hello(601)));
    a.binary(to_hub(&roam_snap(601, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0])));
    a.flush().await;
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 1).await["players"], 1);
    assert_eq!(hub.vips().await.unwrap().len(), 1);
    a.terminate();
    assert!(wait_for(2000, || sw.lan.peer_count() == 0).await, "Ann is off the switch");
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 0).await["players"], 0, "the hub forgot her");
    assert!(hub.vips().await.unwrap().is_empty());
    sw.close().await;
}

/// a bundle (the switch's frame kind 32) of (frame, destinations) entries: none for the frame's own destination
fn bundle_to(entries: &[(Vec<u8>, Vec<u32>)]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = vec![32, 0, 0, 0];
    for (f, to) in entries {
        b.push(to.len() as u8);
        b.push(0);
        b.extend_from_slice(&(f.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
        for v in to {
            b.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
        }
        b.extend_from_slice(f);
    }
    b
}

// bundles with the hub on the switch: a page that takes bundles sends its datagrams in them, an entry to the hub by
// its own destination, and one whose list names the hub and a friend: the hub takes both (the friend's SNAP links
// the two), the friend gets its copy with the sender's address
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn datagrams_to_the_hub_inside_bundles_reach_it() {
    let hub = roam_hub(RoamOptions::default());
    let sw = start(LanOptions::default(), None, Some(hub.clone())).await;
    let a = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    a.text(r#"{"t":"hello","name":"Ann","bundle":1}"#);
    let b = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    b.text(r#"{"t":"hello","name":"Bob","bundle":1}"#);
    sleep(50).await;
    let snap = udp(b.vip, 47210, 47210, 1, &roam_snap(701, [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]));
    a.binary(bundle_to(&[(to_hub(&roam_hello(701)), vec![]), (snap, vec![ROAM_HUB_VIP, b.vip])]));
    b.binary(to_hub(&roam_hello(702)));
    b.binary(to_hub(&roam_snap(702, [10.0, 0.0, 0.0])));
    let got = b.until(|g| g.frames.iter().find(|f| f[0] == 1 && be32(f, 4) == a.vip).cloned()).await;
    assert_eq!(be32(&got, 8), b.vip, "the friend's copy, to its own address");
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 2).await["players"], 2, "both reached the hub");
    // Ann's SNAP came to the hub only in the bundle's list: the hub's next tick links the two
    let (_, vip, id) = a.until_ms(2500, |g| list_from_hub(g, a.vip)).await;
    assert_eq!((vip, id), (b.vip, 702));
    let info = sw.info().await;
    assert_eq!(info["limited"], 0, "{info}");
    a.close().await;
    b.close().await;
    sw.close().await;
}

// a claimed name (nfsu2-claims) on the switch: the hello's "claim" names the keyphrase its frames come with, and the
// hub links a player under a claimed name only when that keyphrase claimed it
#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
async fn a_claimed_name_is_its_keyphrases_on_the_switch() {
    let claims = std::sync::Arc::new(nfsu2_claims::Claims::in_memory());
    let (a_token, c_token) = ("A".repeat(43), "C".repeat(43));
    claims.claim("Alex", &nfsu2_claims::owner_of_token(&a_token).unwrap(), nfsu2_util::now_ms()).unwrap();
    let lines = std::sync::Arc::new(parking_lot::Mutex::new(Vec::<String>::new()));
    let l2 = lines.clone();
    let hub = RoamHub::spawn_with(RoamOptions::default(), std::sync::Arc::new(move |l: &str| l2.lock().push(l.to_string())), Some(claims));
    let sw = start(LanOptions { max_payload: 1 << 20, ..LanOptions::default() }, None, Some(hub.clone())).await;
    let hello = |b: &Browser, name: &str, claim: Option<&str>| {
        let mut m = serde_json::json!({ "t": "hello", "name": name });
        if let Some(c) = claim {
            m["claim"] = c.into();
        }
        b.text(&m.to_string());
    };
    // the owner, a player of no keyphrase and one of another under the same name, and a bystander
    let a = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    hello(&a, "Alex", Some(&a_token));
    let b = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    hello(&b, "Bob", None);
    let c = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    hello(&c, "Alex", Some(&c_token));
    let d = Browser::open(sw.port, "", None).await;
    hello(&d, "Alex", None);
    for (x, id, name, at) in [(&a, 501, &b"Alex"[..], 0.0), (&b, 502, b"Bob", 10.0), (&c, 503, b"alex", 20.0), (&d, 504, b"Alex", 30.0)] {
        x.binary(to_hub(&roam_hello_named(id, name)));
        x.binary(to_hub(&roam_snap(id, [at, 0.0, 0.0])));
    }
    assert_eq!(hub_until(&hub, |v| v["players"] == 4).await["players"], 4);
    let (_, vip, _) = b.until_ms(2500, |g| list_from_hub(g, b.vip)).await;
    assert_eq!(vip, a.vip, "Bob's list: the owner, nearest of the two it may see");
    sleep(1200).await;
    let named = |x: &Browser| {
        b.got().frames.iter().any(|f| {
            f.len() >= 16 + 27 && f[0] == 1 && be32(f, 8) == b.vip && f[16 + 16] >= 1 && {
                let n = f[16 + 16] as usize;
                (0..n).any(|i| be32(f, 16 + 17 + 10 * i) == x.vip)
            }
        })
    };
    assert!(named(&a), "the owner is linked");
    assert!(!named(&c) && !named(&d), "the others under its name are not");
    let l = lines.lock().clone();
    assert_eq!(l.iter().filter(|l| l.contains("a name another keyphrase claimed")).count(), 2, "{l:?}");
    for x in [a, b, c, d] {
        x.close().await;
    }
    sw.close().await;
}

{"id": "AT001717", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/app/away.ts", "originalBytes": 4115, "originalSha256": "eafb6ab019c8c4520ee3e8acfb3c8a96fc2cf87575a1136ccd27b67eb72a7950", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 4115, "utf8TotalBytes": 4115}
