// A player who leaves the game running gives their place on the server back.  After inputMs without a key,
// the mouse or a controller (input/index.ts lastInput), a warning counts down warnMs; then the page lets the
// server's switch go (net/index.ts setAway): Online and LAN play lose their connection, free roam its friends,
// and the place is free for another player.  A tab in the background gets no warning anyone would see: after
// hiddenMs there the place goes at once.  The next input takes the link up again (a new address; the game's
// Online mode logs in again).  Only while the game holds a place (free roam, the LAN and Online screens), and
// never while the page cannot see the input (the game's own driver plays an input script).

import type { InputSubsystem, NetSubsystem } from './contract';
import { t } from './i18n';

export interface AwayLimits { inputMs: number; hiddenMs: number; warnMs: number }
export const AWAY_LIMITS: AwayLimits = { inputMs: 12 * 60_000, hiddenMs: 8 * 60_000, warnMs: 2 * 60_000 };

const TICK_MS = 1000;
const span = (ms: number) => ms >= 60_000 ? `${Math.round(ms / 60_000)} min` : `${Math.round(ms / 1000)} s`;

export class AwayCheck {
  private timer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval>;
  private hiddenSince: number | null = document.hidden ? performance.now() : null;
  /** when the warning came up, and when the place went back */
  private warnedAt: number | null = null;
  private awayAt: number | null = null;

  /** s: the running game's subsystems (they attach later); show(text): the message over the game, null: none */
  constructor(private s: { input: InputSubsystem | null; net: NetSubsystem | null }, private limits: AwayLimits,
              private show: (text: string | null) => void, private log: (line: string) => void) {
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', this.onVisibility);
    this.timer = setInterval(() => this.tick(), TICK_MS);
  }

  private onVisibility = () => {
    this.hiddenSince = document.hidden ? this.hiddenSince ?? performance.now() : null;
    this.tick();
  };

  private tick() {
    const net = this.s.net, last = this.s.input?.lastInput?.() ?? null, now = performance.now(), L = this.limits;
    if (!net?.away || last === null) return;
    if (this.awayAt !== null) {
      if (last <= this.awayAt) return;
      this.awayAt = null; this.show(null);
      if (this.hiddenSince !== null) this.hiddenSince = now;      // a controller's button in a background tab
      net.away(false);
      this.log('[app] away: the player is back, the game takes a place on the server again when it needs one');
      return;
    }
    if (this.warnedAt !== null && last > this.warnedAt) {
      this.warnedAt = null; this.show(null);
      this.log('[app] away: input again, the place on the server stays');
    }
    if (!net.holding?.()) { if (this.warnedAt !== null) { this.warnedAt = null; this.show(null); } return; }
    const hidden = this.hiddenSince !== null && now - this.hiddenSince >= L.hiddenMs;
    if (hidden || (this.warnedAt !== null && now - this.warnedAt >= L.warnMs)) {
      this.warnedAt = null; this.awayAt = now;
      net.away(true);
      this.log(`[app] away: ${hidden ? `the tab was in the background for ${span(now - this.hiddenSince!)}` : `no input for ${span(now - last)}`}, ` +
               'so the place on the server goes back');
      this.show(t('You were away, so you left multiplayer and freed your place on the server. Press any key or button to rejoin.'));
      return;
    }
    if (this.warnedAt === null && now - last >= L.inputMs) {
      this.warnedAt = now;
      this.log(`[app] away: no input for ${span(now - last)}: the place on the server goes back in ${span(L.warnMs)} unless there is some`);
    }
    if (this.warnedAt !== null)
      this.show(t('Still there? You leave multiplayer in {n} s. Press any key or button to stay.',
        { n: Math.max(1, Math.ceil((L.warnMs - (now - this.warnedAt)) / 1000)) }));
  }

  stop() {
    clearInterval(this.timer);
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', this.onVisibility);
    this.show(null);
  }
}

// The page's cards over the game in one look (style.css .ov-*: the race lobby's, quick chat's picker, a message to a
// friend): blocks a line apart (a title, what it is about, the keys, one hint), a key cap and what it does.

export const el = <K extends keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap>(tag: K, cls?: string, text?: string) => {
  const e = document.createElement(tag);
  if (cls) e.className = cls;
  if (text !== undefined) e.textContent = text;
  return e;
};

/** a block of a card (a line above all but the first) */
export const block = (...kids: HTMLElement[]) => { const b = el('div', 'ov-block'); b.append(...kids); return b; };

/** a key cap (null: none) and what it does; with f a button too (a click or a tap does it, not the game's key) */
export function act(key: string | null, what: string | Node, f?: () => void): HTMLElement {
  const d = el('div', f ? 'ov-act tap' : 'ov-act');
  if (key) d.append(el('kbd', '', key));
  d.append(typeof what === 'string' ? el('span', '', what) : what);
  if (f) {
    d.onpointerdown = e => e.preventDefault();   // the canvas keeps the focus (and with it the keyboard)
    d.onclick = () => f();
  }
  return d;
}

/** a line's text with a player's name in it bold (lime: the names in the log and the notes) */
export function named(s: string, name: string): HTMLSpanElement {
  const span = el('span'), at = name ? s.indexOf(name) : -1;
  if (at < 0) { span.textContent = s; return span; }
  span.append(s.slice(0, at), el('b', '', name), s.slice(at + name.length));
  return span;
}

// The header's Changelog: a popup with the releases of CHANGELOG.md, newest first, as web/build.mjs writes them to
// /changelog.json, each with its new things and, folded under them, its fixes.  Fetched the first time it opens, again
// after a failure.  The changes stay in English (lang="en"); the popup's own words and the releases' dates follow the
// page's language.

import { dateLocale, onLanguage, t, tn } from './i18n';

type Change = [area: string, text: string];
/** one release: its date (yyyy-mm-dd), the last commit it brings, its new things and its fixes ('' area: none) */
type Release = { date: string; commit: string; changes: Change[]; fixes: Change[] };

function list(changes: Change[]) {
  const ul = Object.assign(document.createElement('ul'), { lang: 'en' });
  for (const [area, text] of changes) {
    const li = ul.appendChild(document.createElement('li'));
    if (area) li.append(Object.assign(document.createElement('strong'), { textContent: `${area}:` }), ' ');
    li.append(text);
  }
  return ul;
}

export function changelog(button: HTMLElement, dialog: HTMLDialogElement, body: HTMLElement) {
  let releases: Release[] | null = null, loading: Promise<void> | null = null;
  const draw = () => {
    if (!releases) return;
    const year = new Date().getFullYear();
    body.replaceChildren(...releases.flatMap(r => {
      const d = new Date(`${r.date}T12:00:00Z`);
      const h = Object.assign(document.createElement('h3'), {
        textContent: d.toLocaleDateString(dateLocale(), { day: 'numeric', month: 'long', timeZone: 'UTC', ...(d.getUTCFullYear() === year ? {} : { year: 'numeric' }) }),
      });
      const out: HTMLElement[] = [h];
      if (r.changes.length) out.push(list(r.changes));
      if (r.fixes.length) {
        const fixes = document.createElement('details');
        fixes.append(Object.assign(document.createElement('summary'), { textContent: tn(r.fixes.length, '{n} fix', '{n} fixes') }), list(r.fixes));
        out.push(fixes);
      }
      return out;
    }));
  };
  const load = async () => {
    const r = await fetch('/changelog.json', { cache: 'no-cache' });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
    releases = await r.json() as Release[];
    draw();
  };
  button.onclick = () => {
    dialog.showModal();
    loading ??= load().catch(() => {
      loading = null;
      body.replaceChildren(Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'hint', textContent: t("Couldn't load the changelog.") }));
    });
  };
  onLanguage(draw);
}

{"id": "AT001720", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/app/checks.ts", "originalBytes": 22858, "originalSha256": "8c1011626912270b3d257c3b92b90e235eb6d228cb96fd4571a2b7dfdcbe45b9", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 22858, "utf8TotalBytes": 22858}

// What this browser and this page need before the game can start, each with
// a message that says what to do when it is missing.  The start page shows
// only the ones that fail or warn, in the page's language (i18n.ts), each
// problem with its code: the same in every language, so a screenshot says
// which one it is.

import { homeScreenInstead } from './display';
import { fill, N, type Vars } from './i18n';

export type CheckState = 'pending' | 'ok' | 'warn' | 'fail';
/**
 * label and detail in English, filled in (the log, the tests); tl and td: the same as written, with {name}s for v,
 * which the page shows in its language; code: a failure's or warning's fixed name (GPU-ADAPTER-WIN)
 */
export interface Check { id: string; label: string; state: CheckState; detail: string; code?: string; tl?: string; td?: string; v?: Vars }

/** a check whose label and detail are English with {name}s for v */
export function check(id: string, label: string, state: CheckState, detail: string, code?: string, v?: Vars): Check {
  return { id, label: fill(label, v), state, detail: fill(detail, v), code, tl: label, td: detail, v };
}

export const MIN_CHROME = 140;
/** Atomics.waitAsync (the renderer's and the network's doorbells) is in Firefox from 145 */
export const MIN_FIREFOX = 145;

/** The JavaScript optimizer is off for this site: Chrome's site setting (since 133), Android's Advanced Protection
 *  (Chrome 137 on Android 16) or Edge's Enhanced security.  Chrome then has no WebAssembly at all (checkIsolation), or
 *  only its interpreter, which can't compile the game: "exnref not supported by the Wasm interpreter" (shell.ts). */
export const NO_JIT = N('The JavaScript optimizer is off for this site, and the game can\'t run without it. In Chrome: Settings, Privacy and security, JavaScript optimization and security, allow this site (Android\'s Advanced Protection turns it off). In Edge: add this site as an exception to Enhanced security.');
/** a game module that did not compile for that reason */
export const noJit = (e: unknown) => /Wasm interpreter|WebAssembly is not defined/i.test(String(e));
/** a module of one function with SIMD in it (i8x16.splat, i8x16.popcnt): valid only where the game's SIMD compiles */
const SIMD_PROBE = new Uint8Array([0, 97, 115, 109, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 5, 1, 96, 0, 1, 123, 3, 2, 1, 0, 10, 10, 1, 8, 0, 65, 0, 253, 15, 253, 98, 11]);

/**
 * A Chromium browser's name (Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera; Chromium where it names itself not), its
 * own major version (Opera's and Samsung Internet's aren't Chromium's) and Chromium's, or null (another browser),
 * from User-Agent Client Hints.  Their lists hold a made-up "Not?A_Brand" too.
 */
export function chromeVersion(): { brand: string; own: number; major: number } | null {
  const uad = (navigator as any).userAgentData as { brands?: { brand: string; version: string }[] } | undefined;
  const all = uad?.brands ?? [];
  const named = all.find(x => !/^Chromium$|Not.A.Brand/i.test(x.brand)), engine = all.find(x => x.brand === 'Chromium') ?? named;
  if (engine) {
    const b = named ?? engine;
    return { brand: b.brand, own: parseInt(b.version, 10), major: parseInt(engine.version, 10) };
  }
  const m = /Chrome\/(\d+)/.exec(navigator.userAgent);
  return m ? { brand: 'Chromium', own: +m[1], major: +m[1] } : null;
}

/** Firefox's major version, or null (another browser; Firefox on iOS is WebKit and says FxiOS). */
export function firefoxVersion(): number | null {
  const m = /Firefox\/(\d+)/.exec(navigator.userAgent);
  return m ? +m[1] : null;
}

/** a Chromium browser as it calls itself (Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave): for a setting it names, so Edge's players don't
 *  look for Chrome */
function brandName(): string {
  return (chromeVersion()?.brand ?? 'Chrome').replace(/^(Google|Microsoft) /, '').replace(/^Chromium$/, 'Chrome');
}

/** what the messages call this browser: Firefox, Chrome (any Chromium browser) or the browser */
export function browserName(): string {
  return firefoxVersion() !== null ? 'Firefox' : chromeVersion() ? 'Chrome' : N('the browser');
}

/** Safari's major version, 0 for the other browsers on an iPhone or iPad (all Safari's engine, no Version/), or null */
export function safariVersion(): number | null {
  const ua = navigator.userAgent;
  if (!/AppleWebKit\//.test(ua) || /Chrome\/|Firefox\//.test(ua)) return null;     // Chromium says AppleWebKit too
  const m = /Version\/(\d+)/.exec(ua);
  return m ? +m[1] : 0;
}

/**
 * Which browser this is: a warning at most, never a reason to stop.  What the
 * game needs is checked by what it is (WebGPU, isolation, storage below), so
 * Edge, Brave, Opera (Chrome's engine) and Safari get no warning: the checks
 * below say what one lacks.
 */
export function checkBrowser(): Check {
  const f = firefoxVersion();
  if (f !== null) {
    if (f < MIN_FIREFOX) return check('browser', 'Firefox {v}', 'warn', N('Tested on Firefox {min} or newer: update it (Help, About Firefox) if something doesn\'t work.'), 'BROWSER-FIREFOX-OLD', { v: f, min: MIN_FIREFOX });
    return check('browser', 'Firefox {v}', 'ok', N('A tested browser.'), undefined, { v: f });
  }
  if (homeScreenInstead()) return check('browser', N('Browser'), 'warn', N('For full screen on iPhone, add this page to the Home Screen (Share menu) and play from its icon. That copy has its own saves: Cloud saves bring yours over.'), 'BROWSER-IPHONE');
  const c = chromeVersion();
  if (c) {
    const brand = c.brand.replace(/^(Google|Microsoft) /, '');
    if (c.major < MIN_CHROME) return check('browser', '{brand} {v}', 'warn', N('Tested on Chrome {min} or newer: update it (Help, About Google Chrome) if something doesn\'t work.'), 'BROWSER-CHROME-OLD', { brand, v: c.own, min: MIN_CHROME });
    return check('browser', '{brand} {v}', 'ok', N('A tested browser.'), undefined, { brand, v: c.own });
  }
  const s = safariVersion();
  if (s) return check('browser', 'Safari {v}', 'ok', N('A tested browser.'), undefined, { v: s });
  if (s === 0) return check('browser', N('Browser'), 'ok', N('A tested browser.'));
  return check('browser', N('Browser'), 'warn', N('Only Chrome and Firefox are tested. This browser may still work.'), 'BROWSER-OTHER');
}

export function checkIsolation(): Check {
  const label = N('Secure, isolated page');
  if (!isSecureContext) {
    return check('isolation', label, 'fail', N('This address is not secure, so {browser} blocks what the game needs. Use the https:// address.'),
      'PAGE-NOT-SECURE', { browser: browserName() });
  }
  if (!crossOriginIsolated || typeof SharedArrayBuffer === 'undefined') {
    // on nfsu2.xyz it is almost always an extension that changes the page (a private window shows it)
    return check('isolation', label, 'fail', N('Something in this browser changes the page, most often an extension, so the game can\'t run. Open the page in a private window: if it works there, turn your extensions off one by one.'), 'PAGE-NOT-ISOLATED');
  }
  // the JavaScript optimizer off for this site (Chrome's site setting, Android's Advanced Protection, Edge's Enhanced
  // security): Chrome then has no WebAssembly at all, or only its interpreter, which can't compile the game (shell.ts)
  if (typeof WebAssembly === 'undefined') return check('isolation', label, 'fail', NO_JIT, 'PAGE-NO-JIT');
  // shared memory at all, of one page and no more: a 32-bit Chrome (most phones with up to 4 GB) sets aside up to
  // 1 GB of its addresses for a memory's maximum until the memory is collected, the gigabyte the game asks for at
  // Play (host/memory.ts); whether the game gets its memory is Play's question
  try { new WebAssembly.Memory({ initial: 1, maximum: 1, shared: true }); }
  catch (e) { return check('isolation', label, 'fail', N('Shared WebAssembly memory is not available: {error}'), 'PAGE-NO-MEMORY', { error: String(e) }); }
  if (typeof Atomics.waitAsync !== 'function') {
    return check('isolation', label, 'fail', N('This browser is too old for the game (no Atomics.waitAsync). Update {browser}.'), 'PAGE-NO-WAITASYNC', { browser: browserName() });
  }
  // the game is built with SIMD (web/build.sh): a processor without it (before SSE4.1 on a PC, such as a Phenom II) or
  // an old browser can't compile it, and the module's retries would never pass
  if (!WebAssembly.validate(SIMD_PROBE)) {
    return check('isolation', label, 'fail', N('This computer\'s processor is too old for the game, or the browser is out of date. Update {browser}; if that doesn\'t help, the game can\'t run on this computer.'), 'PAGE-NO-SIMD', { browser: browserName() });
  }
  return check('isolation', label, 'ok', N('HTTPS or localhost, cross-origin isolated, threads and shared memory available.'));
}

/**
 * The graphics, in words a player follows: what is wrong and what to do about it, with the
 * browser's own setting or address to type where there is one.  Chrome's own list of causes
 * (developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/webgpu/troubleshooting-tips) and where each browser
 * has WebGPU on (github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/wiki/Implementation-Status) decide the cases.
 * lostBefore: the last game stopped because its graphics went (GPU-LOST).
 */
export async function checkGpu(lostBefore = false): Promise<Check & { adapter?: string }> {
  const label = N('Graphics (WebGPU)');
  const gpu = (navigator as any).gpu as GPU | undefined;
  const ua = navigator.userAgent;
  const ff = firefoxVersion() !== null, chromium = !ff && chromeVersion() !== null;
  const android = /Android/.test(ua), linux = /Linux/.test(ua) && !android, windows = /Windows/.test(ua);
  // every browser on an iPhone or iPad is Safari's engine (an iPad says Macintosh, with touch)
  const ios = /iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(ua) || (/Macintosh/.test(ua) && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 1);
  const fail = (detail: string, code: string, v?: Vars) => check('gpu', label, 'fail', detail, code, v);
  // navigator.gpu is there in secure pages only: the isolation check says what to do
  if (!isSecureContext) return fail(N('Off because this address is not secure (see above).'), 'GPU-NOT-SECURE');
  // Firefox: on by itself on Windows (141) and on Macs with Apple chips (147), elsewhere in Nightly only
  if (!gpu) return ff
    ? android
      ? fail(N('Firefox for Android has no WebGPU yet. Play in Chrome.'), 'GPU-OFF-FIREFOX-ANDROID')
      : fail(N('This Firefox has no WebGPU. On Windows and Apple-chip Macs, update Firefox (Help, About Firefox). Elsewhere, such as Linux, play in Chrome or set dom.webgpu.enabled to true in about:config.'), 'GPU-OFF-FIREFOX')
    : chromium
      ? fail(N('This Chrome has no WebGPU. Update Chrome (Help, About Google Chrome). On Linux, also turn on chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu and restart Chrome.'), 'GPU-OFF')
      : ios
        ? fail(N('This browser has no WebGPU. It comes with iOS 26 and iPadOS 26: update this device (Settings, General, Software Update).'), 'GPU-OFF-IOS')
        : fail(N('This browser has no WebGPU. Play in Chrome or Firefox.'), 'GPU-OFF-OTHER');
  let ad: GPUAdapter | null = null;
  try { ad = await gpu.requestAdapter({ powerPreference: 'high-performance' }); } catch { /* reported below */ }
  if (!ad) {
    // the graphics went during the last game, and the reloaded page gets no adapter: the browser keeps them off for a
    // while, not graphics too old (two players' Intel Iris Xe, a hung Direct3D 12 device, then GPU-ADAPTER-WIN in Chrome
    // and Brave).  Chrome blocks a site whose graphics hung from them for two minutes (gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc,
    // kBlockedDomainExpirationPeriod); the page asks again until they are back (shell.ts recheckGpu)
    if (lostBefore) {
      const b = browserName();
      // a phone or a tablet has no graphics driver of its own to update
      if (android || ios) return fail(N('The graphics stopped during your last game and {browser} hasn\'t given them back yet. Wait a minute or two (the page checks every 10 seconds). If Play stays off, close {browser} completely and open it again.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-AFTER-LOST', { browser: b });
      return fail(N('The graphics stopped during your last game and {browser} hasn\'t given them back yet. Wait a minute or two (the page checks every 10 seconds). If Play stays off, close every {browser} window and open it again. If it keeps happening, update the graphics driver.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-AFTER-LOST', { browser: b });
    }
    // Firefox has one list of graphics drivers it leaves out, and on Windows, as Chrome, Direct3D 12 only
    if (ff) return fail(N('Firefox won\'t use this computer\'s graphics: they or their driver may be too old. Update the driver or try Chrome (about:support, Graphics, says why).'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-FIREFOX');
    if (chromium) {
      // Chrome 121: Android 12 and newer, on some graphics chips; the unsafe flag lifts its blocklist (Samsung's
      // Xclipse runs the game with it)
      // (the step that works first: players stopped reading after "update")
      if (android) return fail(N('Chrome can\'t use this device\'s graphics yet. On some phones one switch fixes it: 1. In the Chrome app, type chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu into the address bar at the top. 2. Set it to Enabled. 3. Tap Relaunch. Still not working? Update Android and Chrome; some phones can\'t run the game.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-ANDROID');
      // graphics acceleration off in Chrome's settings (or graphics it uses for nothing): WebGL draws in software, or not at all;
      // named as the browser calls itself (Edge, Opera), the setting as it reads in each
      const gl = webglRenderer();
      if (gl === null || /SwiftShader|llvmpipe|softpipe|Basic Render/i.test(gl))
        return fail(N('{browser} isn\'t using this computer\'s graphics card. Type chrome://settings/system into the address bar, turn on "Use graphics acceleration when available", then close {browser} completely and open it again. If it\'s already on, update the graphics driver.'), 'GPU-ACCEL-OFF',
          { browser: brandName() });
      // Windows on ARM (Snapdragon): WebGPU behind a flag in Chrome
      if (windows && await architecture() === 'arm')
        return fail(N('On Windows with an ARM chip (such as Snapdragon), Chrome keeps WebGPU off. Turn on chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu and restart Chrome.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-WIN-ARM');
      // Chrome on Linux runs WebGPU on Vulkan while the rest of it stays on OpenGL, so
      // chrome://gpu says WebGPU is on even when no Vulkan driver is installed
      if (linux) return fail(N('Chrome couldn\'t use this computer\'s graphics, most likely because the Vulkan driver is missing. Install it (mesa-vulkan-drivers on Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora) and restart Chrome. If chrome://gpu says WebGPU is disabled, also turn on chrome://flags/#enable-unsafe-webgpu.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-LINUX');
      // and on Windows on Direct3D 12 only: the D3D11 adapters are compatibility mode, blocklisted
      // (players took "needs DirectX 12" for a download, and kept trying on graphics that can never run it)
      if (windows) return fail(N('This computer\'s graphics are too old for the game: it needs graphics with DirectX 12 support, which older ones such as Intel HD 4000, 4400 and 4600 lack. Installing DirectX doesn\'t change that. If this computer has newer graphics, update their driver and restart Chrome.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER-WIN');
    }
    // macOS, ChromeOS, another browser: a crashed graphics process (a restart), or an old system
    const b = browserName();
    return fail(N('{Browser} couldn\'t use this computer\'s graphics. Restart {browser}; if that doesn\'t help, update {browser} and the system.'), 'GPU-ADAPTER',
      { browser: b, Browser: b === 'the browser' ? N('The browser') : b });
  }
  let info = ad.info ? [ad.info.vendor, ad.info.architecture, ad.info.description].filter(Boolean).join(' ') : '';
  const ffg = ff && windows && !info ? firefoxGraphics() : null;
  if (ffg) info = ffg.name;
  const named = info ? N('Graphics: {info}') : label;
  // the processor standing in for the graphics (Chrome's SwiftShader, Mesa's llvmpipe): what Chrome hands out with its
  // WebGPU flag where it can't use the graphics, as on a Steam Deck (Chrome on Linux with Vulkan off): the game runs
  // at ~13 fps.  That player's fix was Vulkan for Chrome and for ANGLE (the flags below, as in Chrome 156 on Linux)
  if (chromium && ((ad.info as { isFallbackAdapter?: boolean } | undefined)?.isFallbackAdapter || /swiftshader|llvmpipe|lavapipe|softpipe/i.test(info))) {
    return { ...check('gpu', named, 'warn', linux
      ? N('Chrome gave the game its software graphics, which run on the processor, so the game will be very slow. Turn on chrome://flags/#enable-vulkan and chrome://flags/#default-angle-vulkan, then restart Chrome.')
      : N('{browser} isn\'t using this computer\'s graphics card. Type chrome://settings/system into the address bar, turn on "Use graphics acceleration when available", then close {browser} completely and open it again. If it\'s already on, update the graphics driver.'),
    'GPU-SOFTWARE', { info, browser: brandName() }), adapter: info };
  }
  // no BC (PowerVR, Mali): the renderer unpacks the textures (web/src/gpu/dxt.ts), so it plays.  With ASTC (iPhones,
  // iPads, most phones) the most of them go up as ASTC instead (astc.ts): ~50 MB more, not 200, nothing to say
  if (!ad.features.has('texture-compression-bc') && !ad.features.has('texture-compression-astc')) {
    return { ...check('gpu', named, 'warn', N('This device can\'t read the game\'s packed textures, so the page unpacks them. The game runs fine but needs about 200 MB more memory, and loading screens may pause briefly.'), 'GPU-NO-BC', { info }), adapter: info };
  }
  if (ffg?.integrated) {
    return { ...check('gpu', named, 'warn', N('Firefox is using the processor\'s built-in graphics. If this computer has an NVIDIA or AMD card, set Firefox to High performance in Windows Settings, System, Display, Graphics, then restart Firefox.'), 'GPU-INTEGRATED-FIREFOX', { info }), adapter: info };
  }
  return { ...check('gpu', named, 'ok', N('Adapter with BC texture compression.'), undefined, { info }), adapter: info };
}

/** WebGL's renderer string (the unmasked one where the browser gives it), or null: no WebGL here */
function webglRenderer(): string | null {
  try {
    const gl = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl');
    if (!gl) return null;
    const ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
    const r = String(gl.getParameter(ext ? ext.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER));
    gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context')?.loseContext();
    return r;
  } catch { return null; }
}

/** the computer's CPU architecture ('arm', 'x86') from Chromium's User-Agent Client Hints, or null */
async function architecture(): Promise<string | null> {
  try { return (await (navigator as any).userAgentData?.getHighEntropyValues?.(['architecture']))?.architecture ?? null; }
  catch { return null; }
}

/**
 * Firefox on Windows: which graphics the game runs on.  Firefox gives WebGPU the adapter its
 * compositor draws the windows with, whatever powerPreference asks (gfx/wgpu_bindings server.rs:
 * the D3D12 adapter with the compositor's LUID), and its adapter.info is empty.  WebGL's renderer
 * string names the same graphics as a vendor and a class (dom/canvas/SanitizeRenderer.cpp): Intel's
 * integrated graphics become "Intel(R) HD Graphics[ 400]" (Arc cards "Intel(R) Arc(TM) A750
 * Graphics"), and the Ryzen APUs' unnumbered "AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics" "Radeon HD 3200 Graphics".
 * (Chrome does the same: powerPreference has no effect there either, per Chrome's troubleshooting
 * page, but its adapter.info names the graphics.)
 */
function firefoxGraphics(): { name: string; integrated: boolean } | null {
  const r = webglRenderer();
  if (r === null) return null;
  const vendor = /NVIDIA|GeForce|Quadro/.test(r) ? 'NVIDIA' : /Intel/.test(r) ? 'Intel' : /AMD|Radeon/.test(r) ? 'AMD' : null;
  if (!vendor) return null;
  const integrated = vendor === 'Intel' ? !/Arc/.test(r) : vendor === 'AMD' && /Radeon HD 3200/.test(r);
  return { name: `${vendor}${integrated ? ' (integrated)' : ''}`, integrated };
}

/**
 * Firefox asks the player before it keeps a site's data for good (a prompt by
 * the address bar), and persist() waits for the answer: the check does not.
 * It says so then, and `answer` is the check again once the player answered.
 * Without that promise the data stays until the disk is nearly full, which the
 * page cannot see: Chrome's estimate() tells such a site usage + 10 GiB (since
 * Chrome 133), whatever the disk has.  So that is no warning: backups are the
 * safety net (docs/web/PLAYING.md).
 */
export async function checkStorage(): Promise<Check & { answer?: Promise<Check> }> {
  const label = N('Browser storage');
  try { await navigator.storage.getDirectory(); }
  catch { return check('storage', label, 'fail', N('This window can\'t store files (a guest or private window?), so saves won\'t work.'), 'STORAGE-NONE'); }
  // the page writes files (createWritable: Safari has it from 26 on) at Play: the registry's first seed, settings.ini,
  // the cloud's saves.  Safari 18 with its WebGPU feature flag on passed every other check, then Play stopped with
  // "createWritable is not a function" (Discord 2026-11-02)
  if (typeof FileSystemFileHandle === 'undefined' || !('createWritable' in FileSystemFileHandle.prototype)) {
    return check('storage', label, 'fail', N('This browser is too old for the game: it needs iOS 26, iPadOS 26 or Safari 26. Update this device (Settings, General, Software Update).'), 'STORAGE-OLD');
  }
  const verdict = (persisted: boolean): Check => persisted
    ? check('storage', label, 'ok', N('Saves and cached game data are kept for good.'))
    : check('storage', label, 'ok', N('Saves and game data stay until the disk is nearly full, when {browser} may clear them.'), undefined, { browser: browserName() });
  const ask = (async () => await navigator.storage.persisted() || await navigator.storage.persist())()
    .catch(() => false);                 // not decisive
  const quick = await Promise.race([ask, new Promise<null>(res => setTimeout(() => res(null), 500))]);
  if (quick !== null) return verdict(quick);
  const b = browserName();
  return { ...check('storage', label, 'warn', N('{Browser} asks by the address bar to keep this site\'s data for good: allow it so your saves survive a full disk.'),
    'STORAGE-ASK', { Browser: b === 'the browser' ? N('The browser') : b }), answer: ask.then(verdict) };
}

export function fmtBytes(n: number): string {
  if (n >= 1e9) return `${(n / 1e9).toFixed(1)} GB`;
  if (n >= 1e6) return `${(n / 1e6).toFixed(n >= 1e8 ? 0 : 1)} MB`;
  if (n >= 1e3) return `${(n / 1e3).toFixed(0)} KB`;
  return `${n} bytes`;
}

// Claimed names on the start page (claim.ts): the line under Your name (the Online tab) with its Claim button, and
// what Play asks about the name (shell.ts settleName):
// - One name: a passphrase with a claimed name plays as that name, whatever Your name says (2026-11-05: a player who
//   typed another name after claiming played under one nobody held, which nobody could add as a friend, while the
//   friends lists went by the claim; the line only said the typed name was free).  Typing another name changes
//   nothing until Change name (once a week): Play never moves a claim, so nobody loses theirs by typing.
// - Your name: as typed, the line says what the name is to this player: free (Claim; without a keyphrase, Claim
//   turns cloud saves on first), claimed by this keyphrase (as long as it lasts), another player's (the digits it plays
//   under), NAME (the game's default, which nobody claims), or, with a claim, that the claimed name is the one played
//   (and Change name, once a week).  A claim runs Cloudflare's check in the row when the server asks for it.
// - Play: NAME asks once for a name of the player's own; a name another player claimed asks once (per name) for
//   another; either way the game plays under the name with this browser's four digits until then (with no claim of
//   its own).  A free name with a keyphrase but no claim yet is claimed as the game starts: Cloudflare's check shows
//   only when it wants a click.

import { dateLocale, t } from './i18n';
import { CLAIM_TRIED, localStore, NAME_ASKED, NAME_CLAIMED } from './prefs';

/** a day as the page writes dates: "26 Apr 2027" in the page's language */
export function day(ms: number): string {
  return new Date(ms).toLocaleDateString(dateLocale(), { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric' });
}

/** what a typed name is, before the server is asked: a line and its class, or null (ask the server) */
function local(typed: string): [string, string] | null {
  if (!onlineName(typed)) return [t('3 to 15 letters, digits, - or _.'), 'bad'];
  if (readsAsSlur(typed)) return [`${t('"{value}" is not a name (it reads as a slur)', { value: typed })}.`, 'bad'];
  return null;
}

/** a claim refused, as the line says it */
export function claimError(r: Extract<Claimed, { ok: false }>, name: string): string {
  switch (r.error) {
    case 'captcha': return t('Cloudflare\'s check did not pass. Try again.');
    case 'captcha-down': return t('Cloudflare\'s check could not be reached. Try again later.');
    case 'keyphrase': return t('Your cloud saves are not on the server yet. Try again in a moment.');
    case 'taken': return t('Another player claimed {name} just now.', { name });
    case 'soon': return t('You can change your name again on {date}.', { date: day(r.next ?? Date.now()) });
    case 'busy': return t('Too many claims from this network today. Try again tomorrow.');
    case 'default': return t('{name} is the game\'s default and can\'t be claimed. Pick your own.', { name });
    case 'blocked': return `${t('"{value}" is not a name (it reads as a slur)', { value: name })}.`;
    case 'invalid': return t('3 to 15 letters, digits, - or _.');
    default: return t('The server did not take the claim. Try again later.');
  }
}

export interface NameRowDeps {

/** The line under Your name, with its button; kept across the settings panel's re-renders (`attach` each time). */
export class NameRow {
  private info: NameInfo | null = null;
  /** the name (Online form) `info` is about, and its digits */
  private of = '';
  private alt = '';
  private claiming = false;
  /** a claim's own line (an error), until the name is typed again */
  private note: string | null = null;
  private seq = 0;
  private timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  private els: { input: HTMLInputElement; btn: HTMLButtonElement; line: HTMLParagraphElement; use: HTMLButtonElement } | null = null;
  /** the box's own placeholder (settings-ui's: the profile's name), shown again when there is no claimed name */
  private placeholder = '';
  /** Cloudflare's widget's box: one for every drawing of the row (the panel draws its rows again as settings change,
   *  turning cloud saves on among them, and a widget drawn into a box gone from the page never answers) */
  private readonly check = Object.assign(document.createElement('div'), { className: 'claim-check', hidden: true });

  /** the row settings-ui made: its text box and control */
  attach(row: HTMLElement, input: HTMLInputElement, ctl: HTMLElement) {
    const btn = Object.assign(document.createElement('button'), { type: 'button', className: 'btn', hidden: true });
    btn.onclick = () => void this.claim();
    ctl.append(btn);
    const line = Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'set-state free', id: 'set-roam_name-claim', hidden: true });
    line.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
    const use = Object.assign(document.createElement('button'), { type: 'button', className: 'text-btn', hidden: true });
    use.onclick = () => { input.value = this.alt; input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input')); input.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); };
    row.append(this.check, line);
    this.els = { input, btn, line, use };
    this.placeholder = input.placeholder;
    input.maxLength = 15;
    input.addEventListener('input', () => { this.note = null; clearTimeout(this.timer); this.timer = setTimeout(() => void this.ask(), 300); this.draw(); });
    this.draw();
    void this.ask();
  }

  /** the name the row is about: what is typed, else the profile's */
  private async typed(): Promise<string> {
    const v = this.els?.input.value.trim() ?? '';
    return v || (await this.d.profileName()) || '';
  }

  /** `typed` is not what Play plays: the passphrase here holds another name (the last one heard of; the line under
   *  the box says so) */
  notPlayed(typed: string | null): boolean {
    const mine = this.info?.mine, name = typed ? onlineName(typed) : null;
    return !!mine && this.d.linked() && !!name && name.toLowerCase() !== mine.name.toLowerCase();
  }

  /** the server asked about the name typed (or the profile's); with a passphrase here, also with none to ask about
   *  (an empty box and no profile, a name the page refuses): its claimed name is the one played all the same */
  async ask() {
    const typed = await this.typed();
    const name = onlineName(typed);
    const n = ++this.seq;
    const ok = !!name && !local(typed);
    if (!ok && !this.d.linked()) { this.of = name ?? ''; this.info = null; this.draw(); return; }

    const info = await this.d.claims.check(ok ? name! : '', alt || undefined);
    if (n !== this.seq) return;
    this.of = ok ? name! : ''; this.alt = alt; this.info = info;
    this.d.kept(info?.mine?.name ?? null);
    this.draw();
  }

    const e = this.els;
    if (!e) return;
    const { btn, line, use } = e;
    const check = this.check;
    const show = (text: string | null, cls = 'free', button: string | null = null, offer: string | null = null) => {
      line.hidden = !text;
      line.textContent = text ?? '';
      line.className = `set-state ${cls}`;
      btn.hidden = !button;
      btn.textContent = button ?? '';
      btn.disabled = this.claiming || !this.d.writable();
      use.hidden = !offer;
      if (offer) { use.textContent = t('Use {name}', { name: offer }); line.append(' ', use); }
    };
    check.hidden = !this.claiming;
    if (this.claiming) return show(t('A quick check that you\'re human. Once per name.'), 'free', t('Claiming'));
    const typed = e.input.value.trim();
    const bad = typed ? local(typed) : null;
    if (bad) return show(bad[0], bad[1]);
    if (this.note) return show(this.note, 'bad');
    const i = this.info, mine = i?.mine;
    // an empty box plays as the claimed name: it shows there
    e.input.placeholder = mine?.name ?? this.placeholder;
    if (!i || this.d.claims.here === false) return show(null);
    if (mine && !typed) return show(t('Claimed with your passphrase. It stays yours as long as the passphrase does.'), 'ok');
    if (onlineName(typed || this.of) !== this.of) return show(null);
    const name = i.name ?? this.of;
    // one name (the module's doc): another name typed is not played until Change name
    if (mine && i.state !== 'yours') {
      const claimed = mine.name, soon = mine.next > Date.now();
      switch (i.state) {
        case 'free':
          if (soon) return show(t('You play as {claimed}, your claimed name. You can change it to {name} on {date}.', { claimed, name, date: day(mine.next) }), 'env');
          return show(t('You play as {claimed}, your claimed name. To play as {name}, press Change name: your friends move with you, and {claimed} stays yours for {n} days. One change a week.', { claimed, name, n: GRACE_DAYS }), 'env', t('Change name'));
        case 'old':
          return show(t('You play as {claimed}, your claimed name. {name} was yours before: yours until {date}.', { claimed, name, date: day(i.until ?? 0) }), 'env', soon ? null : t('Change name'));
        case 'taken':
          return show(t('Another player claimed {name}. You play as {claimed}, your claimed name.', { claimed, name }), 'env');
        default:
          return show(t('You play as {claimed}, your claimed name.', { claimed }), 'env');
      }
    }
    switch (i.state) {
      case 'default':
        return show(t('{name} is the game\'s default and can\'t be claimed. Pick your own.', { name }), 'env', null, this.alt);
      case 'yours':
        return show(t('Claimed with your passphrase. It stays yours as long as the passphrase does.'), 'ok');
      case 'old':
        return show(t('{name} was your name before your change: yours until {date}.', { name, date: day(i.until ?? 0) }), 'ok');
      case 'taken':
        // with a passphrase here, entering one is no way back to it: that one is another (2026-11-02, a player's
        // report: told to enter the passphrase this browser already had)
        if (this.d.linked()) return show(t('Another passphrase claimed {name}, not the one this browser syncs with, so you play as {alt}. Pick another name.', { name, alt: this.alt }), 'bad', null, this.alt);
        return show(t('Another player claimed {name}, so you play as {alt}. Pick another name, or if it\'s yours, enter your passphrase under Cloud saves.', { name, alt: this.alt }), 'bad', null, this.alt);
      case 'free':
        if (!this.d.linked()) return show(t('Not claimed: anyone can play as {name}. Claiming makes you an 8-word passphrase that holds the name and your cloud saves.', { name }), 'free', t('Claim'));
        return show(t('Not claimed yet. Your passphrase claims it the next time you play with others.'), 'free', t('Claim'));
      default:
        return show(null);
    }
  }

  /** Claim (or Change name): cloud saves first when there is no keyphrase (the keyphrase shown to keep after the
   *  claim, for the name too), Cloudflare's check when the server asks */
  private async claim() {
    if (!this.els || this.claiming || !this.d.writable()) return;
    const name = onlineName(await this.typed());
    if (!name) return;
    const phrase = this.d.linked() ? null : await this.made();
    if (phrase === undefined) return;
    if (phrase && this.info?.state !== 'free') {
      await this.d.showPassphrase(phrase, null, this.info?.state === 'taken' ? this.info.name ?? name : null);
      return;
    }
    const r = await this.claimNow(name);
    if (phrase) await this.d.showPassphrase(phrase, r.claimed, r.taken ? name : null);
  }

  /** a keyphrase made for the claim (cloud saves on), the name asked about again; undefined: none */
  private async made(): Promise<string | undefined> {
    this.d.log('[app] claim: cloud saves first (no keyphrase here)');
    const phrase = await this.d.enable();
    if (!phrase) return undefined;
    await this.ask();
    return phrase;
  }

  /** the claim itself: the name claimed, or null (the line says why); taken: another player's claim came first */
  private async claimNow(name: string): Promise<{ claimed: string | null; taken: boolean }> {
    this.claiming = true; this.note = null; this.draw();
    let captcha: string | null = null;
    if (this.info?.captcha) {
      this.check.replaceChildren();
      captcha = await turnstile(this.info.captcha, this.check);
      if (!captcha) { this.claiming = false; this.note = t('Cloudflare\'s check did not pass. Try again.'); this.draw(); return { claimed: null, taken: false }; }
    }
    const r = await this.d.claims.claim(name, captcha);
    this.claiming = false;
    if (r.ok) {
      this.d.log('[app] claim: your name claimed with this browser\'s keyphrase');
      if (this.els?.input.value.trim() !== r.mine.name) await this.d.save(r.mine.name);
      this.d.say(t('Claimed: {name}.', { name: r.mine.name }));
      await this.ask();
      return { claimed: r.mine.name, taken: false };
    }
    this.d.log(`[app] claim: your name not claimed (${r.error})`);
    this.note = claimError(r, name);
    this.draw();
    return { claimed: null, taken: r.error === 'taken' };
  }
}

export interface PlayNameDeps {
  claims: NameClaims;
  seed(): string;
  linked(): boolean;
  /** the page's question box: 'ok', 'cancel' or '' (Esc) */
  choose(title: string, body: Node, ok: string, cancel: string): Promise<string>;
  save(name: string): Promise<void>;
  log(s: string): void;
  /** the passphrase's claimed name as the page last heard it (the line under Your name), for a Play the server does
   *  not answer: null, none known */
  claimed?(): string | null;
}

/** the question under key k was asked in this browser (storage off: asked again) */
const asked = (k: string) => localStore.get(k) === '1';
const ask = (k: string) => localStore.set(k, '1');
const para = (text: string) => Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { textContent: text });

/**
 * The name this game plays under, by the claims: `typed` is Your name, or the profile's.  null: as it is (no claims
 * on this server, no answer, or nothing to change).  A passphrase with a claimed name plays as that name, whatever is
 * typed (one name: the module's doc; the claim never moves here).  Else NAME and a name another player claimed play
 * under this browser's digits, after a question the first time (per save folder for NAME, per name for a claimed
 * one); a free name with a keyphrase here is claimed (`quiet`: Cloudflare's check where it wants a click).
 */
export async function settleName(d: PlayNameDeps, typed: string, saveDir: string, quiet: (name: string, site: string) => Promise<string | null>): Promise<string | null> {
  const name = onlineName(typed);
  const linked = d.linked();
  const ok = !!name && !readsAsSlur(typed);
  if (!ok && !linked) return null;
  const alt = ok ? await digitsFor(name!, d.seed()) : '';
  const info = await d.claims.check(ok ? name! : '', alt || undefined);
  const known = linked ? d.claimed?.() ?? null : null;
  if (!info) {
    if (known) d.log('[app] your name: no answer about it: your claimed name as heard before');
    return known && !(name && name.toLowerCase() === known.toLowerCase()) ? known : null;
  }
  if (linked && info.mine) {
    // (the claimed name in the case typed, if that is all that differs)
    const same = ok && name!.toLowerCase() === info.mine.name.toLowerCase();
    d.log(`[app] your name: your claimed name${same ? '' : ' (Your name says another: it is played only after Change name)'}`);
    return same ? name! : info.mine.name;
  }
  if (!ok) return null;
  d.log(`[app] your name: ${info.state === 'yours' || info.state === 'old' ? 'claimed with this browser\'s keyphrase'
    : info.state === 'taken' ? `claimed by another player (${linked ? 'with another passphrase than this browser\'s' : 'no passphrase here'})` : info.state}`);
  switch (info.state) {
    case 'yours':
    case 'old':
      return name;
    case 'default': {
      const k = NAME_ASKED + saveDir;
      if (asked(k)) return alt;
      ask(k);
      return await pick(d, t('Pick your name'),
        [para(t('Other players see your name over your car. {name} is the game\'s default, so pick your own.', { name }))], alt, quiet) ?? alt;
    }
    case 'taken': {
      const k = NAME_CLAIMED + name.toLowerCase();
      if (asked(k)) return alt;
      ask(k);
      return await pick(d, t('{name} is claimed', { name }),
        [para(t('Another player claimed {name}. Pick another, or play as {alt} this time.', { name, alt }))], alt, quiet,
        para(linked ? t('This browser\'s passphrase did not claim {name}: another one did, first.', { name })
          : t('Is {name} yours? Enter your passphrase under Cloud saves to get it back here.', { name }))) ?? alt;
    }
    case 'free':
      if (linked && !info.mine) await claimQuietly(d, name, info, quiet);
      return name;
    default:
      return null;
  }
}

/** after a claim at Play that did not go through (the check failed, Not now, a refusal), Play tries again only this
 *  much later: a check that hangs costs its 15 s once, a player who said Not now is not asked at every Play; Claim
 *  under Your name works any time */
const RETRY_MS = 7 * 86_400_000;

/** a free name claimed at Play, Cloudflare's check quiet unless it wants a click */
export async function claimQuietly(d: PlayNameDeps, name: string, info: NameInfo, quiet: (name: string, site: string) => Promise<string | null>): Promise<Mine | null> {
  const k = CLAIM_TRIED + name.toLowerCase();
  if (Date.now() - Number(localStore.get(k) ?? 0) < RETRY_MS) return null;      // (storage off: tried)
  const later = () => localStore.set(k, String(Date.now()));
  const captcha = info.captcha ? await quiet(name, info.captcha) : null;
  if (info.captcha && !captcha) { d.log('[app] claim at Play: Cloudflare\'s check did not pass (not claimed; Play tries again in a week)'); later(); return null; }
  const r = await d.claims.claim(name, captcha);
  d.log(r.ok ? '[app] claim at Play: your name claimed with this browser\'s keyphrase' : `[app] claim at Play: not claimed (${r.error}; Play tries again in a week)`);
  if (!r.ok) later();
  return r.ok ? r.mine : null;
}

/** a question for a name of the player's own: the box (filled with `alt`) checked as it is typed; the name, or null */
async function pick(d: PlayNameDeps, title: string, before: Node[], alt: string, quiet: (name: string, site: string) => Promise<string | null>, after?: Node): Promise<string | null> {
  const body = document.createElement('div');
  const row = document.createElement('p'); row.className = 'dlg-field';
  const label = Object.assign(document.createElement('label'), { className: 'set-label', htmlFor: 'claim-ask-name', textContent: t('Your name') });
  const f = Object.assign(document.createElement('input'), { type: 'text', id: 'claim-ask-name', value: alt, maxLength: 15, autocomplete: 'off', spellcheck: false });
  row.append(label, f);
  const line = Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'hint claim-line' });
  line.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
  body.append(...before, row, line);
  if (after) body.append(after);
  const got: { info: NameInfo | null } = { info: null };
  let seq = 0;
  const check = async () => {
    const n = ++seq, typed = f.value.trim(), bad = local(typed);
    if (bad) { line.textContent = bad[0]; line.dataset.state = 'bad'; f.setCustomValidity(bad[0]); return; }
    const name = onlineName(typed)!;
    const i = await d.claims.check(name);
    if (n !== seq) return;
    got.info = i;
    const [text, state] = !i ? ['', ''] : i.state === 'taken' ? [t('Another player claimed {name}.', { name }), 'bad']
      : i.state === 'blocked' ? [t('{name} isn\'t allowed here.', { name }), 'bad']
      : i.state === 'default' ? [t('{name} is the game\'s default and can\'t be claimed. Pick your own.', { name }), 'env']
      : i.state === 'yours' || i.state === 'old' ? [t('{name} is yours.', { name }), 'ok'] : [t('{name} is free.', { name }), 'free'];
    line.textContent = text; line.dataset.state = state;
    f.setCustomValidity(state === 'bad' || state === 'env' ? text : '');
  };
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  f.oninput = () => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => void check(), 250); };
  void check();
  const answer = d.choose(title, body, t('Use this name'), t('Not now'));
  f.focus(); f.select();
  const how = await answer;
  if (how !== 'ok') { d.log('[app] your name: not now (plays with this browser\'s digits)'); return null; }
  await check();
  const name = onlineName(f.value.trim());
  const info = got.info;
  if (!name || local(f.value.trim()) || !info || info.state === 'taken' || info.state === 'default' || info.state === 'blocked') return null;
  await d.save(name);
  d.log('[app] your name: one of the player\'s own picked at Play');
  if (info.state === 'free' && d.linked() && !info.mine) await claimQuietly(d, name, info, quiet);
  return name;
}

/**
 * The server's operator took the player's name away (net/index.ts onRename: `was`, with the operator's `msg`): a
 * question for another, the box empty and checked as it is typed (a name another player claimed, or one the server
 * does not allow, will not do; a server without claims asks nothing).  The name picked, saved as Your name; null: Not
 * now.  seat2: co-op player 2's name was taken (the box says so; the name is player 2's, for this game only, not saved).
 */
export async function renamePick(d: PlayNameDeps, was: string, msg: string, seat2 = false): Promise<string | null> {
  const body = document.createElement('div');
  body.append(para(t('{name} isn\'t allowed here.', { name: was })));
  if (msg) body.append(para(msg));
  const row = document.createElement('p'); row.className = 'dlg-field';
  const label = Object.assign(document.createElement('label'), { className: 'set-label', htmlFor: 'rename-ask-name', textContent: seat2 ? t('Player 2\'s name') : t('Your name') });
  const f = Object.assign(document.createElement('input'), { type: 'text', id: 'rename-ask-name', maxLength: 15, autocomplete: 'off', spellcheck: false });
  row.append(label, f);
  const line = Object.assign(document.createElement('p'), { className: 'hint claim-line' });
  line.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');
  body.append(row, line);
  const same = (a: string, b: string) => onlineName(a)?.toLowerCase() === onlineName(b)?.toLowerCase();
  let seq = 0, good = false;
  const check = async () => {
    const n = ++seq, typed = f.value.trim();
    good = false;
    const bad = !typed ? [t('Pick another name to keep playing with others.'), 'env'] : local(typed)
      ?? (same(typed, was) ? [t('{name} isn\'t allowed here.', { name: onlineName(typed)! }), 'bad'] : null);
    if (bad) { line.textContent = bad[0]; line.dataset.state = bad[1]; f.setCustomValidity(bad[0]); return; }
    const name = onlineName(typed)!;
    const i = await d.claims.check(name);
    if (n !== seq) return;
    const [text, state] = !i ? ['', ''] : i.state === 'taken' ? [t('Another player claimed {name}.', { name }), 'bad']
      : i.state === 'blocked' ? [t('{name} isn\'t allowed here.', { name }), 'bad']
      : i.state === 'default' ? [t('{name} is the game\'s default and can\'t be claimed. Pick your own.', { name }), 'bad']
      : i.state === 'yours' || i.state === 'old' ? [t('{name} is yours.', { name }), 'ok'] : [t('{name} is free.', { name }), 'free'];
    line.textContent = text; line.dataset.state = state;
    f.setCustomValidity(state === 'bad' ? text : '');
    good = state !== 'bad';
  };
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  f.oninput = () => { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => void check(), 250); };
  void check();
  const answer = d.choose(t('Pick another name'), body, t('Use this name'), t('Not now'));
  f.focus();
  if (await answer !== 'ok') return null;
  await check();
  const name = onlineName(f.value.trim());
  if (!name || !good) return null;
  if (!seat2) await d.save(name);
  return name;
}

/** Cloudflare's check for claiming `name` at Play: its dialog (#claim-check) stays out of sight unless the check
 *  wants a click; 15 s without an answer or a click, or Not now: no claim this time */
export async function quietCheck(name: string, site: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const dlg = document.querySelector<HTMLDialogElement>('#claim-check');
  if (!dlg) return null;
  dlg.querySelector('h2')!.textContent = t('Claiming {name}', { name });
  dlg.querySelector('.claim-about')!.textContent = t('A quick check that you\'re human. Once per name.');
  const box = dlg.querySelector<HTMLDivElement>('.claim-check')!;
  const no = dlg.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.claim-no')!;
  no.textContent = t('Not now');
  const stop = new AbortController();
  no.onclick = () => stop.abort();
  dlg.oncancel = e => { e.preventDefault(); stop.abort(); };
  dlg.classList.add('quiet');
  dlg.showModal();
  let shown = false;
  const timer = setTimeout(() => { if (!shown) stop.abort(); }, 15_000);
  const token = await turnstile(site, box, { quiet: true, stop: stop.signal, asks: () => { shown = true; dlg.classList.remove('quiet'); no.focus(); } });
  clearTimeout(timer);
  dlg.close();
  box.replaceChildren();
  return token;
}

// Claimed names (docs/web/PLAYING.md, Your name): a player claims the name it plays under with its keyphrase (the
// one that keeps its cloud saves), and while the claim holds nobody else plays under that name.  The server keeps
// the claims and checks them where names are used (web/server-rs/crates/claims; /names, the Online lobby, free
// roam's hub); this is the page's side of it:
// - onlineName: the Online form of a name (runtime/online.c clean(), nfsu2-claims clean()), which both the Online
//   menu and free roam use, and by which names are compared, in any case;
// - digitsFor: the name with four digits in place of its end, the same ones for this browser and name: what the page
//   plays under when another player claimed the name, or for NAME, the game's default that nobody claims;
// - NameClaims: /names, asked with the keyphrase's token (never the keyphrase): what a name is to this player, and
//   the claim itself, with Cloudflare Turnstile's answer when the server asks for its check (turnstile below).

import { blockedName } from './names.mjs';

/** the name before a change stays the player's this long (GRACE_DAYS) */
export const GRACE_DAYS = 14;
/** the game's names for nobody in particular, which nobody claims (lower case) */
export const UNCLAIMABLE = ['name', 'player'];

/** The Online form of a name: the letters, digits, - and _, any other run of characters one _ (none at either end),
 *  cut to 15; one or two characters padded with _.  null: nothing of a name in it. */
export function onlineName(s: string): string | null {
  let out = '', gap = false;
  for (const ch of s) {
    if (out.length >= 15) break;
    if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]$/.test(ch)) { gap = true; continue; }
    if (gap && out && out.length < 14) out += '_';
    gap = false;
    out += ch;
  }
  if (!out) return null;
  while (out.length < 3) out += '_';
  return out;
}

/** the name as typed or its Online form reads as a slur (the server's nfsu2-claims reads_as_slur) */
export function readsAsSlur(typed: string): boolean {
  const o = onlineName(typed);
  return blockedName(typed) || (o !== null && blockedName(o));
}

/** The name with four digits in place of its end, the same ones for one seed (this browser's id) and name;
 *  "Player" with the digits where the shortened name reads as a slur (as nfsu2-online free_variant). */
export async function digitsFor(name: string, seed: string): Promise<string> {
  const base = onlineName(name) ?? 'Player';
  const h = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(`${seed}\n${base.toLowerCase()}`)));
  const d = String(((h[0] << 24 | h[1] << 16 | h[2] << 8 | h[3]) >>> 0) % 9000 + 1000);
  const cut = base.slice(0, 11) + d;
  return blockedName(cut) ? `Player${d}` : cut;
}

export type NameState = 'free' | 'yours' | 'old' | 'taken' | 'default' | 'blocked' | 'invalid';
export interface Mine { name: string; until: number; next: number }
/** what a name is to this player (GET /names) */
export interface NameInfo {
  name: string | null;
  state: NameState;
  /** yours, old: until when */
  until?: number;
  /** the second name asked about (the page's digits) */
  alt?: NameInfo;
  /** the keyphrase's own name */
  mine?: Mine;
  /** Cloudflare Turnstile's site key: a claim needs its check */
  captcha?: string;
}
export type ClaimError = 'captcha' | 'captcha-down' | 'keyphrase' | 'invalid' | 'default' | 'blocked' | 'taken' | 'soon' | 'full' | 'busy' | 'net';
export type Claimed = { ok: true; mine: Mine } | { ok: false; error: ClaimError; next?: number };

type Fetch = (url: string, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;

/** /names for this player: `token()` is its keyphrase's (null: it has none) */
export class NameClaims {
  /** the server keeps claims: unknown until it answered once */
  here: boolean | null = null;
  constructor(private token: () => Promise<string | null>, private f: Fetch = (u, i) => fetch(u, i)) {}

  private async headers(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
    const t = await this.token().catch(() => null);
    return t ? { authorization: `Bearer ${t}` } : {};
  }

  /** what `name` (and `alt`) is to this player; null: no answer, or a server without claims */
  async check(name: string, alt?: string): Promise<NameInfo | null> {
    const u = new URLSearchParams({ name });
    if (alt) u.set('alt', alt);
    try {
      const r = await this.f(`/names?${u}`, { headers: await this.headers(), cache: 'no-store', signal: AbortSignal.timeout(8000) });
      if (r.status === 404) { this.here = false; return null; }
      if (!r.ok) return null;
      this.here = true;
      const info = await r.json() as NameInfo & { mine?: Mine & { blocked?: boolean } };
      // (a claim on a name the operator took away from someone that reads the same: not played, and the next claim is
      // a change of it)
      if (info.mine?.blocked) delete info.mine;
      return info;
    } catch { return null; }
  }

  /** this player's keyphrase claims `name` (a change when it had another), with Turnstile's answer when asked for */
  async claim(name: string, captcha: string | null): Promise<Claimed> {
    try {
      const r = await this.f('/names', {
        method: 'POST', headers: { ...await this.headers(), 'content-type': 'application/json' }, cache: 'no-store',
        body: JSON.stringify({ name, ...(captcha ? { captcha } : {}) }), signal: AbortSignal.timeout(20_000),
      });
      const j = await r.json().catch(() => ({})) as { mine?: Mine; error?: ClaimError; next?: number };
      if (r.ok && j.mine) return { ok: true, mine: j.mine };
      if (r.status === 429 && !j.error) return { ok: false, error: 'busy' };
      return { ok: false, error: j.error ?? 'net', ...(j.next ? { next: j.next } : {}) };
    } catch { return { ok: false, error: 'net' }; }
  }
}

// ---- Cloudflare Turnstile ----

interface TurnstileApi {
  render(el: HTMLElement, o: Record<string, unknown>): string;
  remove(id: string): void;
}
let script: Promise<TurnstileApi> | null = null;

function load(): Promise<TurnstileApi> {
  script ??= new Promise<TurnstileApi>((ok, no) => {
    const s = document.createElement('script');
    s.src = 'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit';
    s.onload = () => { const ts = (window as unknown as { turnstile?: TurnstileApi }).turnstile; if (ts) ok(ts); else no(new Error('no turnstile')); };
    s.onerror = () => { s.remove(); no(new Error('the script did not load')); };
    document.head.append(s);
  }).catch(e => { script = null; throw e; });
  return script;
}

/**
 * Turnstile's widget for `siteKey` in `box`: its answer once it passed, null when it failed, timed out (`ms`) or was
 * stopped (`stop`).  `quiet`: the widget shows only when it wants a click (`asks` then says so); else always.
 */
export async function turnstile(siteKey: string, box: HTMLElement, o: { quiet?: boolean; asks?: () => void; stop?: AbortSignal; ms?: number } = {}): Promise<string | null> {
  let ts: TurnstileApi;
  try { ts = await load(); } catch { return null; }
  return new Promise<string | null>(done => {
    let id = '';
    const end = (v: string | null) => { clearTimeout(timer); try { if (id) ts.remove(id); } catch { /* gone */ } done(v); };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => end(null), o.ms ?? 120_000);
    o.stop?.addEventListener('abort', () => end(null), { once: true });
    try {
      id = ts.render(box, {
        sitekey: siteKey, action: 'claim', theme: 'dark', size: 'flexible',
        appearance: o.quiet ? 'interaction-only' : 'always',
        callback: (token: string) => end(token),
        'error-callback': () => end(null),
        'expired-callback': () => end(null),
        'before-interactive-callback': () => o.asks?.(),
      });

// Two pictures of one moment to compare: the second over the first from a line the player drags (or moves with the
// arrow keys), as Play's Full Scene Anti-Aliasing question shows the car's edges off and on (shell.ts askFsaa).  The
// line's place is a CSS variable set through the CSSOM: the page's CSP takes no inline style attributes.

/** a picture pair shown: its element, and dispose() for the object URLs once it is gone */
export interface Compare { el: HTMLElement; dispose(): void }

/** two pictures of the server's game folder (it sends its files as bytes, whatever their names: given `type` here), or
 *  null when either is missing, unreadable, or the server does not answer in `ms` (offline, a server without them) */
export async function fetchPair(a: string, b: string, type: string, ms = 3000): Promise<[Blob, Blob] | null> {
  const ctl = new AbortController(), timer = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), ms);
  const one = async (url: string) => {
    const r = await fetch(url, { signal: ctl.signal });
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${r.status}`);
    return new Blob([await r.arrayBuffer()], { type });
  };
  try { return await Promise.all([one(a), one(b)]); } catch { return null; } finally { clearTimeout(timer); }
}

/** the pair, `before` on the left of the line and `after` on its right, the line in the middle */
export function compare(before: Blob, after: Blob, text: { before: string; after: string; drag: string }): Compare {
  const urls = [URL.createObjectURL(before), URL.createObjectURL(after)];
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.className = 'compare';
  const img = (src: string, cls: string) => Object.assign(document.createElement('img'), { src, alt: '', className: cls, draggable: false });
  const tag = (s: string, cls: string) => Object.assign(document.createElement('span'), { textContent: s, className: `compare-tag ${cls}` });
  const split = Object.assign(document.createElement('span'), { className: 'compare-split' });
  const range = Object.assign(document.createElement('input'), { type: 'range', min: '0', max: '100', value: '50' });
  range.setAttribute('aria-label', text.drag);
  const place = () => el.style.setProperty('--x', `${range.value}%`);
  range.addEventListener('input', place);
  place();
  el.append(img(urls[0], 'compare-before'), img(urls[1], 'compare-after'), split, tag(text.before, 'before'), tag(text.after, 'after'), range);
  return { el, dispose: () => { for (const u of urls) URL.revokeObjectURL(u); } };
}

/** what the drawing says, for a screen reader */
function spoken(f: Family): string {
  const say = (r: Row) => r.say?.[f === 'xb' ? 0 : 1] ?? (SPOKEN[r[f]] ? t(SPOKEN[r[f]]) : r[f]);
  const low = (s: string) => language() === 'english' ? s.toLowerCase() : s;
  return t('Controller: {list}', { list: [...LEFT, ...MIDDLE, ...RIGHT].map(r => `${say(r)}: ${low(doesOf(r))}${subOf(r) ? `, ${t(subOf(r)!)}` : ''}`).join('; ') });
}

function padSvg(): string {
  let s = drawing();
  const does = (r: Row) => esc(doesOf(r));
  for (const r of LEFT) {
    const x = 86 - chipW(r);
    s += chip(x, r) + `<text class="pad-label" x="${x - 5}" y="${r.y + 4}" text-anchor="end">${does(r)}</text>`;
    const sub = subOf(r);
    if (sub) s += `<text class="pad-sub" x="${x - 5}" y="${r.y + 18}" text-anchor="end">${esc(t(sub))}</text>`;
    if (r.to) s += line(89, r.y, r.to);
  }
  for (const r of RIGHT) {
    s += chip(248, r) + `<text class="pad-label" x="${248 + chipW(r) + 5}" y="${r.y + 4}">${does(r)}</text>`;
    // a second line under the last row, ending at the drawing's edge: there is room below the grip, not beside it
    const sub = subOf(r);
    if (sub) s += `<text class="pad-sub" x="335" y="${r.y + 16}" text-anchor="end">${esc(t(sub))}</text>`;
    if (r.to) s += line(245, r.y, r.to);
  }
  for (const [i, r] of MIDDLE.entries()) {
    s += chip(r.x, r) + (i === 0 ? `<text class="pad-label" x="${r.x - 5}" y="${r.y + 4}" text-anchor="end">${does(r)}</text>`
      : `<text class="pad-label" x="${r.x + 19}" y="${r.y + 4}">${does(r)}</text>`);
    s += line(r.x + 7, r.y + 7.5, r.to!);
  }
  for (const b of BRACKETS) s += `<path class="pad-line" d="M${b.x} ${b.y0}V${b.y1}"/>` + line(b.x, b.from, b.to);
  return `<svg class="pad" viewBox="0 0 336 154" role="img" aria-label="${esc(spoken('xb'))}">${s}</svg>`;
}

/** a key cap with the button's Xbox and PlayStation names */
function cap(xb: string, ps: string): string {
  const one = (v: string) => v in SHAPE ? `<svg class="glyph" viewBox="0 0 14 14" role="img" aria-label="${esc(t(SPOKEN[v]))}">${SHAPE[v]}</svg>` : v;
  return `<kbd><span class="xb">${one(xb)}</span><span class="ps">${one(ps)}</span></kbd>`;
}

/** relabel: drawn again in the page's language (i18n.ts onLanguage) */
export interface ControlsSheet { show(tab: Tab, focus?: boolean): void; family(f: Family): void; relabel(): void; readonly tab: Tab; readonly fam: Family }

/**
 * Wires the sheet in root (its tabs and their panels in the page's markup; the controller's tab is drawn here):
 * id prefixes the ids the tabs and panels get, so the page's sheet and its copy in the dialog differ.  follow: a
 * controller connecting shows its tab, unless the player picked one, and its family's names.
 */
export function controlsSheet(root: HTMLElement, id: string, opts: { tab?: Tab; fam?: Family; follow?: boolean } = {}): ControlsSheet {
  const tabs = [...root.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('[role="tab"]')];
  const panels = [...root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[role="tabpanel"]')];
  for (const p of panels) {
    p.id = `${id}-${p.dataset.tab}`;
    p.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', `${id}-tab-${p.dataset.tab}`);
  }
  for (const t of tabs) { t.id = `${id}-tab-${t.dataset.tab}`; t.setAttribute('aria-controls', `${id}-${t.dataset.tab}`); }
  const pad = panels.find(p => p.dataset.tab === 'pad')!;
  const wheel = wheelSection(pad, cap);
  let svg: SVGElement, radios: HTMLInputElement[] = [];
  /** the drawing and its foot, in the page's language; the wheel's part after them, then what the page keeps there
   *  (data-keep: the start page's Controller settings, settings-ui.ts) */
  const kept = [...pad.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [data-keep]')];
  const draw = () => {
    const menus = esc(t('In menus: D-pad and {a}, {b} goes back.')).replace('{a}', cap('A', 'cross')).replace('{b}', cap('B', 'circle'));
    const hold = siteButton('button_hold'), look = siteButton('button_look');   // (the player's: sitekeys.ts)
    pad.innerHTML = padSvg() + `<div class="pad-foot">
    <p class="hint">${menus}</p>
    ${hold === 'off' ? '' : `<p class="hint">${esc(t('Parked in free roam: hold {button} to open hood, then trunk, then doors, then all.', { button: buttonName(hold) }))}</p>`}
    ${look === 'off' ? '' : `<p class="hint">${esc(t('Right stick up: headlights off or on; hold it for high beam.'))}</p>`}
    <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label="${esc(t('Button names'))}">
      <label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="${id}-fam" value="xb">Xbox</label>
      <label class="opt"><input type="radio" name="${id}-fam" value="ps">PlayStation</label>
    </div>
    ${steamPadsPossible() ? '<p class="hint steam-state"></p><div class="row"><button type="button" class="btn" data-steam></button></div>' : ''}
    </div>`;
    pad.append(wheel.box, ...kept);
    svg = pad.querySelector('svg')!;
    radios = [...pad.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>('.pad-foot input[type="radio"]')];
    for (const r of radios) r.onchange = () => { if (r.checked) sheet.family(r.value as Family); };
    steamPart();
    wheel.relabel();
    requestAnimationFrame(fit);
  };
  /** Valve's controllers under the drawing, where the browser can read them (steampad.ts: WebHID, Chrome and Edge on a
   *  computer): those connected in this browser, and the button that opens the browser's list of them (it opens only
   *  from a click; the one picked works at once in a running game, else from Play, and on later visits too) */
  const steamPart = () => {
    const btn = pad.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('[data-steam]'), state = pad.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.steam-state');
    if (!btn || !state) return;
    const show = (names: string[]) => {
      state.textContent = names.length ? t('{names}: connected in this browser.', { names: names.join(', ') })
        : t('Steam Controller or Steam Deck: connect it once.');
      btn.textContent = names.length ? t('Connect another') : t('Connect a Steam Controller');
    };
    show([]);
    void steamPadsPicked().then(show);
    btn.onclick = () => connectSteamPad().then(() => steamPadsPicked()).then(show, () => {});
  };
  /** a label too long for the drawing (another language's words) a little smaller, so it stays inside the 336 px;
   *  measured once the tab shows (a hidden one has no size).  Measured again after each change: a renderer that draws
   *  at a rounded size keeps the width for a while as the size goes down (Chromium on Linux draws a Japanese label
   *  63 units wide at 10.5 px and at 10 px), so one step in proportion can leave it past the drawing's edge; while it
   *  is (the first step aims 1 unit inside), the next steps take at least 3 % off.  Where the width follows the size,
   *  the first step fits and nothing changes. */
  const fit = () => {
    if (pad.hidden) return;
    for (const el of svg.querySelectorAll<SVGTextElement>('.pad-label, .pad-sub')) {
      el.style.fontSize = '';
      for (let step = 0; step < 8; step++) {
        const b = el.getBBox(), over = Math.max(1 - b.x, b.x + b.width - 335);
        if (!b.width || over <= (step ? 1 : 0)) break;
        el.style.fontSize = `${parseFloat(getComputedStyle(el).fontSize) * Math.min((b.width - over) / b.width, step ? 0.97 : 1)}px`;
      }
    }
  };

  let tab: Tab = opts.tab ?? 'keys', fam: Family = opts.fam ?? 'xb', picked = false;
  const sheet: ControlsSheet = {
    get tab() { return tab; },
    get fam() { return fam; },
    show(t, focus) {
      tab = t;
      for (const b of tabs) { const on = b.dataset.tab === t; b.setAttribute('aria-selected', String(on)); b.tabIndex = on ? 0 : -1; if (on && focus) b.focus(); }
      for (const p of panels) p.hidden = p.dataset.tab !== t;
      if (t === 'pad') requestAnimationFrame(fit);
    },
    family(f) {
      fam = f;
      root.dataset.fam = f;
      svg.setAttribute('aria-label', spoken(f));
      for (const r of radios) r.checked = r.value === f;
    },
    relabel() { draw(); sheet.family(fam); },
  };
  draw();
  for (const b of tabs) b.onclick = () => { picked = true; sheet.show(b.dataset.tab as Tab); };
  // the arrow keys between the tabs, Home and End to the first and last (a tab list's keys)
  root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[role="tablist"]')!.onkeydown = e => {
    const i = tabs.findIndex(b => b.dataset.tab === tab);
    const to = e.key === 'ArrowRight' ? (i + 1) % tabs.length : e.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? (i + tabs.length - 1) % tabs.length
      : e.key === 'Home' ? 0 : e.key === 'End' ? tabs.length - 1 : -1;
    if (to < 0) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    picked = true;
    sheet.show(tabs[to].dataset.tab as Tab, true);
  };
  const steer = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-steer]');
  if (steer) {
    const sel = steer.querySelector('select')!;
    sel.id = `${id}-steering`; steer.querySelector('label')!.htmlFor = sel.id;
    const help = steer.querySelector('.set-help')!; help.id = `${id}-steering-help`; sel.setAttribute('aria-describedby', help.id);
    const fill = () => {
      sel.replaceChildren(...STEERING.map(s => { const o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = s; o.textContent = steeringName(s); return o; }));
      sel.value = steering();
    };
    sel.onchange = () => {
      const to = sel.value as Steering;
      if (to === 'tilt') void askMotion();          // iOS asks from a choice of the player's
      setSteering(to);
    };
    onSteering(() => { sel.value = steering(); });
    onLanguage(fill);
    fill();
  }
  // the switches: Nitro on the steering's side, the level horizon
  const toggle = (set: HTMLElement | null, name: string, setting: SwitchSetting) => {
    if (!set) return;
    const sw = set.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('.switch')!, val = set.querySelector('.val')!;
    sw.id = `${id}-${name}`; set.querySelector('label')!.htmlFor = sw.id;
    const help = set.querySelector('.set-help')!; help.id = `${id}-${name}-help`; sw.setAttribute('aria-describedby', help.id);
    const show = () => { sw.checked = setting.get(); val.textContent = sw.checked ? t('On') : t('Off'); };
    sw.onchange = () => setting.set(sw.checked);
    setting.on(show);
    onLanguage(show);
    show();
  };
  toggle(root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-nitro]'), 'nitro', nitroSteerSide);
  toggle(root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-level]'), 'level', levelHorizon);
  // the touch controls' position's list and the sizes': the touch controls' and the game's menu buttons'
  const list = <T extends string | number>(set: HTMLElement | null, name: string, setting: ListSetting<T>) => {
    if (!set) return;
    const sel = set.querySelector('select')!;
    sel.id = `${id}-${name}`; set.querySelector('label')!.htmlFor = sel.id;
    const help = set.querySelector('.set-help')!; help.id = `${id}-${name}-help`; sel.setAttribute('aria-describedby', help.id);
    const fill = () => {
      sel.replaceChildren(...setting.values.map(v => { const o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = String(v); o.textContent = setting.name(v); return o; }));
      sel.value = String(setting.get());
    };
    sel.onchange = () => { const to = setting.values.find(v => String(v) === sel.value); if (to !== undefined) setting.set(to); };
    setting.on(fill);
    onLanguage(fill);
    fill();
  };
  list(root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-position]'), 'position', touchPosition);
  list(root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-size]'), 'size', touchSize);
  list(root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-menu-size]'), 'menu-size', menuSize);
  if (opts.follow) {
    const seen = (g: Gamepad) => {
      sheet.family(familyOf(g.id).family === PADF_PLAYSTATION ? 'ps' : 'xb');
      if (!picked) sheet.show('pad');
    };
    window.addEventListener('gamepadconnected', e => seen(e.gamepad));
    window.addEventListener(PAD_DRIVER_EVENT, () => { const g = drivingPad(); if (g) seen(g); });
    try { const g = allPads().find(p => p?.connected); if (g) seen(g); } catch { /* no Gamepad API */ }
  }
  sheet.show(tab);
  sheet.family(fam);
  return sheet;
}
