// The page's copy buttons (an invite link, the passphrase, a friend's Discord username): the text onto the clipboard
// (copyText), and a small toast right at the button that says so (copyToast), gone after a moment.
import { t } from './i18n';

/** how long a toast stays (ms); one the player has to read (a name the browser would not copy) longer */
export const TOAST_MS = 1600;
export const READ_MS = 4000;

/** Text onto the clipboard: the Clipboard API, else the old way (an older WebView, a page without the focus), in the
 *  dialog of button `at` when it is in one (the page under a modal dialog takes no selection).  False: neither did. */
export async function copyText(text: string, at?: Element): Promise<boolean> {
  try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text); return true; } catch { /* the old way, then */ }
  const ta = document.createElement('textarea'); ta.value = text; ta.setAttribute('readonly', ''); ta.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;opacity:0';
  const back = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
  (at?.closest('dialog') ?? document.body).append(ta); ta.select();
  let ok = false;
  try { ok = document.execCommand('copy'); } catch { /* none */ }
  ta.remove();
  back?.focus?.({ preventScroll: true });
  return ok;
}

/** the toast each button has now (one at a time a button: a second click puts a new one in its place) */
const shown = new WeakMap<Element, HTMLElement>();

/** A small toast at button `at`: over its middle (under it where there is no room above), inside the window, for
 *  `ms`.  In the top layer (a popover) where the browser has one, so a button in a modal dialog has it over the
 *  dialog; else in the button's dialog or the page. */
export function copyToast(at: HTMLElement, text = t('Copied'), ms = TOAST_MS) {
  shown.get(at)?.remove();
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.className = 'copy-toast';
  el.setAttribute('role', 'status');
  el.textContent = text;
  const layer = 'showPopover' in el;
  if (layer) el.popover = 'manual';
  (layer ? document.body : at.closest('dialog') ?? document.body).append(el);
  if (layer) el.showPopover();
  const b = at.getBoundingClientRect(), { width: w, height: h } = el.getBoundingClientRect(), gap = 8, edge = 8;
  const above = b.top - gap - h >= edge;
  el.style.left = `${Math.floor(Math.max(edge, Math.min(b.left + b.width / 2 - w / 2, innerWidth - w - edge)))}px`;
  el.style.top = `${Math.round(above ? b.top - gap - h : b.bottom + gap)}px`;
  el.classList.toggle('below', !above);
  shown.set(at, el);
  requestAnimationFrame(() => el.classList.add('on'));
  setTimeout(() => {
    el.classList.remove('on');
    setTimeout(() => { el.remove(); if (shown.get(at) === el) shown.delete(at); }, 200);
  }, ms);
}

// The Crews setting (settings.ini roam_crew, NFSU2_ROAM_CREW): the crews a player is in, by name, in the player's
// order and separated by commas ("Blue Room, Night Owls").  Crew-mates still see everyone in free roam, but each other
// in their crew's colour, at any distance.  A crew is its name's hash, as a Room is (players.ts roomHash: capitals A
// to Z and spaces do not count), so "Blue Room" and "blueroom" are the same crew.  Not private: anyone who types the
// same name is in it.  A name that reads as a slur (names.mjs, as for a player's name) is no crew: the box does not
// join it and a hand-written one is left out, as the game does (runtime/roam_game.c crews_parse).  Pure (no DOM), so
// the settings and their tests use it under node.
import { N } from './i18n';
import { blockedName } from './names.mjs';
import { roomHash } from './players';

/** most crews a player is in (roam_core.h RC_CREW_MAX), and the longest name, in characters (the texts say 4 and 24) */
export const CREW_MAX = 4;
export const CREW_LEN = 24;
/** a crew of more players than this in one room is not linked first by the server's hub (hub.rs CREW_GROUP_MAX): its
 *  players see each other only nearby, as everyone else, and the control says so by its count */
export const CREW_BIG = 64;
/** the colours a player picks a crew's from (its name over the car, its map arrow), rrggbb: no green or orange, the
 *  game's own arrow's and the opponents'.  The first 4 are the defaults by the crew's place in the list, and must
 *  match runtime/roam_game.c's CREW_RGB. */
export const CREW_PALETTE: readonly string[] = ['3cd2ff', 'ff50c8', 'a078ff', 'ff4646', '4f7dff', 'fff03c', '3cf0f0', 'ff9ad5'];
/** each palette colour's name (the picker's buttons say it) */
export const CREW_COLOUR_NAMES: readonly string[] = [N('Cyan'), N('Magenta'), N('Violet'), N('Red'), N('Blue'), N('Yellow'), N('Teal'), N('Light pink')];

/** a crew as the controls show it: its name, and its colour (rrggbb, lower case: the one set, else its place's) */
export interface Crew { name: string; rgb: string }

/** the blanks bundle.m's trim and the hash skip (ASCII only: a no-break space is a character of the name) */
const BLANKS = /[\t\n\v\f\r ]+/g;
const trimBlanks = (s: string) => s.replace(/^[\t\n\v\f\r ]+|[\t\n\v\f\r ]+$/g, '');
/** a name's length as the player counts it: characters, not bytes */
export const crewLength = (name: string) => [...trimBlanks(name)].length;

/** The crews a value names, as the game takes them: split at its commas and trimmed, the empty ones, repeats (the
 *  same hash as an earlier one) and the ones that read as a slur left out, the first 4. */
export function crewList(value: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [], seen = new Set<number>();
  for (const part of value.split(',')) {
    const name = trimBlanks(part).replace(BLANKS, ' '), h = roomHash(name);
    if (!h || seen.has(h) || blockedName(name)) continue;
    seen.add(h); out.push(name);
    if (out.length === CREW_MAX) break;
  }
  return out;
}

/** a list as settings.ini keeps it */
export const crewsValue = (list: readonly string[]) => list.join(', ');

/** What a typed name does to the list: ok, the name to join (trimmed); or why not, an English text for t() (null:
 *  nothing typed, nothing to say; name: the crew it repeats).  A comma would split it, and a # or ; after a blank
 *  would start a comment in settings.ini (the free-roam keys' "value ; comment"), so a name has none of them. */
export type CrewCheck = { ok: true; name: string } | { ok: false; why: string | null; name?: string };
export function checkCrew(typed: string, list: readonly string[]): CrewCheck {
  if (list.length >= CREW_MAX) return { ok: false, why: N('Up to 4 crews: leave one to join another.') };
  const name = trimBlanks(typed).replace(BLANKS, ' ');
  if (!roomHash(name)) return { ok: false, why: null };
  if (/[,;#\x00-\x1f\x7f]/.test(name)) return { ok: false, why: N('No commas, # or ; in a crew name.') };
  if (crewLength(name) > CREW_LEN) return { ok: false, why: N('At most 24 characters.') };
  if (blockedName(name)) return { ok: false, why: N('Not a crew name: it reads as a slur.') };
  const h = roomHash(name), same = list.find(c => roomHash(c) === h);
  if (same !== undefined) return { ok: false, why: N('Already in your crews: {name}.'), name: same };
  return { ok: true, name };
}

/** settings.ini's check of a whole value: every crew at most 24 characters (more than 4, or repeats, are fine: the
 *  game takes the first 4) */
export const crewsOk = (value: string) => value.split(',').every(c => crewLength(c) <= CREW_LEN);

// ---- the crews' colours (settings.ini roam_crew_colours, NFSU2_ROAM_CREW_RGB) ----
// One entry per crew, in the order of roam_crew as the game takes it (crewList), joined by ", ": 6 hex digits without
// a '#' (one after a blank would start a comment), or empty for the place's default (CREW_PALETTE[i]).

/** an entry as bundle.m's K_RGBS takes it: spaces and tabs, then none or 6 hex digits (any case), then spaces and tabs */
const RGB_ENTRY = /^[ \t]*([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})?[ \t]*$/;
/** settings.ini's check of the colours (bundle.m K_RGBS): at most 4 entries, each as RGB_ENTRY */
export function rgbsOk(value: string): boolean {
  const e = value.split(',');
  return e.length <= CREW_MAX && e.every(x => RGB_ENTRY.test(x));
}

/** The crews of the two settings: each name with its colour (entry i, else CREW_PALETTE[i]); a colours value the
 *  check refuses counts as none. */
export function crewsOf(crews: string, rgbs: string): Crew[] {
  const set = rgbsOk(rgbs) ? rgbs.split(',').map(x => (RGB_ENTRY.exec(x)?.[1] ?? '').toLowerCase()) : [];
  return crewList(crews).map((name, i) => ({ name, rgb: set[i] || CREW_PALETTE[i] }));
}

/** the colours as settings.ini keeps them.  Every crew's is written, its place's default too: a crew keeps the colour
 *  it was seen in when one before it is left and it moves up a place. */
export const rgbsValue = (list: readonly Crew[]) => list.map(c => c.rgb).join(', ');

/** a joining crew's colour: the first of the palette no crew has (the defaults first) */
export const freeColour = (list: readonly Crew[]) => CREW_PALETTE.find(p => !list.some(c => c.rgb === p)) ?? CREW_PALETTE[0];

/** the colours as the game's net mailbox takes them (crews_rgb: 0x00rrggbb each) */
export const rgbWords = (list: readonly Crew[]) => list.map(c => parseInt(c.rgb, 16) >>> 0);

// What kind of device the page runs on, for the defaults and the hints that
// differ on phones and touch screens.
//   phone:       the browser says it is a mobile one (Chrome's User-Agent
//                Client Hints; "Mobile" or "iPhone" in the user agent of the
//                others), or it asks for desktop websites (Safari's Request
//                Desktop Website, Chrome's Desktop site: Macintosh or Linux,
//                no "Mobile") on a touch screen whose short side is a phone's
//                (under 600 CSS px; an iPad mini's is 744).  Tablets are not
//                phones.

// The Controls sheet and the hints follow touch first (html[data-touch]).
import { allPads } from '../input/steampad';
import { DEVICE_RENDER, localStore } from './prefs';

export function isPhone(): boolean {
  const uad = (navigator as unknown as { userAgentData?: { mobile?: boolean } }).userAgentData;

/** a touch screen with a phone's short side (a phone whatever its browser says), from the screen in CSS px */
export function phoneScreen(touchPoints: number, w = screen.width, h = screen.height): boolean {

}

/** settings.ini keys whose default is another on this device: what applies when neither the file nor the page
 *  address sets them.  Phones: 75% resolution scale (a phone's screen has more pixels than its GPU fills at 60 fps),
 *  or 100% once the render check found room to spare on this one (rendercheck.ts), full screen (no browser bars

 *  controls' steering and the speedometer under Brake, the 4:3 one between the thumbs.  Players' cars shown in free
 *  roam: 16 on phones, 24 on tablets (an iPhone was stopped for memory as 22 friends' cars loaded at once at the new

export function deviceDefaults(): Record<string, string> {
  const kind = deviceKind();
  if (kind === 'phone') return { render: rememberedRender() === 'backing' ? 'backing' : 'scale:0.75', fullscreen: fullScreenFails() ? 'off' : 'on', hud: '43', roam_max_cars: '16', roam_map_max: '2048', coop: 'off', fsaa: 'off', anisotropic: 'off', hq_vinyls: 'off' };
  if (kind === 'tablet') return { roam_max_cars: '24', coop: 'off', anisotropic: 'off', hq_vinyls: 'off' };

/** the device as its defaults see it: a phone, a touch-first one that is not a phone (a tablet), or a computer */
export function deviceKind(): 'phone' | 'tablet' | 'pc' {
  return isPhone() ? 'phone' : touchFirst() ? 'tablet' : 'pc';

/** The guest heap's window (runtime/guest_span.h): the game's memory 2 GB from the start, 768 MB more of it for the
 *  game's own heap than its 512 MB, which a crowded free roam fills on its trips out and back (450-507 MB measured,
 *  2026-11-04).  On a computer only: a phone's or tablet's Chrome for Android is a 32-bit program on most such devices
 *  and sets aside 1 GB at most (host/memory.ts), and Safari keeps every buffer in one area that a few large memories
 *  use up (WebKit bug 269937).  Not where the browser says the device has less than 8 GB (Chrome and Edge say 8 at
 *  most; Firefox says nothing): the memory counts against the computer's commit limit on Windows. */
export function heapWindow(kind = deviceKind(), ua = navigator.userAgent,
                           memoryGB = (navigator as unknown as { deviceMemory?: number }).deviceMemory,
                           platform = (navigator as unknown as { userAgentData?: { platform?: string } }).userAgentData?.platform): boolean {
  const safari = /AppleWebKit\//.test(ua) && !/Chrome\/|Chromium\/|Firefox\//.test(ua);
  // (an Android tablet with a mouse, or a phone on a desktop screen (DeX), reads as a computer: its platform says Android)
  const android = platform === 'Android' || /Android/.test(ua);
  return kind === 'pc' && !safari && !android && (memoryGB === undefined || memoryGB >= 8);
}

/** the render check's verdict on this phone: in this browser only, like the other device defaults (settings.ini,

}

/** html[data-touch] while the primary pointer is a finger (the Controls sheet and the hints show what fits) */
export function markTouch() {
  const q = matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)');
  const set = () => document.documentElement.toggleAttribute('data-touch', q.matches);
  set();
  q.addEventListener('change', set);
}

/** no pinch zoom on an iPhone: Safari ignores the viewport's user-scalable=no, and cancelling its own gesture events
 *  is what stops a pinch there (style.css's touch-action stops the double tap) */
export function noPinchZoom() {
  for (const t of ['gesturestart', 'gesturechange']) document.addEventListener(t, e => e.preventDefault(), { passive: false });
}

// The browser and the device as the log names them (the session lines, shell.ts): enough to tell what ran and what it
// had to run on, nothing that tells who (the audit's PRIV-5: the browser's major version and the system, no more).

/** "Chrome 155 on Windows", "Safari 26 on iOS", "Safari 26 on iPadOS" (an iPad's Safari says Macintosh, but has touch),
 *  "Safari 26 on iOS (desktop website)" (an iPhone's Safari asked for desktop websites: Macintosh, touch, a phone's
 *  screen; phone: device.ts phoneScreen), "Chrome 156 on Android 11" (android: the major version, androidMajor) */
export function browserBrief(ua: string, touchPoints = 0, phone = false, android?: string): string {
  const mac = /Macintosh/.test(ua) && touchPoints > 1;
  const ios = /iPhone|iPod/.test(ua) ? 'iOS' : mac && phone ? 'iOS (desktop website)' : /iPad/.test(ua) || mac ? 'iPadOS' : null;
  const os = ios ?? (/CrOS/.test(ua) ? 'ChromeOS' : /Windows/.test(ua) ? 'Windows' : /Mac OS X|Macintosh/.test(ua) ? 'macOS'
    : /Android/.test(ua) ? 'Android' : /Linux/.test(ua) ? 'Linux' : 'another system');
  const v = (re: RegExp) => re.exec(ua)?.[1];
  const safari = v(/Version\/(\d+)[\d.]* (?:Mobile\/\S+ )?Safari\//);
  let name: string;
  // every browser on iOS and iPadOS is WebKit underneath: Chrome, Firefox and Edge there say CriOS, FxiOS and EdgiOS
  if (ios) name = v(/CriOS\/(\d+)/) ? `Chrome ${v(/CriOS\/(\d+)/)} (WebKit)` : v(/FxiOS\/(\d+)/) ? `Firefox ${v(/FxiOS\/(\d+)/)} (WebKit)`
    : v(/EdgiOS\/(\d+)/) ? `Edge ${v(/EdgiOS\/(\d+)/)} (WebKit)` : safari ? `Safari ${safari}` : 'another browser (WebKit)';
  else name = v(/Firefox\/(\d+)/) ? `Firefox ${v(/Firefox\/(\d+)/)}` : v(/(?:Chrome|Chromium)\/(\d+)/) ? `Chrome ${v(/(?:Chrome|Chromium)\/(\d+)/)}`
    : safari ? `Safari ${safari}` : 'another browser';
  return `${name} on ${os}${os === 'Android' && android && /^\d+$/.test(android) ? ` ${android}` : ''}`;
}

/** The Android version's major number, where the browser says it: Chrome's user agent says "Android 10" on every
 *  version since 110 (reduced), but its client hints give the real one.  Some Adreno phones' graphics drivers fail
 *  where others run (2026-10/11, game.ts GPU-ANDROID-DRIVER): the version tells the old ones apart.  The major
 *  number only (the audit's PRIV-5); undefined elsewhere, or when the browser does not answer within a second. */
export async function androidMajor(): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const d = (navigator as { userAgentData?: { platform?: string; getHighEntropyValues?(h: string[]): Promise<{ platformVersion?: string }> } }).userAgentData;
  if (d?.platform !== 'Android' || !d.getHighEntropyValues) return undefined;
  try {
    const v = await Promise.race([d.getHighEntropyValues(['platformVersion']), new Promise<undefined>(r => setTimeout(r, 1000))]);
    return /^(\d+)/.exec(v?.platformVersion ?? '')?.[1];
  } catch { return undefined; }
}

export interface DeviceFacts {
  /** the screen in CSS pixels and the device pixels to one */
  screenW: number; screenH: number; dpr: number;
  /** navigator.hardwareConcurrency, navigator.deviceMemory (Chrome only; Safari has none) */
  cores?: number; memoryGB?: number;
  touchPoints: number;
  /** started from the Home Screen (no browser bars), not in a browser tab */
  homeScreen: boolean;
  /** the refresh rate the page measured before Play */
  displayHz: number;
}

/** "screen 428x926 at 3x, 6 cores, touch, browser tab"; a 30 Hz display before Play is most likely Low Power Mode */
export function deviceBrief(d: DeviceFacts): string {
  const parts = [`screen ${d.screenW}x${d.screenH} at ${+d.dpr.toFixed(2)}x`];
  if (d.cores) parts.push(`${d.cores} cores`);
  if (d.memoryGB) parts.push(`${d.memoryGB} GB memory`);
  parts.push(d.touchPoints > 1 ? 'touch' : 'no touch', d.homeScreen ? 'Home Screen app' : 'browser tab');
  if (d.displayHz > 0 && d.displayHz <= 31) parts.push(`the display at ${d.displayHz} Hz before Play (Low Power Mode, or a window in the background)`);
  return parts.join(', ');
}

// The display side of the shell: the refresh rate (for NFSU2_DISPLAY_HZ, so
// "fps = auto" can follow a 120 Hz screen), the canvas kept at the
// device-pixel size of its box, and full screen with Keyboard Lock (so
// Escape, the game's Back/Pause, reaches the game; hold Escape to leave),
// and the screen kept on while a game runs.

const COMMON_HZ = [30, 48, 50, 60, 72, 75, 90, 100, 120, 144, 165, 180, 240, 360];

/** Median requestAnimationFrame rate over `frames` frames, snapped to a common refresh rate when close.  The median
 *  is of spans of 4 frames: Safari on an iPhone or iPad gives rAF times in whole milliseconds, and single intervals
 *  of 8 or 9 ms at 120 Hz had a median of 125 Hz (as the renderer's measurement, gpu/index.ts). */
export function measureRefresh(frames = 60): Promise<{ hz: number; raw: number }> {
  return new Promise(resolve => {
    const t: number[] = [];
    const step = (now: number) => {
      t.push(now);
      if (t.length <= frames) { requestAnimationFrame(step); return; }
      const d = t.slice(4).map((x, i) => (x - t[i]) / 4).sort((a, b) => a - b);
      const raw = 1000 / d[d.length >> 1];
      const snap = COMMON_HZ.reduce((a, b) => Math.abs(b - raw) < Math.abs(a - raw) ? b : a);
      resolve({ hz: Math.abs(snap - raw) / snap < 0.04 ? snap : Math.round(raw), raw });
    };
    requestAnimationFrame(step);
  });
}

/**
 * Keeps canvas.width/height at the device-pixel size of the canvas's CSS
 * box (devicePixelContentBoxSize: exact, no rounding drift at fractional
 * zoom).  The renderer reads canvas.width/height; a WebGPU context's
 * texture follows them by itself.
 */
export function trackCanvasSize(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, onChange?: (w: number, h: number) => void): () => void {
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(entries => {
    for (const e of entries) {
      const s = e.devicePixelContentBoxSize?.[0];
      const w = s ? s.inlineSize : Math.round(e.contentRect.width * devicePixelRatio);
      const h = s ? s.blockSize : Math.round(e.contentRect.height * devicePixelRatio);
      if (w > 0 && h > 0 && (canvas.width !== w || canvas.height !== h)) { canvas.width = w; canvas.height = h; onChange?.(w, h); }
    }
  });
  try { ro.observe(canvas, { box: 'device-pixel-content-box' }); } catch { ro.observe(canvas); }
  return () => ro.disconnect();
}

/** The next size the observer reports, or the current one after `ms`. */
export function settledSize(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, ms = 400): Promise<{ w: number; h: number }> {
  return new Promise(resolve => {
    let done = false;
    const finish = () => { if (!done) { done = true; ro.disconnect(); resolve({ w: canvas.width, h: canvas.height }); } };
    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(finish)));
    ro.observe(canvas);
    setTimeout(finish, ms);
  });
}

export function isFullscreen(): boolean { return !!document.fullscreenElement; }

/** whether this browser shows a page's element full screen (Safari on an iPhone does not: only its videos go full screen) */
export function canFullscreen(): boolean {
  return typeof document.documentElement.requestFullscreen === 'function' && document.fullscreenEnabled !== false;
}

/** the page started from the Home Screen (added there, or an installed web app): no browser bars around it */
export function fromHomeScreen(): boolean {
  return matchMedia('(display-mode: fullscreen), (display-mode: standalone)').matches || (navigator as { standalone?: boolean }).standalone === true;
}

/** an iPhone's browser: no full screen for the page, but the page added to the Home Screen opens without the browser's bars */
export function homeScreenInstead(): boolean {
  return /iPhone|iPod/.test(navigator.userAgent) && !canFullscreen() && !fromHomeScreen();

/** Full screen on `el` (needs a user gesture), then Keyboard Lock. */
export async function enterFullscreen(el: HTMLElement): Promise<{ ok: boolean; locked: boolean; error?: string }> {
  try {
    if (document.fullscreenElement !== el) await el.requestFullscreen({ navigationUI: 'hide' });
  } catch (e) { return { ok: false, locked: false, error: String(e) }; }
  return { ok: true, locked: await lockKeys() };
}

export async function lockKeys(): Promise<boolean> {
  const kb = (navigator as any).keyboard as { lock?: (codes?: string[]) => Promise<void> } | undefined;
  if (!kb?.lock || !document.fullscreenElement) return false;
  try { await kb.lock(); return true; } catch { return false; }
}

/**
 * The screen kept on while a game runs (Screen Wake Lock): the buttons of a controller do not keep every system's
 * screen awake, so a race with one could dim and lock the screen.  The browser lets the lock go while the page is
 * hidden; it is taken again when the page shows.  Returns the stop.
 */
export function keepScreenOn(log: (s: string) => void): () => void {
  const wl = (navigator as { wakeLock?: { request(t: 'screen'): Promise<WakeLockSentinel> } }).wakeLock;
  if (!wl) { log('[app] no Wake Lock in this browser: the screen may turn off while a controller plays'); return () => {}; }
  let lock: WakeLockSentinel | null = null, asking = false, stopped = false, said = false;
  const take = () => {
    if (stopped || asking || lock || document.hidden) return;
    asking = true;
    wl.request('screen').then(l => {
      if (stopped) { void l.release().catch(() => {}); return; }
      lock = l;
      l.addEventListener('release', () => { if (lock === l) lock = null; });
      if (!said) { said = true; log('[app] the screen stays on while the game runs (Wake Lock)'); }
    }, e => { if (!said) { said = true; log(`[app] Wake Lock refused: ${e}`); } })
      .finally(() => { asking = false; });
  };
  const onVisible = () => { if (!document.hidden) take(); };
  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisible);
  take();
  return () => {
    stopped = true;
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisible);
    void lock?.release().catch(() => {});
    lock = null;
  };
}

export function exitFullscreen() {
  try { (navigator as any).keyboard?.unlock?.(); } catch { /* not locked */ }
  if (document.fullscreenElement) void document.exitFullscreen().catch(() => {});
}

  private fillBoard(bs: { t: number; me: string; a: number; vs: string; b: number }) {

      if (st && st.has('drift')) {

        if (this.keys >= 0 && k !== this.keys) {
          this.deps.toast(d & 4 ? t('Drift mode only works in free roam') : d & 1 ? t('Drift mode: on') : t('Drift mode: off'), 2500);
          this.deps.log(`[app] drift mode: X ${d & 4 ? 'outside free roam' : d & 1 ? 'on' : 'off'}`);
        }
        this.keys = k;
        this.on = (d & 2) !== 0;
        const total = st.get('drift_total') ?? 0, pend = st.get('drift_pend') ?? 0, was = this.counting;
        const grew = this.banked >= 0 && total > this.banked;
        this.counting = this.on && st.get('drift_st') === 0 && pend > 0;
        if (this.counting) this.counter('live', pend);
        else if (this.on && grew) this.counter('banked', total - this.banked);
        else if (this.on && was) this.counter('lost', this.pend);   // over without banking: a wall took it
        this.pend = pend; this.banked = total;
        this.fill(st.get('drift_best') ?? 0, st.get('drift_x') ?? 1, st.get('drift_gain') ?? 0, total);
      }
    }
    this.show(this.on && !pageDialog());
    const board = this.shown && this.bs !== null;
    if (board !== this.boardShown) { this.boardShown = board; this.board.hidden = !board; }
    if (this.shown) this.place(s);
    else this.pop.hidden = true;
  }

  /** DRIFT and the points: live while the drift counts, then banked or lost, fading out (the animation's end hides it) */
  private counter(kind: 'live' | 'banked' | 'lost', points: number) {
    const q = this.pop, again = kind !== 'live' || !q.classList.contains('live') || q.hidden;
    q.firstElementChild!.textContent = t('DRIFT');
    q.lastElementChild!.textContent = String(Math.floor(points));
    if (!again) return;
    q.className = `drift-pop ${kind}`;
    q.hidden = true; void q.offsetWidth; q.hidden = !this.shown;    // a fade from its start
  }

  private show(on: boolean) {
    if (on === this.shown) return;
    this.shown = on;
    this.root.hidden = !on;
  }

  /** the numbers, and the labels in the page's language */
  private fill(best: number, x: number, gain: number, total: number) {
    const key = `${best} ${x} ${gain} ${total} ${t('Total')}`;
    if (key === this.filled) return;
    this.filled = key;
    this.best.previousElementSibling!.textContent = t('Best:');
    this.best.textContent = String(best);
    this.mult.textContent = `X${x}`;
    this.gain.hidden = x >= 5 || gain <= 0;
    this.gain.firstElementChild!.textContent = t('Gain {n}X with:', { n: x + 1 });
    this.gain.lastElementChild!.textContent = String(gain);
    this.total.firstElementChild!.textContent = t('Total');
    this.total.lastElementChild!.textContent = String(total);
  }

  /** under the game's Bank panel, its right edge on the Bank panel's */
  private place(s: GameSession) {
    const v = s.viewRect();
    if (!v.w || !v.h) return;
    const u = Math.min(v.w / 640, v.h / 480), e169 = 320 * (16 / 9 * 0.75 - 1);
    const out = this.deps.wide() ? Math.min(Math.max(320 * (v.w / v.h * 0.75 - 1), 0), e169) * 109 / e169 : 0;
    const st = this.root.style, ps = this.pop.style;
    st.left = `${v.x + v.w / 2 + (RIGHT_U + out - WIDE_U) * u}px`;
    st.top = `${v.y + v.h / 2 + TOP_U * u}px`;
    st.setProperty('--u', `${u}px`);
    ps.left = `${v.x + v.w / 2}px`;                                      // its middle (the style's translate)
    ps.top = `${v.y + v.h / 2 + POP_TOP_U * u}px`;
    ps.setProperty('--u', `${u}px`);
    if (this.boardShown) {                                               // the scoreboard: 4 under the panel, as wide
      const bs = this.board.style;
      bs.left = st.left;
      bs.top = `${v.y + v.h / 2 + TOP_U * u + this.root.offsetHeight + 4 * u}px`;
      bs.setProperty('--u', `${u}px`);
    }
  }

/** /flags.png (web/build.mjs, from runtime/flags.dat): every flag at 48x36 in FLAG_CODES' order, this many a row */
export const FLAG_SHEET_COLS = 16;
export const FLAG_W = 48, FLAG_H = 36;
/** where a flag is in /flags.png, in its pixels ([x, y] of its top left), or null for none */
export function flagAt(code: string): [number, number] | null {
  const i = FLAG_CODES.indexOf(code as FlagCode);
  return i < 0 ? null : [(i % FLAG_SHEET_COLS) * FLAG_W, Math.floor(i / FLAG_SHEET_COLS) * FLAG_H];
}

/** a setting's text as a flag's code (any case, spaces round it), '' for none or anything else */
export function flagCode(v: string): FlagCode | '' {
  const c = v.trim().toLowerCase();
  return CODES.has(c) ? c as FlagCode : '';
}

/** the nations of the United Kingdom and Quebec, which have no region name of their own in the browser */
const NATIONS: Record<string, string> = {
  'gb-eng': N('England'), 'gb-sct': N('Scotland'), 'gb-wls': N('Wales'), 'gb-nir': N('Northern Ireland'),
  'ca-qc': N('Quebec'),
};
let names: Intl.DisplayNames | null = null, namesFor = '';
/** the flag's name in the page's language */
export function flagName(code: FlagCode): string {
  if (code in NATIONS) return t(NATIONS[code]);
  const loc = LOCALE[language()];
  if (namesFor !== loc) {
    namesFor = loc;
    try { names = new Intl.DisplayNames([loc, 'en'], { type: 'region' }); } catch { names = null; }
  }
  try { return names?.of(code.toUpperCase()) ?? code.toUpperCase(); } catch { return code.toUpperCase(); }
}

/** every flag by its name in the page's language */
export function flagsByName(): { code: FlagCode; name: string }[] {
  const loc = LOCALE[language()];
  return FLAG_CODES.map(code => ({ code, name: flagName(code) })).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name, loc));
}

/** two names of one player: the same Online form, in any case (the name over a car, a claimed name) */
function sameName(a: string, b: string): boolean {
  return (onlineName(a) ?? a).toLowerCase() === (onlineName(b) ?? b).toLowerCase();
}

/** a friend as the start page shows it: where it plays ('roam' free roam, 'online' the Online lobby, '' neither),
 *  its room's name in free roam ('' the room of everyone; none: its page did not say), its room's hash there (its
 *  world's, or a race track's spot's: tracks.ts friendSpot; none from a server of before), and its line for its
 *  friends */
export interface Friend { name: string; where: 'roam' | 'online' | ''; room?: string; at?: number; contact?: string }
/** the lists: the player's claimed name (null: none, so no friends), its friends, the requests that wait for its
 *  answer and its own that wait, the friends' messages that waited for it (gone from the server now); `done` what the
 *  last change did (friends.rs) */
export interface FriendLists {
  me: string | null; friends: Friend[]; asks: string[]; sent: string[]; mail: { from: string; body: string; t: number }[]; done?: string;
  /** the player's own Discord username (null: none) */
  contact?: string | null;
}

/** A Discord username as Discord allows one (2 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, _ and ., never two . together), from what the
 *  player typed: the spaces around it, a leading @ and capitals let go (as the server's buddy.rs discord_name).
 *  null: not one. */
export function discordName(typed: string): string | null {
  let s = typed.trim();
  if (s.startsWith('@')) s = s.slice(1);
  s = s.replace(/[A-Z]/g, c => c.toLowerCase());
  return /^[a-z0-9_.]{2,32}$/.test(s) && !s.includes('..') ? s : null;
}

/** the friends of an answer of the server's (GET /friends, "where"), read leniently: a world's name only when its room's
 *  hash leads to the friend (tracks.ts friendRoom) */
function friendsOf(v: unknown): Friend[] {
  return Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((f: any) => typeof f?.name === 'string').map((f: any) => {
    const at: number | undefined = Number.isInteger(f.at) && f.at >= 0 && f.at <= 0xffffffff ? f.at : undefined;
    const room = friendRoom(typeof f.room === 'string' ? f.room : undefined, at);
    return {
      name: f.name, where: f.where === 'roam' || f.where === 'online' ? f.where : '',
      ...(room !== undefined ? { room } : {}), ...(at !== undefined ? { at } : {}),
      ...(typeof f.contact === 'string' ? { contact: f.contact } : {}),
    };
  }) : [];
}

/** /friends on this server: null when the page has no keyphrase or the server none (404) */
export class FriendsApi {
  constructor(private token: () => Promise<string | null>) {}

  private async ask(init?: RequestInit): Promise<FriendLists | null> {
    const tk = await this.token().catch(() => null);
    if (!tk) return null;
    const r = await fetch('/friends', { ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: `Bearer ${tk}` }, cache: 'no-store' });
    if (!r.ok) return null;
    const j = await r.json();
    const names = (v: unknown) => Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string') : [];
    return {
      me: typeof j.me === 'string' ? j.me : null, friends: friendsOf(j.friends), asks: names(j.asks), sent: names(j.sent), mail: mailOf(j.mail),
      done: typeof j.done === 'string' ? j.done : undefined, contact: typeof j.contact === 'string' ? j.contact : null,
    };
  }

  list(): Promise<FriendLists | null> { return this.ask(); }
  act(op: 'accept' | 'decline' | 'remove' | 'block' | 'ask', name: string): Promise<FriendLists | null> {
    return this.ask({ method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ op, name }) });
  }
  /** the player's Discord username from now on ('' none): the lists after it, `done` "ok", "name" (refused), "rate" */
  discord(name: string): Promise<FriendLists | null> {
    return this.ask({ method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ op: 'discord', name }) });
  }
  /** a message to friend `name` (messages.ts): the lists after it, `done` what became of it */
  send(name: string, body: string): Promise<FriendLists | null> {
    return this.ask({ method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ op: 'msg', name, body }) });
  }
  /** an invite to friend `name` (in free roam) to the player's crew `crew`, in room `room` ('' the room of everyone):
   *  the lists after it, `done` "sent", "away" (not in free roam now), "rate", ... (friends.rs crew_invite) */
  crew(name: string, crew: string, room: string): Promise<FriendLists | null> {
    return this.ask({ method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ op: 'crew', name, crew, room }) });
  }
}

/** the room f plays in is `mine` (the game's room: '' none), in free roam */
function inRoom(f: Friend, mine: string): boolean {
  return f.where === 'roam' && f.room !== undefined && roomHash(f.room) === roomHash(mine);
}

/** where a friend plays, after its name: free roam (and its world, but the main world; `mine`: the game's own room, in
 *  the game: your world; and the race track it is at, if one), the Online lobby, offline */
export function whereText(f: Friend, mine?: string): string {
  if (f.where === 'roam') {
    const w = mine !== undefined && inRoom(f, mine) ? t('free roam · your world')
      : f.room ? t('free roam · {world}', { world: worldName(f.room) }) : t('free roam');
    const spot = atName(friendSpot(f.room, f.at));
    return spot ? `${w} · ${spot}` : w;
  }
  return f.where === 'online' ? t('Online lobby') : t('offline');
}

/** whether friend f drives where the player does (`mine` its room, `spot` the race track it is at, 0 the city): the
 *  same room on the server's hub, so a race invite reaches it (without the friend's hash, a server of before: its
 *  world) */
function atSpot(f: Friend, mine: string, spot: number): boolean {
  if (!inRoom(f, mine)) return false;
  if (f.at === undefined) return true;
  const base = roomHash(mine);
  return f.at === (spot >= 1 && spot <= TRACKS.length ? trackRoom(base, TRACKS[spot - 1].key) : base);
}

/** where a friend in free roam plays, in the page menu's Friends (all of them in free roam there): your world (`mine`,
 *  the game's room), its world (worlds.ts), or free roam (its page did not say); and the race track it is at, if one */
function roomText(f: Friend, mine: string): string {
  const w = inRoom(f, mine) ? t('your world') : f.room !== undefined ? worldName(f.room) : t('free roam');
  const spot = atName(friendSpot(f.room, f.at));
  return spot ? `${w} · ${spot}` : w;
}

/** a line of a friends list: the name, where it plays (or the request's state) after it in small text, lime while it

function icon(cls: string, name: string, path: string, f: () => void): HTMLButtonElement {

function friendList(lines: Line[]): HTMLUListElement {
