/** t(en, v) as a Msg */
export const T = (en: string, v?: Vars): Msg => () => t(en, v);

/** the locales for dates and times: in English the browser's own, as before; else the page's language */
export const dateLocale = (): string[] | string => current === 'english' ? [] : LOCALE[current];
/** "a, b and c" in the page's language */
export function listOf(items: string[]): string {
  if (items.length < 2) return items[0] ?? '';
  return new Intl.ListFormat(current === 'english' ? 'en-GB' : LOCALE[current], { type: 'conjunction' }).format(items);
}

/** x as a percentage in the page's language (1.25: 125 %) */
export function percent(x: number): string {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(current === 'english' ? 'en-GB' : LOCALE[current], { style: 'percent' }).format(x);
}

/** a whole number in the page's language, its thousands grouped (7592: 7,592; 7.592 in German) */
export function count(n: number): string {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(current === 'english' ? 'en-GB' : LOCALE[current]).format(n);
}

/** f again whenever the page's language changes */
export function onLanguage(f: () => void) { listeners.push(f); }

/** elements whose text live() keeps in the page's language */
const lives = new Map<Element, { f: Msg; code?: string }>();
/** el's text from f, now and again whenever the language changes, until live() gives it another; code: a problem's
 *  fixed name after it (the same in every language) */
export function live(el: Element, f: Msg, code?: string) {
  lives.set(el, { f, code });
  draw(el, f, code);
}
function draw(el: Element, f: Msg, code?: string) {
  el.textContent = f();
  if (code) el.append(codeOf(code));
}
/** a problem's code as the page shows it (beside its text, in any language), after a line break opportunity: the text
 *  ends with no space before it, so without one its last word and the code were one piece, wider than a phone's box
 *  where both are long (Spanish "comprobaciones." and BROWSER-CHROMIUM at 320 px); now the code takes the next line */
export function codeOf(code: string): DocumentFragment {
  const c = document.createElement('code');
  c.className = 'err-code'; c.textContent = code;
  const f = document.createDocumentFragment();
  f.append(document.createElement('wbr'), c);
  return f;
}

/**
 * The page in language l: its file fetched (English has none), then the markup, the live texts and every onLanguage
 * listener.  False: the file did not load (the page stays as it was; the log says why).
 */
export async function setLanguage(l: string, log?: (s: string) => void): Promise<boolean> {
  const want: Language = isLanguage(l) ? l : 'english';
  asked = want;
  if (want === current) return true;
  let next: Record<string, string | Forms> = {};
  if (want !== 'english') {
    try {
      const r = await fetch(`/lang/${want}.json`);
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`);
      next = await r.json() as Record<string, string | Forms>;
    } catch (e) {
      log?.(`[app] the page's ${want} texts did not load (${e}): it stays ${current}`);
      return false;
    }
  }
  if (asked !== want) return false;            // a newer pick came first
  current = want; dict = next; plural = null;
  localStore.set(PAGE_LANGUAGE, want);         // (not kept: the next start shows English until settings.ini is read)
  if (typeof document !== 'undefined') {
    document.documentElement.lang = LOCALE[want];
    translatePage(document);
    for (const [el, x] of lives) { if (el.isConnected) draw(el, x.f, x.code); else lives.delete(el); }
  }
  for (const f of listeners) { try { f(); } catch (e) { log?.(`[app] the page in ${want}: a part was not drawn again (${e})`); } }
  log?.(`[app] the page is in ${want} now`);
  return true;
}

/** the language this browser showed last (the page asks for its file at once, before settings.ini is read) */
export function lastLanguage(): Language {
  const v = localStore.get(PAGE_LANGUAGE) ?? '';
  return isLanguage(v) ? v : 'english';
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ the markup --

const norm = (s: string) => s.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;');
const unesc = (s: string) => s.replace(/&lt;/g, '<').replace(/&gt;/g, '>').replace(/&amp;/g, '&');

/** A data-i18n-html element's English: its text, each element in it <k>…</k> in the order they open (and numbered
 *  with data-i18n-n, so a copy of the markup finds them as well).  web/test/i18n.test.mjs makes the same of index.html. */
function htmlKey(el: Element): string {
  let k = 0;
  const walk = (n: Node): string => {
    let s = '';
    for (const c of n.childNodes) {
      if (c.nodeType === 3) s += esc(c.textContent ?? '');
      else if (c instanceof Element) { const i = k++; c.setAttribute('data-i18n-n', String(i)); s += `<${i}>${walk(c)}</${i}>`; }
    }
    return s;
  };
  return norm(walk(el));
}

/** The element's content from text, a translation of its key: the text between the tags, and its own elements
 *  (the same nodes, so what listens on them stays) where the tags put them.  A tag it does not have is left out. */
function build(el: Element, text: string) {
  const nodes = new Map<number, Element>();
  for (const e of el.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n-n]')) if (e.parentElement?.closest('[data-i18n-html]') === el) nodes.set(+e.getAttribute('data-i18n-n')!, e);
  const stack: Element[] = [el];
  el.replaceChildren();
  for (const part of text.split(/(<\/?\d+>)/)) {
    const m = /^<(\/?)(\d+)>$/.exec(part);
    if (!m) { if (part) stack[stack.length - 1].append(unesc(part)); continue; }
    const e = nodes.get(+m[2]);
    if (!e) continue;
    if (m[1]) { if (stack.length > 1 && stack[stack.length - 1] === e) stack.pop(); continue; }
    e.replaceChildren();
    stack[stack.length - 1].append(e);
    stack.push(e);
  }
}

/** The marked markup in root in the page's language (the English kept on each element the first time). */
export function translatePage(root: ParentNode) {
  for (const el of root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-i18n]')) {
    const src = el.getAttribute('data-i18n-src') ?? norm(el.textContent ?? '');
    el.setAttribute('data-i18n-src', src);
    el.textContent = t(src);
  }
  for (const el of root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-i18n-html]')) {
    const src = el.getAttribute('data-i18n-src') ?? htmlKey(el);
    el.setAttribute('data-i18n-src', src);
    build(el, t(src));
  }
  for (const el of root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-i18n-attr]')) {
    for (const a of el.getAttribute('data-i18n-attr')!.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)) {
      const src = el.getAttribute(`data-i18n-${a}`) ?? el.getAttribute(a) ?? '';
      el.setAttribute(`data-i18n-${a}`, src);
      el.setAttribute(a, t(src));
    }
  }
}

// One game per browser profile and server: the saves live in this origin's
// storage, and two tabs writing the same profile or registry would corrupt
// it.  A Web Lock held for the life of the tab says who owns the saves; a
// second tab waits for it and takes over when the first one closes.

const LOCK = 'nfsu2-saves';

export interface Instance {
  /** true once this tab holds the lock */
  readonly owner: boolean;
  /** resolves when this tab holds the lock (immediately if it already does) */
  whenOwner: Promise<void>;
}

export function claimInstance(name = LOCK): Instance {
  let owner = false;
  let gotIt!: () => void;
  const whenOwner = new Promise<void>(r => (gotIt = r));
  const hold = () => new Promise<void>(() => { /* released with the tab */ });
  const inst = { get owner() { return owner; }, whenOwner };
  if (!navigator.locks) { owner = true; gotIt(); return inst; }   // no Web Locks: nothing to coordinate
  void navigator.locks.request(name, { ifAvailable: true }, lock => {
    if (lock) { owner = true; gotIt(); return hold(); }
    // someone else has it: queue for it
    void navigator.locks.request(name, () => { owner = true; gotIt(); return hold(); });
    return undefined;
  });
  return inst;
}

{"id": "AT001739", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/src/app/invite.ts", "originalBytes": 5845, "originalSha256": "74d24fd0bc8bd11df292e8332bdee2018b27fa9ebc46a9bd06d1248a99210975", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 5845, "utf8TotalBytes": 5845}

// Invite links (a player's request: "why can't we just invite them to rooms using links?"): this server's start page
// with a free-roam room or crew after its '#', nfsu2.xyz/#room=Blue%20Room or nfsu2.xyz/#crew=Night%20Owls (with the
// sender's room after it when the sender is in one: crew-mates meet only within one room; a room's link never has a
// crew).  The page that opens one
// asks the player whether to join (shell.ts); nothing changes before Join, so a link cannot change a player's game by
// itself (the audit's PAGE-1).  The names stay in the address's fragment, which a browser never sends: the server and
// its logs never see them.  Pure (no DOM), so its test runs under node.
import { N, type Vars } from './i18n';
import { checkCrew } from './crews';
import { checkSetting } from './settings';
import { roomHash, roomText } from './players';

/** what a link joins: a room, a crew, or a crew in a room ('' with a crew: in no room, everyone's, from the menu's
 *  Friends; a link has no empty room) */
export interface Invite { room?: string; crew?: string }

/** Unicode's blanks (each one a blank to roomFold), and the invisible characters it leaves out too */
const BLANK = '\\s\\u00a0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000';
const HIDDEN = '\\u00ad\\u200b-\\u200d\\u2060\\ufeff';
const BLANKS = new RegExp(`[${BLANK}]+`, 'gu'), INVISIBLE = new RegExp(`[${HIDDEN}]`, 'gu'), UNSEEN = new RegExp(`[${BLANK}${HIDDEN}]`, 'u');
/** a typed or linked name as the settings keep it: composed (NFC), its blanks single spaces, the invisible characters
 *  out, trimmed */
export const tidyName = (s: string) => roomText(s).replace(INVISIBLE, '').replace(BLANKS, ' ').trim();

/** A typed Room: ok, the name to keep; or why not, an English text for t() with its names in v (null: nothing typed).
 *  settings.ini reads a # or ; after a blank as a comment (the free-roam keys' "value ; comment"), which would cut the
 *  name short there, so a name has none; else the setting's own check (at most 63 bytes, nothing that reads as a slur). */
export type RoomCheck = { ok: true; name: string } | { ok: false; why: string | null; v?: Vars };
export function checkRoom(typed: string): RoomCheck {
  const name = tidyName(typed);
  if (!roomHash(name)) return { ok: false, why: null };
  if (/(^|[ \t])[#;]/.test(name)) return { ok: false, why: N('no # or ; after a space in a world name') };
  const c = checkSetting('roam_room', name);
  if (c && !c.ok) return { ok: false, why: c.why, v: c.v };
  return { ok: true, name };
}

/** a name in a link: letters, digits, - _ ~ and the visible characters past ASCII as they are (a chat shows them so),
 *  every other as %XX of its UTF-8: blanks, the URL's own signs, and the . , ) ! that a chat would cut off a link's end */
function enc(s: string): string {
  let out = '';
  for (const ch of s) {
    const c = ch.codePointAt(0)!;
    if (/[A-Za-z0-9_~-]/.test(ch) || (c >= 0xa0 && !(c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdfff) && !UNSEEN.test(ch))) { out += ch; continue; }
    let e: string;
    try { e = encodeURIComponent(ch); } catch { e = '%EF%BF%BD'; }           // (half a surrogate pair: U+FFFD, as UTF-8 has it)
    out += e.replace(/[!'()*.]/g, c => `%${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase()}`);
  }
  return out;
}

/** The link to this server (origin: 'https://nfsu2.xyz') that joins inv: the crew first, then the room when there
 *  is one (a crew's from a sender in no room: the crew alone, its friend's own room left as it is). */
export function inviteLink(origin: string, inv: Invite): string {
  const p: string[] = [];
  if (inv.crew) p.push(`crew=${enc(inv.crew)}`);
  if (inv.room) p.push(`room=${enc(inv.room)}`);
  return `${origin}/#${p.join('&')}`;
}

/** The invite in a page address's fragment ('#room=...'), its names tidied; null: none (another fragment, a name
 *  that does not decode, or a room of blanks alone).  An empty room is no room (a crew's link of before,
 *  '#crew=X&room=': the crew alone). */
export function readInvite(hash: string): Invite | null {
  const inv: Invite = {};
  for (const part of hash.replace(/^#/, '').split('&')) {
    const eq = part.indexOf('='), key = eq < 0 ? part : part.slice(0, eq);
    if (eq < 0 || (key !== 'room' && key !== 'crew')) continue;
    let v: string;
    try { v = decodeURIComponent(part.slice(eq + 1).replace(/\+/g, ' ')); } catch { return null; }
    inv[key] = tidyName(v);
  }
  if (!inv.crew) delete inv.crew;
  if (!inv.room) delete inv.room;
  return inv.room || inv.crew ? inv : null;
}

/** Whether a link's names can be joined: each as the Room row and the Crews box check a typed one.  why: an English
 *  text for t(), with the name it is about as {name} and the check's own names. */
export type InviteCheck = { ok: true } | { ok: false; why: string; v: Vars };
export function checkInvite(inv: Invite): InviteCheck {
  if (inv.room) {
    const r = checkRoom(inv.room);
    if (!r.ok && r.why) return { ok: false, why: r.why, v: { name: inv.room, ...r.v } };
  }
  if (inv.crew) {
    const c = checkCrew(inv.crew, []);
    if (!c.ok && c.why) return { ok: false, why: c.why, v: { name: inv.crew } };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}

/** inv with its names as a link's are read (tidyName): what every Join checks and keeps, whoever sent the names (a
 *  friend's room comes from the friend's own page, a line break and all; the 2026-11-05 security audit) */
export function tidyInvite(inv: Invite): Invite {
  const out: Invite = {};
  if (inv.room !== undefined) out.room = tidyName(inv.room);
  if (inv.crew !== undefined) out.crew = tidyName(inv.crew);
  return out;
}

/** whether two names are one room or one crew (the hash's rules: capitals, blanks and invisible characters do not count) */
export const sameName = (a: string, b: string) => roomHash(a) === roomHash(b);
